doc.queryBuilder_desc: Visual builder for constructing complex search queries.
doc.querybuilder_logic_desc: In QueryBuilder, AND/OR are selected via SegmentedControl (toggle), while NOT is controlled by an independent Switch. This is due to the following reasons:
doc.querybuilder_logic_andor_desc: They determine how rules within a group are joined. Since they are mutually exclusive, they are provided as a selection.
doc.querybuilder_logic_not_desc: An operator that inverts the entire joined result. Since it can be applied to either AND or OR states, it is an independent switch.
doc.querybuilder_token_destructive: Border and background highlight color for excluded groups.
doc.querybuilder_token_border: Border color for groups and rules.
doc.querybuilder_token_bg_secondary: Background color for groups (auto-switches in dark mode).
doc.querybuilder_token_bg_component: Background color for individual rule rows.
doc.querybuilder_token_radius: Corner radius for groups and rules (8px).
doc.querybuilder_token_transition: Animation for border color change on hover.
doc.querybuilder_design_intent: QueryBuilder enables end-users to construct complex, nested logical queries without writing code. Use it when search criteria are dynamic and user-defined rather than fixed.
doc.querybuilder_choice_matrix_desc: Choose the right component based on the complexity of your search requirements:
doc.querybuilder_choice_self_when: When users need to build arbitrary nested conditions with AND/OR/NOT logic across multiple field types.
doc.querybuilder_choice_filterbar_when: When filtering criteria are limited to a fixed set of predefined fields.
doc.querybuilder_anatomy_root: The top-level rule group. Always present and cannot be deleted. Contains the combinator toggle and the rules list.
doc.querybuilder_anatomy_group: A sub-group nestable up to maxDepth levels. Supports its own AND/OR/NOT combinator.
doc.querybuilder_anatomy_rule: A single condition consisting of a Field selector, an Operator selector, and a Value input.
doc.querybuilder_anatomy_combinator: SegmentedControl (AND / OR) that determines how rules within the group are joined.
doc.querybuilder_anatomy_not: Switch that inverts the entire group result. When active, the group is visually highlighted as excluded.
doc.querybuilder_content_guideline_1: Use concise, user-recognizable field labels. Avoid exposing raw technical identifiers as field names.
doc.querybuilder_content_guideline_2: Limit maxDepth to 3 or fewer to prevent queries so complex they confuse users.
doc.querybuilder_motion_desc: Group add/remove uses a subtle fade transition via --transition-fast. Hovering over group borders animates the border-color.
doc.querybuilder_a11y_desc: The root element carries role="region" with aria-label. Each rule row has role="group". Field, Operator, and Value inputs carry individual aria-labels. Add and remove actions are announced via an aria-live="polite" live region.
doc.querybuilder_scenario_1: Admin dashboard search: Build multi-condition filters against a user table (e.g., age > 18 AND city = Tokyo).
doc.querybuilder_scenario_2: Report generator: Let users define export conditions across multiple fields before generating a report.
doc.querybuilder_best_practice_1: Always provide a defaultQuery so the component does not start in an empty state that may confuse first-time users.
doc.querybuilder_best_practice_2: Validate the generated QueryGroup on the server; never rely solely on the client-side query structure.
doc.querybuilder_responsive_desc: Rule rows wrap vertically on narrow containers. Add Rule and Add Group buttons remain accessible on mobile layouts.
doc.querybuilder_keyboard_desc: Tab moves focus through Field, Operator, Value, Add Rule, Add Group, and Remove buttons in DOM order. Within the SegmentedControl (AND/OR), arrow keys switch the combinator. The NOT Switch is toggled with Space.
doc.querybuilder_i18n_desc: Field labels are resolved through i18n keys passed in the fields array. Operator labels, combinator labels (AND/OR/NOT), and button labels use the components namespace.
doc.nodeGraph_desc: Visualizes complex networks and relationships between nodes.
doc.scheduleView_desc: Displays tasks or events on a chronological timeline or calendar view.
doc.promptInput_desc: Interactive input optimized for AI prompt engineering with multi-line support and action triggers.
doc.streamingText_desc: Renders text with a typewriter-like animation, ideal for AI chat responses.
doc.smartSearchInput_desc: Smart search input enabling both traditional search and AI prompting.
doc.thoughtProcess_desc: Visualizes AI reasoning steps and execution states in a timeline format.
doc.aiResponseFeedback_desc: Thumbs-up/down feedback controls and regenerate button for AI responses.
doc.sourceCitation_desc: Displays cited sources with title, domain, and external link for AI-generated content.
doc.codeBlock_desc: Syntax-highlighted code block with copy button, line numbers, and collapsible overflow.
doc.passwordStrength_desc: Visual meter to indicate password security level.
doc.imageCropper_desc: Front-end image cropping and rotation tool.
doc.tagInput_desc: Input field for creating free-form tags.
doc.codeDiffViewer_desc: Displays code changes as a side-by-side or unified diff, with line-level highlighting and Apply/Reject actions.
doc.terminal_desc: Renders terminal-style output with ANSI color support, prompt prefixes, and copy/clear controls.
doc.jsonDiffViewer_desc: Compares two JSON values as a formatted side-by-side or unified diff, built on top of CodeDiffViewer.
doc.reaction_desc: Display emoji reaction buttons with toggleable state and counts
doc.keyboardShortcuts_desc: Display a structured list of keyboard shortcuts
doc.autosave_desc: Inline status indicator for automatic save state
doc.leaderboard_desc: Display a ranked list of entries with scores and medal highlights for the top three positions.
doc.gallery_desc: Displays a responsive image grid with configurable columns, aspect ratios, multi-select, and an optional lightbox.
doc.dashboard_desc: Arranges widgets in a configurable grid with an edit mode for adding, removing, and resizing them.
doc.field_character_count_desc: Standardizes the display of character counts and limit indicators across text-based form inputs.
doc.relativeTime_desc: Display a timestamp as a localized relative phrase ("3 minutes ago", "yesterday") that updates automatically as time passes.
doc.countdown_desc: Display the remaining time until a target moment as a live ticking timer, for sale deadlines, OTP resend waits, and maintenance notices.
doc.spoiler_desc: Collapse long text such as reviews and comments to a fixed number of lines, with an accessible "show more" toggle that appears only when the text overflows.
doc.toolbar_desc: Action strip for IconButton, ToggleGroup, and related controls with toolbar keyboard navigation.
doc.menubar_desc: Desktop-style application menu bar with floating File / Edit / View submenus.

annotation.outside_field: Notes should be outside the field, not as placeholders.

btn.page_transition: When transitioning pages but needing visual emphasis as a button (semantics is `<a>`).

chat.placeholder_interactive: What time is the meeting tomorrow?

critical.info_only_in_p_desc: Providing critical info only through placeholders.

dashboard.desc: Dashboard for managing WIM UI component development status.
dashboard.title: Component Development Dashboard

datacontainer.accordion_desc: Saves space while disclosing details progressively.
datacontainer.box_desc: Groups image, title, description, and button together.
datacontainer.faqsection_desc: Organized list of questions and answers using accordions.
datacontainer.guide_desc: Groups information and provides layout cohesion.

dataindicator.guide_desc: Visually presents summary info like status, attributes, or user info.
dataindicator.relativetime_label: Freshness of a point in time
dataindicator.relativetime_usage: "3 minutes ago" in feeds, chats, tables.

ex-large.paragraph: Extra Large paragraph, Extra Large paragraph, Extra Large paragraph, Extra Large paragraph, Extra Large paragraph, Extra Large paragraph, Extra Large paragraph, Extra Large paragraph, Extra Large paragraph, Extra Large paragraph

ex-small.paragraph: Extra Small paragraph, Extra Small paragraph, Extra Small paragraph, Extra Small paragraph, Extra Small paragraph, Extra Small paragraph, Extra Small paragraph, Extra Small paragraph, Extra Small paragraph, Extra Small paragraph

large.paragraph: Large paragraph,Large paragraph, Large paragraph, Large paragraph, Large paragraph, Large paragraph, Large paragraph, Large paragraph, Large paragraph, Large paragraph

linkvsbutton.btn_examples: Submitting forms, opening modals, changing states, executing calculations.
linkvsbutton.link_examples: Navigating to other pages, anchor links, external sites.

medium.paragraph: Medium paragraph, Medium paragraph, Medium paragraph, Medium paragraph, Medium paragraph, Medium paragraph, Medium paragraph, Medium paragraph, Medium paragraph, Medium paragraph

rule.overload_dont_desc: Cramming rules like "8+ chars, including symbols"
rule.same_tier_desc: Dependencies within the same tier are allowed as long as they don't become bloated.
rule.transparent_props_desc: Wrapping components should spread internal component props as much as possible to ensure flexibility.
rule.unidirectional_desc: Lower tiers must not depend on upper tiers (e.g., Button (Tier 2) is prohibited from importing Select (Tier 4)).

small.paragraph: Small paragraph, Small paragraph, Small paragraph, Small paragraph, Small paragraph, Small paragraph, Small paragraph, Small paragraph, Small paragraph, Small paragraph

smart.search_placeholder: What types of buttons are in WIM UI?

tier1.desc: Smallest building blocks that rarely depend on other components.
tier1.role: Provides basic styling, layout, and low-level behavior.

tier2.desc: Independent components with a single function.
tier2.role: Provides unified UI parts for the entire design system.

tier3.desc: Components that combine multiple Tier 1/2 elements to achieve specific UI patterns or functions.
tier3.role: Provides the foundation for complex interactions and state management.

tier4.desc: Components that wrap multiple components to complete specific sections or complex features of the application.
tier4.role: Provides complete UI units and domain-specific features.

typo.code_desc: Uses monospace font to clearly indicate inline code snippets.
typo.contrast_desc: Maintain sufficient contrast (WCAG AA or better) against background. Check via `ContrastChecker`.
typo.filled_usage: Selected states, critical alerts, dark mode visibility.
typo.guide_desc: Guidelines for maximizing readability and accessibility by clarifying info hierarchy.
typo.icon_alt_desc: Convey info to screen readers via `aria-label` etc., when icons have meaning (e.g., as buttons).
typo.icon_aria_desc: Assists text or provides standalone action clues. Use `aria-label` for standalone use.
typo.icon_role_desc: Icons assist text or indicate standalone actions.
typo.inline_desc: Emphasizes parts of text or applies specific styles.
typo.kbd_desc: Uses monospace font to clearly indicate keyboard operations or shortcuts.
typo.link_desc: Navigation to other pages or resources. Use `Link` for navigation and `Button` for execution.
typo.mark_desc: Emphasizes hit portions of search results or critical parts with background colors.
typo.outline_usage: Standard UI parts, navigation, form assistance.
typo.quote_desc: Visually separates external quotes or text to be emphasized.
typo.readability_desc: For better readability, it is recommended to limit the line-width of body text to 30–45 characters for Japanese and 45–75 characters for alphabetic languages (English, Portuguese, etc.) using components like `Container`.
typo.semantics_desc: Use heading levels (h1, h2...) correctly according to document structure, not just visual size.
typo.text_desc: Has appropriate line-height and spacing to ensure readability of long text.
typo.title_desc: Possesses visual weight (boldness/size) to indicate page structure.

util.a11y_strong_allies_desc: Utilities like `FocusTrap` are key to high-a11y UIs. Don't overlook them.
util.divider_usage_desc: Separating content clusters. Prefer whitespace (Stack) for simple separators.
util.errorboundary_resilient_note: Use `ErrorBoundary` for critical components to make the system resilient.
util.errorboundary_usage_desc: Prevent app-wide crashes by catching execution errors at the component level.
util.focustrap_usage_desc: Ensure a11y by trapping focus within modals.
util.infscroll_perf_note: For thousands of records, consider `DataGrid` (virtualized) over `InfiniteScroll`.
util.infscroll_usage_desc: Sequentially load data upon reaching the bottom (feed style).
util.markdown_usage_desc: Gracefully formats Markdown strings into structural HTML elements.
util.markdown_xss_note: Ensure proper sanitization for Markdown to prevent XSS attacks.
util.marquee_usage_desc: For heavy emphasis like news tickers. Use sparingly.
util.portal_debug_note: Only use Portals when strictly necessary (e.g., stacking context issues).
util.portal_usage_desc: Avoid parent `overflow: hidden` issues for Modals or Tooltips.
util.scrollarea_usage_desc: Ensures cross-OS scrollbar consistency and better styling.
util.scrollprogress_pos_note: Usually pinned at the top (`Affix` or inside `Header`).
util.scrollprogress_usage_desc: Indicates read progress on long documents.
util.transition_usage_desc: Centralized management for entry/exit CSS animations.
util.vh_usage_desc: Hiding elements visually while keeping them read by screen readers.

utility.guide: WIM UI provides many low-level auxiliary components that support UI construction. Though not direct UI parts, they are essential for enhancing functionality and operability.

vis.chart_colors: Manages default color themes used in charts (CHART_COLORS) and styles for grids and axes.
vis.concentration: 'Concentration' per specific segment such as time axis
vis.large_items: Visualization of proportions with many items (5 or more)
vis.login_freq: (e.g., login frequency by week or time)
vis.ratio: Proportion of each item relative to the whole
vis.recharts_desc: WIM UI's chart components are built based on Recharts, automatically applying styles that match the project's design tokens.
vis.small_items: (When the number of items is less)

unit.guide_desc: Guidelines for selecting CSS units in WIM UI to balance accessibility and maintainability.
unit.item_rem_desc: Relative to the root element (html) font size. The most recommended unit for ensuring accessibility (respecting user browser settings).
unit.item_px_desc: Pixel unit. Used when a fixed size must be maintained regardless of device or settings.
unit.item_relative_desc: Relative to the parent element or container. Ideal for responsive layouts and grid configurations.
unit.item_viewport_desc: Relative to the viewport width or height. Used for full-screen displays and dynamic positioning.
unit.usage_typography: Font size, margin, padding, basic component sizes
unit.usage_layout_flow: Element widths within containers, grid columns, fluid layouts
unit.usage_screen_fit: Hero sections, full-screen backgrounds, modal max-height
unit.a11y_desc: When users change their browser's font size settings, the entire UI scales appropriately if `rem` is used. Overriding with `px` can impair visibility, so `rem` is generally preferred.
unit.fixed_desc: Use `px` for elements that should not blur or lose their proportions due to scaling, such as 1px borders or small corner radii.
unit.responsive_desc: Use relative units for the layout framework to allow flexible changes according to device size.

sortable_list.keyboard_instruction: Press Space or Enter to pick up an item. Use Arrow keys to move, and Space or Enter to drop.

doc.button_a11y_keyboard: Executed using the Space or Enter keys.
doc.button_a11y_role: Uses the standard <button> element with role="button" automatically assigned.
doc.button_anatomy_container: Manages the button's boundary, padding, and rounded corners.
doc.button_anatomy_icon: Supplements the label. Can be placed before or after.
doc.button_anatomy_label: Text indicating the action. Centered alignment is standard.
doc.button_best_practice_1: In principle, limit to one Primary button per visual hierarchy or modal.
doc.button_best_practice_2: Use specific verbs for labels to help users predict the outcome of their action.
doc.button_check1: Does it convey the result (benefit) after clicking?
doc.button_check2: Are you avoiding generic words like "OK" or "Yes"?
doc.button_check3: Does the button make sense by itself without context?
doc.button_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate button type based on the context.
doc.button_choice_primary_when: The main action on the screen, or the single completion button.
doc.button_choice_secondary_when: Auxiliary actions, secondary options paired with Primary (Cancel/Back).
doc.button_choice_tertiary_when: Subtle or supplementary actions in dense UIs.
doc.button_click_area_desc:
Ensure the click area is large enough to prevent misclicks
Especially consider finger operations on mobile devices
doc.button_considerations_visibility_desc:
Make it stand out so users can find it quickly
Increase contrast between background and text
doc.button_consistency_desc:
Keep a consistent design for the same types of buttons to avoid user confusion
Recommended to use the same styles across the site
doc.button_design_intent: Buttons are the primary interface for users to explicitly perform actions (submit, save, delete, navigate) on a screen. Through visual weighting (Priority), they aim to smoothly guide the user to the next step.
doc.button_ex3_eg: When shortening "Save it" to "Save" to fit mobile footers
doc.button_feedback_desc:
Provide feedback upon clicking so users can confirm their action
Use color changes or animations
doc.button_guide_link: Guide: Refer to Guides / Link vs Button for when to use
doc.button_icon_after_desc: Used for actions with directionality like "Next" or "Submit" to express progression.
doc.button_icon_before_desc: The most common placement. Enhances visibility and visually supplements the action's meaning.
doc.button_icon_only_case_desc: Used for widely recognized features (Search, Settings, etc.) to achieve a clean look. Alternative text (aria-label) is required for accessibility.
doc.button_icons_only_desc:
Indicates a specific action
Use only if the icon is self-explanatory
doc.button_icons_with_text_desc: A button combining text and an icon
doc.button_ja_notes:
Notes on Languages:
Too polite expressions might drop visibility. Keep it concise.
doc.button_label_desc:
Use concise and clear words to convey what happens next
Example: Submit, Confirm, Cancel
doc.button_label_guidelines_desc: Use "Verbs" for button labels. This clarifies "what will happen" after clicking.
doc.button_meaning_desc:
Limit to around 3 colors to avoid confusion
Provide icons too, since color-blind users may not distinguish color alone
doc.button_noun_impact: May delay judgment of whether it is an action or a state
doc.button_primary_desc:
Indicates the main action, designed to stand out more than other buttons
Indicates the action you want users to take next
The most desired action on the screen
doc.button_scenario_form: Form Submission: Primary button placed at the bottom right of a modal.
doc.button_scenario_toolbar: Toolbar: Compact layout with icon-only buttons to save space.
doc.button_secondary_desc: Indicates an auxiliary action, designed to be less prominent than the primary button
doc.button_secondary_eg: "Cancel" (paired with primary, dialogue, major changes) or "Back", etc.
doc.button_size_desc_l:
Thumb-friendly size for mobile
Important buttons like CTA (landing pages) or Login
doc.button_size_desc_s:
Suitable size for mobile lists
In tables, sidebars, dense UIs, etc.
doc.button_state_active_desc:
Behavior when clicked
Conveys the pressing action
doc.button_state_disabled_desc:
Makes it inoperable
Conveys that it cannot be clicked
doc.button_state_focus_desc:
Behavior during keyboard operation
Conveys that it is the active target
doc.button_state_hover_desc:
Behavior when hovered
Conveys that it can be clicked
doc.button_state_loading_desc:
Makes it inoperable until processing finishes
Conveys it cannot be clicked until back to normal
Examples: "Loading...", "Processing...", "Saving..."
doc.button_states_desc: Unless intentionally animated, keep the size constant so layout shifts do not occur
doc.button_tertiary_desc:
Appears broken when placed next to primary/secondary without a background
Provides a clear click area when the background is shown
Like a "Text Link" or a "Ghost Button" where the background appears only on hover
doc.button_tertiary_eg: "Edit", "Cancel" (minor changes), "Link to submenu", "Help", "Share to SNS", "Add new", "Upload photo", "See details", etc.
doc.button_tokens_desc: Uses design tokens for background color, text color, borders, and spacing. Major tokens include --wim-color-primary, --wim-spacing-md, --wim-radius-md, etc.
doc.button_var_pri_dest_act: Particularly dangerous operations (Account deletion, clear all data)
doc.button_var_pri_dest_desc: Stands out the most, strongly warning the user "Are you sure?".
doc.button_var_sec_dest_act: General deletions (Remove one from list, delete a message, etc.)
doc.button_var_sec_dest_desc:
Not too prominent but still indicates "dangerous action"
Adjust size to fit properly with border thickness
doc.button_var_ter_dest_act: Subtle deletions (Delete at the corner of settings, minor clear)
doc.button_var_ter_dest_desc: When you don't want it to interfere with other options, but want to alert the user when noticed.
doc.button_variations_desc: Ensure button height remains the same across variations
doc.button_verb_impact: Purpose is clear at a glance
doc.buttongroup_a11y_spec: Assign role="group" to the container and set an aria-label to explain the purpose. Each button must be keyboard accessible.
doc.buttongroup_anatomy_buttons: Each element in the group. In joined mode, they share boundaries.
doc.buttongroup_anatomy_container: Holds the buttons and defines the outer frame and background.
doc.buttongroup_basic_desc: Places buttons horizontally. You can adjust the spacing using the gap property.
doc.buttongroup_best_practice_1: Group only related actions together; unrelated actions should be separate buttons.
doc.buttongroup_best_practice_2: Avoid using primary variant for all buttons in a group — use secondary or tertiary to reduce cognitive load.
doc.buttongroup_choice_group_when: When multiple actions are closely related (e.g., Undo/Redo, Align Left/Center/Right) and you want to visually unify them.
doc.buttongroup_choice_matrix_desc: Choose based on the relevance of actions and the visual weight on the UI.
doc.buttongroup_choice_segmented_when: When presenting mutually exclusive options (tabs-like behavior) and wanting to maintain the current selection state.
doc.buttongroup_choice_single_when: When each action is independent and has a different context.
doc.buttongroup_design_intent: Grouped buttons present a set of parallel actions or related options. By visually joining them, you communicate to the user that they are a single logical group.
doc.buttongroup_joined_desc:
Setting the joined property to true joins the buttons without gaps.
In this mode, the rounded corners of intermediate buttons are removed for a unified design.
doc.buttongroup_long_desc: The ButtonGroup component is used to group and display multiple buttons.
doc.buttongroup_override_desc:
By specifying the priority property, you can unify the priority of all buttons in the group.
Especially when using joined mode, mixed priorities can break the design.
doc.buttongroup_scenario_pagination: Pagination: Unifying Prev, Next, and page numbers into one set.
doc.buttongroup_scenario_toggle: Related action cluster: Joining List / Grid triggers as adjacent buttons. For a persistent exclusive selection, prefer ToggleGroup or SegmentedControl.
doc.buttongroup_scenario_toolbar: Editor Toolbar: Grouping decoration buttons like Bold, Italic, Underline.
doc.buttongroup_sizes_desc: Examples of placing Large, Medium, and Small buttons.
doc.buttongroup_ux_note_desc:
As a UI design principle, it is recommended to have only one primary button per screen (or context).
If you use priority="primary" for multiple buttons, it increases cognitive load.

When unifying a group, choose secondary or tertiary. primary is possible but should be done with care.
doc.copybutton_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.copybutton_anatomy_content: The central icon or label that changes state when the content is successfully copied.
doc.copybutton_anatomy_root: The interactive trigger that manages the copy to clipboard logic and the temporary success state.
doc.copybutton_best_practice_1: Use CopyButton consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.copybutton_best_practice_2: Test CopyButton behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.copybutton_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like Button better suits the use case.
doc.copybutton_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.copybutton_choice_self_when: When CopyButton functionality with standard options is required.
doc.copybutton_comparison_2: Ideal for copying code snippets or unique IDs.
doc.copybutton_comparison_desc: Unlike regular buttons, CopyButton automatically gives visual feedback (icons/messages) after copying.
doc.copybutton_design_intent: CopyButton provides a one-click mechanism to copy text to the clipboard, complete with immediate visual feedback (such as changing the icon to a checkmark) to reassure the user that the action was successful.
doc.copybutton_long_desc: Details and usage for the Copy Button component.
doc.copybutton_scenario_1: Code Snippets: Allowing developers to copy terminal commands or API keys with one click.
doc.copybutton_scenario_2: Referral Links: Enabling users to easily share their unique invite URLs from a profile page.
doc.floatbutton_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.floatbutton_anatomy_content: The central icon or label displayed within the floating trigger.
doc.floatbutton_anatomy_root: The fixed-position container that anchors the button to a specific viewport corner.
doc.floatbutton_auto_shrink_desc: Float buttons auto-shrink based on scroll.
doc.floatbutton_backtop_desc: Quickly return to the top of the page when scrolled down.
doc.floatbutton_basic_usage: Standard implementation of FloatButton, typically positioned in a fixed corner of the screen.
doc.floatbutton_best_practice_1: Use FloatButton consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.floatbutton_best_practice_2: Test FloatButton behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.floatbutton_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like Button better suits the use case.
doc.floatbutton_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.floatbutton_choice_self_when: When FloatButton functionality with standard options is required.
doc.floatbutton_design_intent: FloatButton is used for primary, high-frequency actions that should remain accessible at all times, such as 'Create New', 'Support Chat', or 'Scroll to Top', regardless of the user's scroll position.
doc.floatbutton_extended_desc: Float buttons can have extended text.
doc.floatbutton_extended_sizes_desc: Extended Float buttons are also available in different sizes.
doc.floatbutton_fixed_pos_desc: Define precise fixed coordinates for the floating button.
doc.floatbutton_group_desc: Organize multiple related actions into a single floating container.
doc.floatbutton_long_desc: Details and usage for the Float Button component.
doc.floatbutton_menu_desc: Expands child buttons when clicked or hovered, saving screen space while offering multiple choices.
doc.floatbutton_scenario_1: Customer Support: Providing a persistent 'Help' or 'Chat' trigger at the bottom-right of every page.
doc.floatbutton_scenario_2: Quick Create: A 'New Post' button that stays accessible while browsing a social feed.
doc.floatbutton_sizes_desc: Float buttons are available in different sizes.
doc.floatbutton_tooltip_desc: Display a helpful description when hovering over the floating button.
doc.hamburgermenu_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.hamburgermenu_anatomy_content: The hidden navigation links or menu items that are revealed when the toggle is active.
doc.hamburgermenu_anatomy_root: The interactive 'three-bar' icon that serves as the toggle for the collapsible menu.
doc.hamburgermenu_best_practice_1: Use HamburgerMenu consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.hamburgermenu_best_practice_2: Test HamburgerMenu behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.hamburgermenu_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like Sidebar better suits the use case.
doc.hamburgermenu_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.hamburgermenu_choice_self_when: When HamburgerMenu functionality with standard options is required.
doc.hamburgermenu_design_intent: HamburgerMenu is the industry-standard pattern for mobile navigation. It saves valuable screen real estate by tucking navigation links into a collapsible drawer or overlay, ensuring that the main content remains the focus on small devices.
doc.hamburgermenu_scenario_1: Mobile Headers: Consolidating secondary links on small screens to keep the UI clean.
doc.hamburgermenu_scenario_2: Responsive Apps: Switching from a sidebar to a hamburger menu on tablet viewpoints.
doc.iconbutton_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.iconbutton_anatomy_content: The central SVG icon that visually communicates the button's action.
doc.iconbutton_anatomy_root: The compact container that manages interaction states and ensures a consistent hit area.
doc.iconbutton_best_practice_1: Use IconButton consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.iconbutton_best_practice_2: Test IconButton behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.iconbutton_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like Button better suits the use case.
doc.iconbutton_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.iconbutton_choice_self_when: When IconButton functionality with standard options is required.
doc.iconbutton_design_intent: IconButton is used for triggers that are globally recognized by icons (like 'close', 'edit', or 'delete') where space is limited. It provides a compact interface while maintaining the same interactive properties as a standard button.
doc.iconbutton_long_desc: A button component that displays only an icon.
doc.iconbutton_scenario_1: Table Actions: Providing 'Edit' and 'Delete' triggers in a dense data grid.
doc.iconbutton_scenario_2: Toolbar: Compact formatting triggers (Bold, Italic) in a text editor.
doc.iconbutton_title: A button component that displays only an icon instead of text.
doc.link_a11y_note_desc: Avoid ambiguous text like "Click here" or "Learn more". Instead, use specific descriptive phrases that clarify the destination (e.g., "View Pricing Plans"). This helps screen reader users understand where the link leads and strongly improves SEO.
doc.link_icons_desc: Icons can be placed on the left or right of the label.
doc.link_long_desc: The Link component provides text-based navigation or links to external resources. It supports internationalization, resizing, icon additions, and three levels of priority.
doc.link_priority_desc: Select from primary, secondary, or tertiary based on the link importance.
doc.link_priority_primary_desc: The most visible style. Used for primary actions like "View Pricing Plans".
doc.link_priority_secondary_desc: The standard text link style. Used for general navigation.
doc.link_priority_tertiary_desc: A subtle link style used for supplementary or lower-priority navigation items.
doc.link_priority_tertiary_style_desc: A subtle style with minimal decoration. Suitable for supplementary links or crowded areas.
doc.link_sizes_desc: Supports three sizes: small, medium, and large.
doc.link_vs_button_guide_desc: See Guides / Link vs Button for when to use `` vs `
doc.linkbutton_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.linkbutton_anatomy_content: The text label or icon that indicating the navigation target.
doc.linkbutton_anatomy_root: The anchor-based container that inherits button styling while maintaining semantic link behavior.
doc.linkbutton_best_practice_1: Use LinkButton consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.linkbutton_best_practice_2: Test LinkButton behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.linkbutton_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like Button better suits the use case.
doc.linkbutton_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.linkbutton_choice_self_when: When LinkButton functionality with standard options is required.
doc.linkbutton_design_intent: LinkButton is an anchor element styled to look like a standard button. It is intended for navigation-based actions (e.g., 'View Details', 'Go to Dashboard') where button-like visual prominence is desired but the underlying behavior is a URL transition.
doc.linkbutton_long_desc: A button component that functions as a link.
doc.linkbutton_scenario_1: CTA Sections: Promoting a 'Get Started' journey that leads to a signup page.
doc.linkbutton_scenario_2: Social Sharing: Providing 'View on GitHub' or 'Follow on Twitter' buttons in a footer.
doc.linkbutton_title: A button that functions like a link, used for navigation or actions that look like links.
doc.button_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the button. Space or Enter activates it. Disabled buttons are not reachable by keyboard.
doc.buttongroup_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the button group container. Each button within the group is individually focusable.
doc.copybutton_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the button. Enter or Space copies the target content to the clipboard.
doc.floatbutton_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the float button. Enter or Space activates it. When a group is open, Tab moves focus through each button in the group. Escape collapses the group.
doc.hamburgermenu_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the hamburger button. Enter or Space toggles the menu open or closed.
doc.icon_keyboard_desc: This component does not require specific keyboard interaction. Decorative icons should have aria-hidden="true". Meaningful icons should have an accessible label.
doc.iconbutton_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the button. Enter or Space activates it. Disabled buttons are not reachable by keyboard.
doc.link_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the link. Enter activates it. The link follows standard browser anchor navigation behavior.
doc.linkbutton_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the link button. Enter activates it. It behaves as a standard anchor element for keyboard users.
doc.dropdown_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the dropdown trigger. Enter or Space opens the dropdown. Arrow keys navigate options. Enter selects the focused option. Escape closes the dropdown.
doc.button_is_concise: Keep labels concise; prefer a single line by default.

docs_ai.doc.agentStatus_desc: Real-time agent state indicator (thinking / running / waiting)
docs_ai.doc.agentstatus_a11y_1: The root element has role=status and aria-live=polite, announcing state changes to screen readers.
docs_ai.doc.agentstatus_a11y_2: The indicator icon/dot is aria-hidden; the text label (or aria-label) carries the meaning.
docs_ai.doc.agentstatus_choice_streaming: Stream text output as the model generates it
docs_ai.doc.agentstatus_choice_thought: Show a structured log of past reasoning steps
docs_ai.doc.agentstatus_content_guidelines_1: Use the `message` prop to describe what the agent is doing (e.g., "Searching the web…") rather than relying on the generic status label.
docs_ai.doc.agentstatus_content_guidelines_2: Pair with AgentStatus `done` after a completed action rather than leaving it in `running` — this confirms completion to the user.
docs_ai.doc.agentstatus_design_intent: Designed for agentic interfaces where users need to know at a glance whether the AI is actively processing. The compact indicator can appear inline next to a prompt input, in a chat header, or embedded in a status bar.
docs_ai.doc.agentstatus_i18n_desc: Default status labels are sourced from the `form` namespace (`agent_status.*`). Override with the `message` prop for context-specific text.
docs_ai.doc.agentstatus_intro: AgentStatus displays the current state of an AI agent as a compact animated indicator. It complements ThoughtProcess (a historical log) with a live presence signal — idle, thinking, running, waiting, done, or error.
docs_ai.doc.agentstatus_kb_tab: Tab to focus the element (non-interactive by default).
docs_ai.doc.agentstatus_motion_desc: The thinking state pulses with a scale+opacity animation; running spins a ring. Both respect prefers-reduced-motion.
docs_ai.doc.agentstatus_practice_1: Use size=sm inside dense UIs like chat bubbles; size=lg for dedicated status panels.
docs_ai.doc.agentstatus_practice_2: Reset to idle or done after completion — avoid leaving the component stuck in running state.
docs_ai.doc.agentstatus_responsive: AgentStatus is inline and adapts to any container. The size prop controls visual weight for different layout contexts.
docs_ai.doc.agentstatus_scenario_1_desc: Show in the chat header while the model is generating a response, replacing it with done when finished.
docs_ai.doc.agentstatus_scenario_2_desc: Cycle through running → waiting → running as each tool call dispatches and awaits a result.
docs_ai.doc.aifeedback_a11y_1: Each button carries a descriptive aria-label sourced from i18n keys.
docs_ai.doc.aifeedback_a11y_2: aria-pressed reflects the current selection state for screen readers.
docs_ai.doc.aifeedback_a11y_3: The divider between feedback and regenerate is aria-hidden.
docs_ai.doc.aifeedback_a11y_4: All interactive elements are keyboard-reachable and show :focus-visible outlines.
docs_ai.doc.aifeedback_choice_rate: Rate an AI response as helpful or not helpful
docs_ai.doc.aifeedback_choice_regen: Request a fresh response from the model
docs_ai.doc.aifeedback_design_intent: Inline feedback signals let users rate individual AI responses without disrupting the reading flow. The compact icon-button layout keeps the UI uncluttered while staying accessible via keyboard and screen readers.
docs_ai.doc.aifeedback_guideline_1: Do not add text labels next to the icon buttons — rely on aria-label for accessibility.
docs_ai.doc.aifeedback_guideline_2: Show a brief confirmation message (e.g. "Thanks for your feedback!") in the parent, not inside this component.
docs_ai.doc.aifeedback_i18n_desc: Each button carries a descriptive aria-label sourced from i18n keys.
docs_ai.doc.aifeedback_intro: AIResponseFeedback provides thumbs-up/down feedback controls and an optional regenerate button for rating AI-generated responses. It supports both controlled and uncontrolled usage, toggling feedback off when the same button is clicked twice.
docs_ai.doc.aifeedback_motion_desc: Button state transitions (hover/active/selected) use the --wim-duration-fast token for immediate tactile feedback.
docs_ai.doc.aifeedback_practice_1: Keep the component disabled while a response is still streaming to prevent premature feedback.
docs_ai.doc.aifeedback_practice_2: Persist the feedback value to your backend on selection, not on unmount.
docs_ai.doc.aifeedback_practice_3: Use the controlled feedback prop when the parent needs to reset state (e.g. on regenerate).
docs_ai.doc.aifeedback_responsive: AIResponseFeedback is inline and adapts to its container width. On narrow containers, the compact icon-only layout already fits without adjustment.
docs_ai.doc.aifeedback_scenario_chat: Chat interface: Render below each assistant message bubble to collect per-message quality signals.
docs_ai.doc.aifeedback_scenario_search: Search result ranking: Track thumbs-up rates to feed into RLHF pipelines or A/B testing metrics.
docs_ai.doc.aifeedback_scenario_summary: Document summarisation: Let users mark the summary as helpful or request a revised version via regenerate.
docs_ai.doc.artifactsoverlay_a11y: The overlay is a modal-like region. Focus is trapped when open and restored on close.
docs_ai.doc.artifactsoverlay_best_practice_1: Provide a clear way to close the overlay and return to the chat context.
docs_ai.doc.artifactsoverlay_best_practice_2: Use the fullscreen toggle for complex code or large diagrams to improve readability.
docs_ai.doc.artifactsoverlay_choice_code: Displaying long code files or technical specs
docs_ai.doc.artifactsoverlay_choice_doc: Rendering detailed analysis reports or documents
docs_ai.doc.artifactsoverlay_choice_edit: Use when allowing users to edit code or text in a dedicated side-by-side or overlaid editor view.
docs_ai.doc.artifactsoverlay_choice_preview: Use for full-screen previews of documents or visualizations that require more space than the chat bubble allows.
docs_ai.doc.artifactsoverlay_choice_viz: Showing large data visualizations or graphs
docs_ai.doc.artifactsoverlay_content_guidelines: Keep the title clear and descriptive. Use the actions area for primary operations like Save, Copy, or Download.
docs_ai.doc.artifactsoverlay_design_intent: Derived from the need to separate transient chat messages from persistent, high-value content like code or documents. It slides over the main view to provide a focused reading and interaction space.
docs_ai.doc.artifactsoverlay_guideline_1: Typically slides in from the right to complement the main view.
docs_ai.doc.artifactsoverlay_guideline_2: Use the showFullscreenToggle for content that needs maximum horizontal space.
docs_ai.doc.artifactsoverlay_guideline_3: Often contains a MarkdownRenderer, InteractiveGraph, or CodeDiffViewer.
docs_ai.doc.artifactsoverlay_i18n: All labels, titles, and button text are fully localizable via the consumer.
docs_ai.doc.artifactsoverlay_intro: ArtifactsOverlay is a specialized side-panel for displaying large AI-generated content (Artifacts) without interrupting the main chat context.
docs_ai.doc.artifactsoverlay_keyboard: Escape key closes the overlay. Tab and Shift+Tab cycle through internal actions.
docs_ai.doc.artifactsoverlay_motion: Slides in from the right edge with a smooth transition. Fullscreen mode uses a scale-and-fade transition.
docs_ai.doc.artifactsoverlay_responsive: The overlay width is responsive (min 600px on desktop, full-width on mobile). Fullscreen mode allows it to cover the entire viewport regardless of screen size.
docs_ai.doc.artifactsoverlay_scenarios: Commonly used in AI coding assistants to show proposed file changes or in research tools to show generated reports.
docs_ai.doc.codeblock_a11y_1: The copy button has a descriptive aria-label which updates when the content is successfully copied.
docs_ai.doc.codeblock_a11y_2: The code content is wrapped in a <pre> and <code> tag for semantic correctness.
docs_ai.doc.codeblock_a11y_3: Line numbers are user-select: none to prevent them from being included in manual text selections.
docs_ai.doc.codeblock_a11y_4: All buttons are focusable and support keyboard activation.
docs_ai.doc.codeblock_design_intent: In AI interfaces, code snippets are frequent and often lengthy. CodeBlock standardizes their presentation, ensuring consistent typography (monospaced) and providing essential utilities like copy-pasting. The collapsible feature allows users to scan the surrounding conversation without being forced to scroll through long blocks of code.
docs_ai.doc.codeblock_guideline_1: Always specify the language prop to display the correct language label and provide accessibility hints.
docs_ai.doc.codeblock_guideline_2: Use showLineNumbers for multi-line snippets where line-specific discussion might occur.
docs_ai.doc.codeblock_guideline_3: Keep maxLines at a reasonable height (e.g., 10-15 lines) when isCollapsible is true.
docs_ai.doc.codeblock_i18n_desc: Labels for the "Copy" and "Expand/Collapse" actions are localized via the form namespace.
docs_ai.doc.codeblock_intro: CodeBlock provides a robust container for displaying code snippets with optional line numbering and a built-in "Copy to Clipboard" utility. It supports a collapsible mode to keep long snippets from overwhelming the page layout.
docs_ai.doc.codeblock_kb_arrows: Scroll the code content horizontally if needed.
docs_ai.doc.codeblock_kb_tab: Navigate between the Copy button, Expand/Collapse toggle, and the code content scroll area.
docs_ai.doc.codeblock_motion_desc: Expand/collapse transitions use CSS Grid animations with the --wim-duration-normal token. The chevron icon rotates 180 degrees to indicate state change.
docs_ai.doc.codeblock_practice_1: Disable the copy button if the code is empty or if the feature is not applicable to the context.
docs_ai.doc.codeblock_practice_2: Use the onCopy callback to trigger analytics or custom toast notifications.
docs_ai.doc.codeblock_practice_3: Ensure the background color of the CodeBlock contrasts well with the surrounding application background.
docs_ai.doc.codeblock_responsive: The CodeBlock container fills the width of its parent and provides horizontal scrolling for long lines. On narrow viewports, it's recommended to use the collapsible mode to save vertical space.
docs_ai.doc.codeblock_scenario_1_desc: Displaying code suggestions or fixes provided by an AI assistant.
docs_ai.doc.codeblock_scenario_2_desc: Rendering code examples with line numbers for easy reference.
docs_ai.doc.codeblock_scenario_3_desc: Using the collapsible mode to show truncated stack traces or logs.
docs_ai.doc.codediff_a11y_1: Apply and Reject buttons carry descriptive visible labels and are keyboard-reachable.
docs_ai.doc.codediff_a11y_2: Line number columns are aria-hidden to avoid repetitive screen-reader output.
docs_ai.doc.codediff_a11y_3: The copy button label changes to Copied! after activation and reverts after 2s.
docs_ai.doc.codediff_a11y_4: View-toggle buttons use aria-pressed to reflect the active view for assistive technology.
docs_ai.doc.codediff_content_guidelines_1: Add an explanatory message above the component when AI is proposing the change so users understand context before reviewing.
docs_ai.doc.codediff_content_guidelines_2: Use `filename` when the path helps orient the reviewer. Omit it for anonymous snippets.
docs_ai.doc.codediff_design_intent: Designed for agentic coding interfaces where AI proposes code changes the user must review. The split view mirrors git diff; the unified view offers a compact single-pane alternative. Below 640 px the view automatically switches to unified.
docs_ai.doc.codediff_i18n_desc: Apply, Reject, Copy, and view-toggle labels are sourced from the `form` namespace and fully localizable.
docs_ai.doc.codediff_intro: CodeDiffViewer displays before/after code changes in git-diff style with line-level highlighting. It supports split and unified views, and can expose Apply/Reject actions for AI-assisted code editing workflows.
docs_ai.doc.codediff_kb_tab: Move focus between Apply, Reject, Copy, and view-toggle buttons.
docs_ai.doc.codediff_motion_desc: No animations. Visual weight comes from background-color highlights on added/removed lines, not motion.
docs_ai.doc.codediff_practice_1: Provide `onApply`/`onReject` callbacks when the diff represents a proposed change the user needs to act on.
docs_ai.doc.codediff_practice_2: Prefer `filename` over bare `language` to give reviewers file context at a glance.
docs_ai.doc.codediff_responsive: Below 640 px the component switches automatically from split to unified view. The header wraps with flex-wrap, so action buttons remain reachable on narrow screens.
docs_ai.doc.codediff_scenario_1_desc: AI suggests file modifications; CodeDiffViewer lets the user inspect and apply changes in one click.
docs_ai.doc.codediff_scenario_2_desc: Surface key hunks from a pull request diff alongside an AI summary.
docs_ai.doc.interactivegraph_a11y: The graph canvas is zoomable via keyboard (+/- keys). Nodes can be navigated and selected using arrow keys.
docs_ai.doc.interactivegraph_best_practice_1: Provide a 'Recenter' or 'Fit to View' button for large graphs to help users re-orient.
docs_ai.doc.interactivegraph_best_practice_2: Use different node shapes or border styles to indicate different node categories.
docs_ai.doc.interactivegraph_choice_agent: Showing interactions between different AI agents
docs_ai.doc.interactivegraph_choice_mapping: Mapping out multi-step agent workflows or state machine transitions visually.
docs_ai.doc.interactivegraph_choice_rag: Visualizing RAG source clusters and retrieval paths
docs_ai.doc.interactivegraph_choice_state: Visualizing state machines or complex decision trees
docs_ai.doc.interactivegraph_choice_viz: Visualizing complex relationships, such as RAG knowledge graphs or hierarchical data structures.
docs_ai.doc.interactivegraph_content_guidelines: Ensure node labels are concise. Use color coding sparingly to distinguish between different types of nodes or states.
docs_ai.doc.interactivegraph_design_intent: Complex AI processes like retrieval or multi-agent orchestration are easier to understand visually. InteractiveGraph provides a performant, zoomable canvas that follows WIM design tokens.
docs_ai.doc.interactivegraph_guideline_1: Allow users to zoom and pan to explore dense networks.
docs_ai.doc.interactivegraph_guideline_2: Nodes use WIM surface tokens and shadows to maintain visual hierarchy.
docs_ai.doc.interactivegraph_guideline_3: Use in large areas or within an ArtifactsOverlay to provide enough room for exploration.
docs_ai.doc.interactivegraph_i18n: Node content and tooltips are provided by the data source and support full localization.
docs_ai.doc.interactivegraph_intro: InteractiveGraph provides a canvas for visualizing node-based data. Ideal for RAG knowledge bases, agent workflows, or state machines.
docs_ai.doc.interactivegraph_keyboard: Use arrow keys to pan. Use +/- to zoom. Enter to select the focused node.
docs_ai.doc.interactivegraph_motion: Nodes and edges animate smoothly when the layout changes. Zoom and pan interactions use standard easing.
docs_ai.doc.interactivegraph_responsive: The graph container fills the available space. On mobile, users can use pinch-to-zoom and touch-drag to navigate.
docs_ai.doc.interactivegraph_scenarios: Ideal for showing how an AI agent retrieved information from a vector database or how a complex logic chain was executed.
docs_ai.doc.markdownrenderer_a11y: Generates semantic HTML tags. Headings are correctly mapped to title levels for screen reader navigation.
docs_ai.doc.markdownrenderer_best_practice_1: Use semantic headings (H1, H2, H3) to structure long AI responses.
docs_ai.doc.markdownrenderer_best_practice_2: Incorporate CodeBlocks for any technical snippets to ensure proper formatting and copy functionality.
docs_ai.doc.markdownrenderer_choice_docs: Rendering technical documentation or README files
docs_ai.doc.markdownrenderer_choice_rich: When support for tables and complex lists is required
docs_ai.doc.markdownrenderer_content_guidelines: Follow standard Markdown syntax. Ensure that headings are used hierarchically for better accessibility.
docs_ai.doc.markdownrenderer_design_intent: In AI applications, LLM responses are often in Markdown. MarkdownRenderer ensures these responses look like native part of the WIM ecosystem, using semantic Title, Text, and CodeBlock components.
docs_ai.doc.markdownrenderer_guideline_1: All headings and text styles automatically match the Title and Text components.
docs_ai.doc.markdownrenderer_guideline_2: Automatically uses the WIM CodeBlock component to render code snippets.
docs_ai.doc.markdownrenderer_guideline_3: For very long content, consider wrapping this in a ScrollArea or using it inside an ArtifactsOverlay.
docs_ai.doc.markdownrenderer_i18n: Content is rendered as-is. All wrapper components (like CodeBlock) use localized strings.
docs_ai.doc.markdownrenderer_intro: MarkdownRenderer converts a markdown string into WIM UI components. It uses react-markdown under the hood and applies WIM's typography system.
docs_ai.doc.markdownrenderer_keyboard: Standard browser text selection and keyboard navigation for links and code blocks.
docs_ai.doc.markdownrenderer_motion: No specific animations for static text. In StreamingText, new content appears with a subtle fade.
docs_ai.doc.markdownrenderer_responsive: MarkdownRenderer fills the width of its parent. Components like CodeBlock and Tables handle their own internal horizontal scrolling to prevent layout breaking on small screens.
docs_ai.doc.markdownrenderer_scenarios: Used in chat bubbles, documentation pages, or within Artifacts to render formatted AI output.
docs_ai.doc.modelselector_a11y_1: The trigger exposes aria-haspopup, aria-expanded, and aria-controls; the list uses role="listbox" with role="option" items.
docs_ai.doc.modelselector_a11y_2: Arrow keys move the active option and aria-activedescendant tracks it for screen readers.
docs_ai.doc.modelselector_a11y_3: Disabled models carry aria-disabled and cannot be selected by pointer or keyboard.
docs_ai.doc.modelselector_choice_combobox: A long, searchable list of options
docs_ai.doc.modelselector_choice_select: A plain single-choice dropdown without metadata
docs_ai.doc.modelselector_choice_self: Switching models with visible cost and context metadata
docs_ai.doc.modelselector_content_guidelines_1: Keep model names short and recognizable; move the provider into the description line.
docs_ai.doc.modelselector_content_guidelines_2: Format context length compactly (e.g. 128K) and price per 1M tokens so numbers stay scannable.
docs_ai.doc.modelselector_design_intent: Choosing a model is a decision made on trade-offs: capability, context length, and cost. ModelSelector puts those numbers next to each name so the choice is informed rather than guessed.
docs_ai.doc.modelselector_i18n_desc: All built-in meta text (placeholder and the Context/In/Out prefixes) is overridable through the labels prop; model names and prices come from your data.
docs_ai.doc.modelselector_intro: ModelSelector is a dropdown for switching between AI models, surfacing the metadata that matters when choosing one — context window size and per-token pricing.
docs_ai.doc.modelselector_kb_nav: Move between models, skipping disabled ones
docs_ai.doc.modelselector_kb_open: Open the dropdown and focus the current model
docs_ai.doc.modelselector_kb_select: Select the active model, or close without changing
docs_ai.doc.modelselector_motion_desc: The dropdown opens with a short scale-and-fade transition; the chevron rotates 180° to signal the open state.
docs_ai.doc.modelselector_practice_1: Persist the selected model per conversation so switching does not affect existing threads.
docs_ai.doc.modelselector_practice_2: Disable rather than hide deprecated models so links and history remain understandable.
docs_ai.doc.modelselector_practice_3: Hide the pricing row in consumer apps where cost is abstracted away from the user.
docs_ai.doc.modelselector_responsive: The trigger sizes to its content and the dropdown matches the trigger width; set fullWidth to fill a narrow sidebar or mobile sheet.
docs_ai.doc.modelselector_scenario_1_desc: Placed next to the prompt input so users can switch models before sending a message.
docs_ai.doc.modelselector_scenario_2_desc: Used as the default-model picker where pricing and context help teams pick a sensible default.
docs_ai.doc.promptinput_a11y_1: The text area is associated with a label or carries an aria-label.
docs_ai.doc.promptinput_a11y_2: Submit and Attach buttons are focusable and have descriptive labels.
docs_ai.doc.promptinput_a11y_3: Character count and error messages are announced via aria-live.
docs_ai.doc.promptinput_choice_self: Single-turn or multi-turn chat interfaces where users input instructions.
docs_ai.doc.promptinput_choice_textarea: Simple multi-line text entry without AI-specific needs (attach, auto-resize).
docs_ai.doc.promptinput_design_intent: Traditional inputs are often too small for complex AI prompts. PromptInput uses a multi-line auto-resizing area that maintains context while typing long instructions. It visually distinguishes between the text entry and action buttons (like attach or send) to ensure a high-efficiency user experience.
docs_ai.doc.promptinput_guideline_1: Use the placeholder to give examples of effective prompts.
docs_ai.doc.promptinput_guideline_2: Enable showAttach if the model supports file or image grounding.
docs_ai.doc.promptinput_guideline_3: Use fullWidth when the input is the primary action at the bottom of the screen.
docs_ai.doc.promptinput_intro: PromptInput provides a versatile text area optimized for AI prompting, featuring auto-resizing, attachment support, and a dedicated submit action. It handles keyboard shortcuts (e.g., Cmd/Ctrl+Enter to submit) out of the box.
docs_ai.doc.promptinput_kb_attach: Trigger the file selection dialog (if focused).
docs_ai.doc.promptinput_motion_desc: The container height animates smoothly as text wraps, using standard easing tokens.
docs_ai.doc.promptinput_practice_1: Pair with a character counter for models with strict token limits.
docs_ai.doc.promptinput_practice_2: Provide clear error messages if the input is too long or contains invalid characters.
docs_ai.doc.promptinput_practice_3: Disable the submit button while the AI is already generating a response.
docs_ai.doc.promptinput_responsive: The input container fills the available width. On small screens, the action buttons remain accessible within the input area.
docs_ai.doc.promptinput_scenario_1: Conversational assistant where users type long queries.
docs_ai.doc.promptinput_scenario_2: Image generation tool where users provide detailed descriptive prompts.
docs_ai.doc.promptinput_scenario_3: Data analysis tool where users upload CSV files via the attach button.
docs_ai.doc.sourcecitation_a11y_guideline_1: When rendered as a link, the accessible name comes from the aria-label (title or numbered label).
docs_ai.doc.sourcecitation_a11y_guideline_2: The external link icon is aria-hidden — the rel="noopener noreferrer" and target="_blank" attributes are set automatically.
docs_ai.doc.sourcecitation_a11y_guideline_3: The index badge is aria-hidden so screen readers skip the number and read the full title instead.
docs_ai.doc.sourcecitation_best_practice_1: Limit to 5–6 visible citations; additional sources can be hidden behind a "Show more" toggle.
docs_ai.doc.sourcecitation_best_practice_2: Always provide a title. If no URL is available, omit the url prop rather than passing an empty string.
docs_ai.doc.sourcecitation_best_practice_3: Use the index prop only when you also annotate the prose with matching [n] markers.
docs_ai.doc.sourcecitation_choice_list: Show one or more cited sources below an AI response
docs_ai.doc.sourcecitation_choice_table: Full bibliography or paginated source list
docs_ai.doc.sourcecitation_content_guideline_1: Keep titles concise — they are truncated with an ellipsis at the card width.
docs_ai.doc.sourcecitation_content_guideline_2: Descriptions should be a single excerpt sentence (≤ 2 lines). Avoid full paragraphs.
docs_ai.doc.sourcecitation_content_guideline_3: Domain is auto-derived from the URL. Override only when the hostname is ambiguous.
docs_ai.doc.sourcecitation_design_intent: Grounding AI responses in verifiable sources is essential for trust. The compact card layout makes citations scannable without overwhelming the answer text. The numeric index badge ties each card back to inline citation markers in the prose.
docs_ai.doc.sourcecitation_i18n_desc: The aria-label for numbered citations uses the form namespace key source_citation.source_label (interpolated with index).
docs_ai.doc.sourcecitation_intro: SourceCitation displays a single cited reference — title, domain, and optional description — as a compact card. When a URL is provided it becomes a focusable link that opens in a new tab. Use SourceCitationList to render multiple sources as a wrapping grid.
docs_ai.doc.sourcecitation_keyboard_enter: Open the source URL in a new tab
docs_ai.doc.sourcecitation_keyboard_tab: Move focus to the next citation card (when rendered as a link)
docs_ai.doc.sourcecitation_motion_desc: Hover transitions on the link card use --wim-duration-fast for border-color and background changes, keeping the interaction snappy.
docs_ai.doc.sourcecitation_responsive_desc: SourceCitationList uses flex-wrap so cards reflow naturally on narrow containers. Each SourceCitation card has a max-width to keep it readable at any viewport.
docs_ai.doc.sourcecitation_scenario_assistant: Research assistant: Link academic papers or web pages that the model consulted.
docs_ai.doc.sourcecitation_scenario_rag: RAG responses: Attach retrieved document chunks as citations below the answer.
docs_ai.doc.sourcecitation_scenario_wiki: Internal knowledge base: Surface internal wiki pages as non-link citation cards (no URL).
docs_ai.doc.streamingtext_a11y_1: The content is updated in an aria-live="polite" region (managed internally).
docs_ai.doc.streamingtext_a11y_2: Markdown headings and lists are rendered with correct semantic tags.
docs_ai.doc.streamingtext_a11y_3: The thinking indicator is announced as "The assistant is thinking".
docs_ai.doc.streamingtext_choice_loader: While waiting for the first chunk of data (before streaming begins).
docs_ai.doc.streamingtext_choice_markdown: Static content that doesn't need to be streamed.
docs_ai.doc.streamingtext_choice_self: Real-time AI chat responses or live text updates.
docs_ai.doc.streamingtext_design_intent: Showing text as it's generated reduces perceived latency and mimics human-like communication. StreamingText ensures that Markdown formatting is applied incrementally and that the scroll position remains stable during the stream.
docs_ai.doc.streamingtext_guideline_1: Ensure isStreaming is true while data is still being received.
docs_ai.doc.streamingtext_guideline_2: Use showThinking while waiting for the model to start responding.
docs_ai.doc.streamingtext_guideline_3: Avoid very high streaming speeds that may overwhelm the user's ability to read.
docs_ai.doc.streamingtext_intro: StreamingText renders text content with a dynamic "typing" effect, simulating the real-time generation characteristic of large language models. It supports Markdown rendering and can display a "thinking" indicator when generation is pending.
docs_ai.doc.streamingtext_kb_desc: As this is a read-only component, standard keyboard navigation for text and links applies.
docs_ai.doc.streamingtext_motion_desc: New characters appear with a subtle opacity fade. The "thinking" dots use a gentle pulse animation.
docs_ai.doc.streamingtext_practice_1: Provide a "Stop" button in the parent component to let users cancel long streams.
docs_ai.doc.streamingtext_practice_2: Ensure the background contrast is sufficient for reading the streaming text.
docs_ai.doc.streamingtext_practice_3: Use a monospaced font if the stream contains code or data tables.
docs_ai.doc.streamingtext_responsive: The text flows and wraps according to its container width. Scroll management ensures the latest content remains visible on small screens.
docs_ai.doc.streamingtext_scenario_1: Chatbot interface where responses appear word-by-word.
docs_ai.doc.streamingtext_scenario_2: Code generation tool showing snippets as they are written.
docs_ai.doc.streamingtext_scenario_3: Live transcriptions of audio or speech.
docs_ai.doc.terminal_a11y_1: The output body has role=log and aria-live=polite so screen readers announce new lines.
docs_ai.doc.terminal_a11y_3: Copy and Clear buttons carry descriptive aria-label attributes.
docs_ai.doc.terminal_choice_agent: Agent command execution and live output
docs_ai.doc.terminal_choice_error: Error output or process exit messages
docs_ai.doc.terminal_choice_thought: AI reasoning steps with status indicators
docs_ai.doc.terminal_content_guidelines_1: Use `type="input"` for commands, `type="output"` for stdout, `type="error"` for stderr, and `type="info"` for status messages to get correct color coding.
docs_ai.doc.terminal_content_guidelines_2: Provide a `title` that names the running process (e.g., `npm install`) so users immediately know what is executing.
docs_ai.doc.terminal_design_intent: Terminal provides a familiar developer UI for surfacing what an AI agent is doing under the hood. The macOS-style chrome signals this is a terminal at a glance without requiring users to parse a wall of text.
docs_ai.doc.terminal_i18n_desc: Copy and Clear button aria-labels are sourced from the `form` namespace (`terminal.copy_label`, `terminal.copied_label`, `terminal.clear_label`).
docs_ai.doc.terminal_intro: Terminal renders command input, output, errors, and info lines in a dark monospace window. It supports ANSI SGR color codes, auto-scroll to the latest output, and optional copy/clear actions.
docs_ai.doc.terminal_kb_tab: Move focus between Copy and Clear buttons.
docs_ai.doc.terminal_motion_desc: Auto-scroll jumps immediately to the latest line with no animation, minimizing perceived latency during agentic sessions.
docs_ai.doc.terminal_practice_1: Keep `autoScroll` enabled while the agent is running; disable it if the user scrolls up to inspect earlier output.
docs_ai.doc.terminal_practice_2: Set an explicit `height` to cap vertical growth when embedding the terminal in a constrained layout.
docs_ai.doc.terminal_responsive: The terminal fills its container width and scrolls horizontally for long lines. Set an explicit `height` to cap vertical growth in constrained layouts.
docs_ai.doc.terminal_scenario_1_desc: Streaming shell output from an AI agent building a project or running tests.
docs_ai.doc.terminal_scenario_2_desc: Displaying build and deploy steps in a CI/CD workflow embedded in a developer dashboard.
docs_ai.doc.thoughtprocess_a11y: The container uses role='region' with an aria-label. Individual steps are announced as they complete.
docs_ai.doc.thoughtprocess_a11y_1: The container has role="region" with an accessible name.
docs_ai.doc.thoughtprocess_a11y_3: Status changes are announced via aria-live in the parent if critical.
docs_ai.doc.thoughtprocess_best_practice_1: Collapse completed processes by default in long conversations to keep the UI clean.
docs_ai.doc.thoughtprocess_best_practice_2: Use the error status clearly to identify which specific step in a chain failed.
docs_ai.doc.thoughtprocess_choice_self: Complex multi-step AI tasks or agent reasoning.
docs_ai.doc.thoughtprocess_choice_timeline: General historical events or logs unrelated to AI reasoning.
docs_ai.doc.thoughtprocess_choice_transparency: Use when users need to see the internal steps of an AI agent to build trust or for debugging.
docs_ai.doc.thoughtprocess_choice_wait: Use to manage user expectations during long-running tasks by showing active progress.
docs_ai.doc.thoughtprocess_content_guidelines: Keep step descriptions short and actionable. Use the children area for detailed logs or terminal output.
docs_ai.doc.thoughtprocess_design_intent: Transparency in AI reasoning builds user confidence and aids in debugging. ThoughtProcess provides a standardized way to show the progress of background tasks, distinguishing between the high-level goal and individual execution steps.
docs_ai.doc.thoughtprocess_guideline_1: Use title to describe the overall goal (e.g., "Analyzing data...").
docs_ai.doc.thoughtprocess_guideline_2: Update ThoughtStep statuses in real-time as steps complete.
docs_ai.doc.thoughtprocess_guideline_3: Provide meaningful children content for steps to explain what happened in that phase.
docs_ai.doc.thoughtprocess_i18n: Status labels (Thinking, Completed, Error) are localized. Custom step titles are provided by the consumer.
docs_ai.doc.thoughtprocess_i18n_desc: Status labels and screen reader announcements are localized via the form namespace.
docs_ai.doc.thoughtprocess_intro: ThoughtProcess visualizes the "reasoning" steps of an AI agent or complex chain-of-thought process. It uses a timeline-style list of steps, each with its own status (pending, completed, or error), and can be collapsed to save space.
docs_ai.doc.thoughtprocess_kb_focus: Move focus through the toggle and any interactive links within steps.
docs_ai.doc.thoughtprocess_keyboard: Enter or Space on a step header toggles its expanded state. Tab moves between steps.
docs_ai.doc.thoughtprocess_motion: Steps expand and collapse with a smooth accordion-style animation. Status icons pulse when active.
docs_ai.doc.thoughtprocess_motion_desc: Expansion uses CSS transitions on the height and opacity. Status icons animate into view when changed.
docs_ai.doc.thoughtprocess_practice_1: Default to collapsed if the process is long and has already completed.
docs_ai.doc.thoughtprocess_practice_2: Use the 'error' status to highlight exactly where a chain failed.
docs_ai.doc.thoughtprocess_practice_3: Avoid too many steps (>10); group related sub-tasks if necessary.
docs_ai.doc.thoughtprocess_responsive: The timeline layout wraps and scales to fit the container width. The toggle button remains accessible on touch devices.
docs_ai.doc.thoughtprocess_scenario_1: Agentic workflows: Showing a multi-step plan before execution.
docs_ai.doc.thoughtprocess_scenario_2: Code execution: Listing steps like "Spinning up environment", "Running script", "Cleaning up".
docs_ai.doc.thoughtprocess_scenarios: Common in multi-agent workflows, code execution pipelines, or complex RAG retrieval steps.
docs_ai.doc.threadlist_a11y_1: The list is wrapped in a nav landmark with an accessible label so screen-reader users can jump to history.
docs_ai.doc.threadlist_a11y_2: The active thread is marked with aria-current so its selected state is announced.
docs_ai.doc.threadlist_a11y_3: Each delete button has its own aria-label so its purpose is clear out of context.
docs_ai.doc.threadlist_choice_list: A generic list of items without conversation semantics
docs_ai.doc.threadlist_choice_self: A conversation-history sidebar with previews and deletion
docs_ai.doc.threadlist_choice_sidebar: The surrounding collapsible app navigation shell
docs_ai.doc.threadlist_content_guidelines_1: Derive titles from the first user message and truncate to a single line; show a short preview below.
docs_ai.doc.threadlist_content_guidelines_2: Use relative timestamps (2m, 1h, 1d) so recency reads faster than absolute dates.
docs_ai.doc.threadlist_design_intent: Chat history is a navigation surface first. ThreadList keeps titles, previews, and timestamps legible at a glance and reveals destructive actions only on hover or focus.
docs_ai.doc.threadlist_i18n_desc: The new-conversation, empty, and delete labels are overridable through the labels prop; thread content comes from your data.
docs_ai.doc.threadlist_intro: ThreadList renders a conversation-history sidebar for AI chat apps — a scrollable list of past threads with an optional new-conversation action and per-thread deletion.
docs_ai.doc.threadlist_kb_activate: Open the focused thread or trigger its action
docs_ai.doc.threadlist_kb_tab: Move between threads and their delete buttons
docs_ai.doc.threadlist_motion_desc: Rows use a quick background-color transition on hover and focus; the delete button fades in rather than shifting layout.
docs_ai.doc.threadlist_practice_1: Confirm deletion for threads with meaningful content to avoid accidental loss.
docs_ai.doc.threadlist_practice_2: Keep the active thread visible when the list scrolls, and highlight it clearly.
docs_ai.doc.threadlist_practice_3: Group or paginate very long histories rather than rendering thousands of rows at once.
docs_ai.doc.threadlist_responsive: The list fills the width of its container, making it equally at home in a fixed sidebar or a full-width mobile drawer.
docs_ai.doc.threadlist_scenario_1_desc: A persistent left rail listing every conversation, with a new-chat button pinned at the top.
docs_ai.doc.threadlist_scenario_2_desc: Rendered inside a Drawer that slides in over the chat on small screens.
docs_ai.doc.usagemeter_a11y_1: The component uses role="meter" with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, and aria-valuemax.
docs_ai.doc.usagemeter_a11y_2: An accessible label describes the used and maximum values for screen readers even when the bar is hidden.
docs_ai.doc.usagemeter_a11y_3: Warning and danger states are conveyed by the readout value, not by color alone.
docs_ai.doc.usagemeter_choice_self: Showing token usage against a context or quota limit
docs_ai.doc.usagemeter_choice_stats: A static metric tile without a budget or limit
docs_ai.doc.usagemeter_content_guidelines_1: Show both the used and maximum values so the remaining headroom is obvious; offer a percentage as an alternative readout.
docs_ai.doc.usagemeter_content_guidelines_2: Format large counts with thousands separators so 128000 reads as 128,000.
docs_ai.doc.usagemeter_design_intent: Token budgets are invisible until they are exceeded. UsageMeter makes headroom continuously visible and uses color to warn before a request is truncated or rejected.
docs_ai.doc.usagemeter_i18n_desc: The label and unit text are overridable through the labels prop; numeric formatting uses grouped thousands independent of locale.
docs_ai.doc.usagemeter_intro: UsageMeter (also exported as TokenCounter) visualizes token consumption against a budget such as a model's context window — a labeled bar plus a numeric readout that shifts to warning and danger colors near the limit.
docs_ai.doc.usagemeter_kb_desc: UsageMeter is a read-only status display and is not itself focusable or interactive.
docs_ai.doc.usagemeter_motion_desc: The bar animates its width and color as usage changes, so approaching the limit reads as motion, not just a static number.
docs_ai.doc.usagemeter_practice_1: Set warn and danger thresholds that match the real cost of overflowing, not arbitrary round numbers.
docs_ai.doc.usagemeter_practice_2: Update the value as tokens stream in so the meter reflects live consumption.
docs_ai.doc.usagemeter_practice_3: Drop the bar and keep the counter alone when there is no meaningful maximum to measure against.
docs_ai.doc.usagemeter_responsive: The meter fills the width of its container and the readout uses tabular figures so numbers stay aligned as they change.
docs_ai.doc.usagemeter_scenario_1_desc: Shown under a prompt input to track how much of the context window the current conversation consumes.
docs_ai.doc.usagemeter_scenario_2_desc: Displayed in a billing panel to show monthly token usage against the plan allowance.
docs_ai.doc.voicevisualizer_a11y_1: The SVG is aria-hidden by default since it is decorative. Add aria-label to the parent container to describe the audio context.
docs_ai.doc.voicevisualizer_a11y_2: Use isActive=false to apply reduced opacity when the visualizer is not capturing audio — this prevents users from thinking audio is active when it is not.
docs_ai.doc.voicevisualizer_choice_self: Visualize microphone or audio playback levels
docs_ai.doc.voicevisualizer_content_guidelines_1: For bars mode, normalize data from `AnalyserNode.getByteFrequencyData()` (0–255) by dividing by 255 before passing.
docs_ai.doc.voicevisualizer_content_guidelines_2: For waveform mode, use `AnalyserNode.getByteTimeDomainData()` (0–255) and normalize by dividing by 255. Silence = 0.5.
docs_ai.doc.voicevisualizer_design_intent: Voice interfaces need a visual confirmation that audio is being captured and processed. VoiceVisualizer provides this without requiring any Canvas code or audio setup — the consumer feeds normalized data and the component handles all rendering.
docs_ai.doc.voicevisualizer_i18n_desc: This component contains no text content. No i18n configuration is required.
docs_ai.doc.voicevisualizer_intro: VoiceVisualizer renders an SVG audio-level indicator in two styles: animated bars or a smooth waveform. It accepts live amplitude data from the Web Audio API AnalyserNode (normalized 0–1), and falls back to a looping idle animation when no data is provided.
docs_ai.doc.voicevisualizer_kb_tab: The SVG is not keyboard-focusable (aria-hidden). Wrap in a focusable container if needed.
docs_ai.doc.voicevisualizer_motion_desc: Bars animate with a staggered scale-Y pulse during idle; the waveform scrolls horizontally. Data-driven updates use CSS transitions for smooth height changes. Animations are disabled under prefers-reduced-motion.
docs_ai.doc.voicevisualizer_practice_1: Drive the component with `requestAnimationFrame` to keep data in sync with the audio buffer (~60 fps).
docs_ai.doc.voicevisualizer_practice_2: Set `isActive={false}` when the audio context is paused or the mic permission is not granted.
docs_ai.doc.voicevisualizer_responsive: VoiceVisualizer uses `width=100%` so it fills its container naturally. Control size via the parent container width and the `height` prop.
docs_ai.doc.voicevisualizer_scenario_1_desc: Display the microphone level while a user is speaking to an AI assistant, confirming the voice is being captured.
docs_ai.doc.voicevisualizer_scenario_2_desc: Show frequency bars during TTS output to give visual feedback while the AI is speaking.

doc.sparkline_a11y_desc: Provide an ariaLabel summarizing the trend (e.g. "Revenue up 12% over 7 days"); without one, the sparkline is decorative and hidden from assistive tech, so the adjacent value carries the meaning.
doc.sparkline_best_practice_1: Fix the y-domain with min and max when comparing several sparklines so their heights are comparable.
doc.sparkline_best_practice_2: Use color to signal direction (positive vs. negative) rather than to distinguish many series.
doc.sparkline_choice_alt_when: The reader needs axes, tooltips, or exact values.
doc.sparkline_choice_matrix_desc: Use a Sparkline for compact, inline trends and a full chart when the reader needs to read values.
doc.sparkline_choice_self_when: Show a trend inside a cell, tile, or list row with no need for axes.
doc.sparkline_design_intent: A sparkline trades precision for density: no axes, labels, or gridlines, just the trend line at a glance. It is meant to sit beside a number, not replace a full chart.
doc.sparkline_long_desc: Sparkline is a tiny, axis-free chart for embedding a trend inline — inside a table cell, a Stats tile, or a Leaderboard row — where the shape of the data matters more than its exact values.
doc.sparkline_scenario_1: A DataGrid column shows each row's 30-day trend next to its current metric.
doc.sparkline_scenario_2: A Stats tile pairs a headline number with a sparkline of its recent history.
