doc.colorinput_choice_self_when: When ColorInput functionality with standard options is required.
doc.colorinput_design_intent: ColorInput allows users to enter exact color values via text while providing a live preview. It is ideal for design settings or theme configurations where precise hex or RGB codes are necessary.
doc.colorinput_long_desc: A component that provides a color input.
doc.colorinput_scenario_1: Brand Settings: Allowing admins to specify exact primary colors for their white-label app.
doc.colorinput_scenario_2: CSS Editors: Providing a way to enter and preview hex codes in a developer-focused tool.
doc.colorinput_title: Field for selecting colors and entering hex codes with preview
doc.colorpicker_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.colorpicker_anatomy_content: The visual palette or spectrum where users can interactively select a color.
doc.colorpicker_anatomy_root: The trigger or container that manages the picker's visibility and current selection state.
doc.colorpicker_best_practice_1: Use ColorPicker consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.colorpicker_best_practice_2: Test ColorPicker behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.colorpicker_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like ColorInput better suits the use case.
doc.colorpicker_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.colorpicker_choice_self_when: When ColorPicker functionality with standard options is required.
doc.colorpicker_design_intent: ColorPicker provides a visual interface for selecting colors from a spectrum. It is intended for scenarios where users need to creatively explore and 'find' a color rather than entering a known value.
doc.colorpicker_long_desc: A component for users to pick colors. It wraps the native input type="color" and adjusts its styles.
doc.colorpicker_scenario_1: Design Tools: Picking a custom background color for a presentation slide.
doc.colorpicker_scenario_2: User Personalization: Letting users choose a highlight color for their dashboard theme.
doc.colorpicker_title: Component for choosing colors from a visual palette
doc.datepicker_a11y_2: `aria-label` or `aria-describedby` is set for the input field.
doc.datepicker_a11y_4: Disabled dates are explicitly marked with aria-disabled.
doc.datepicker_a11y_desc: The calendar popup uses role='dialog' with aria-label. Date cells are navigable with arrow keys. Selected date is announced with aria-selected.
doc.datepicker_a11y_keyboard: Navigate through dates in the calendar with arrow keys and make selection possible with the Enter key. Also, allow closing the calendar with the Escape key.
doc.datepicker_adv_1: Intuitive date entry without needing specific calendar knowledge.
doc.datepicker_adv_2: Visual confirmation of dates via the calendar UI.
doc.datepicker_adv_3: Automatically prevents format errors during entry.
doc.datepicker_adv_4: Full support for accessible keyboard navigation.
doc.datepicker_anatomy_input: A field that displays the currently selected date and accepts keyboard input.
doc.datepicker_anatomy_popup: A floating panel for visually listing and selecting dates.
doc.datepicker_best_practice_1: Use clear date format labels (e.g., 'MM/DD/YYYY') so users know the expected input format.
doc.datepicker_best_practice_2: Provide both keyboard input and calendar picker to accommodate different user preferences.
doc.datepicker_choice_input_when: When entering a date the user already remembers quickly (e.g., date of birth, expiration date).
doc.datepicker_choice_matrix_desc: Select the optimal entry method depending on the nature of the date to be entered.
doc.datepicker_choice_picker_when: When it's necessary to select while checking the day of the week or availability (e.g., reservation date, event date).
doc.datepicker_clear_btn_desc: Optionally display a button to instantly clear the selected date.
doc.datepicker_content_format: Display the appropriate date format (YYYY/MM/DD, etc.) for the user's locale and communicate entry examples through placeholders.
doc.datepicker_control_types_desc: DatePicker supports both controlled and uncontrolled patterns.
doc.datepicker_custom_format_desc: Control the display format in the input field using the format property.
doc.datepicker_custom_popup_desc: Customize the content of the calendar popup using available slots.
doc.datepicker_design_intent: DatePicker is a component designed to allow users to intuitively select dates through a calendar-format UI. By being able to see the sense of the day of the week and specific periods (yesterday, tomorrow, etc.) while selecting, it prevents entry errors and reduces the user's memory load.
doc.datepicker_flow_1: Click the first time to select the start date.
doc.datepicker_flow_2: Click the second time to select the end date.
doc.datepicker_flow_3: The range between the start and end dates is highlighted during selection.
doc.datepicker_flow_4: If a date earlier than the start date is selected as the end date, they are automatically swapped.
doc.datepicker_guideline_1: Use when users need to select a specific date or ranges with visual calendar confirmation.
doc.datepicker_guideline_2: For dates users know by heart (e.g., birth dates, expiry dates), direct text input is often more efficient.
doc.datepicker_integration_desc: DatePicker utilizes the shared Calendar component internally. See the Calendar documentation for more details.
doc.datepicker_kb_1: Press Enter or Space on the input field to open the calendar.
doc.datepicker_kb_2: Navigate through dates with arrow keys and press Enter to select.
doc.datepicker_kb_3: Close the calendar anytime by pressing the Escape key.
doc.datepicker_long_desc: Details and usage for the Date Picker component.
doc.datepicker_ts_desc: The DatePicker component provides comprehensive type definitions for safe usage.
doc.daterangepicker_a11y_desc: Both start and end date inputs are keyboard-accessible. The calendar popup announces the selected range via aria-live updates.
doc.daterangepicker_best_practice_1: Show a visual preview of the selected range between start and end dates in the calendar.
doc.daterangepicker_best_practice_2: Validate that the end date is not before the start date and provide clear error feedback.
doc.daterangepicker_choice_alt_when: When only a single date is needed (use DatePicker instead).
doc.daterangepicker_choice_matrix_desc: Select based on the type of date selection needed.
doc.daterangepicker_choice_self_when: When users need to select a start and end date as a range (e.g., booking dates, report periods).
doc.daterangepicker_long_desc: Detailed information and usage instructions for the daterangepicker component.
doc.daterangepicker_title: A component for selecting a specific date range (start and end dates).
doc.inputmask_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.inputmask_anatomy_content: The text field that dynamically formats the content as the user types.
doc.inputmask_anatomy_root: The container that manages the masking logic and ensures the input follows the defined pattern.
doc.inputmask_basic_desc: Specify a pattern in the mask property.
doc.inputmask_best_practice_1: Use InputMask consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.inputmask_best_practice_2: Test InputMask behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.inputmask_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like Input better suits the use case.
doc.inputmask_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.inputmask_choice_self_when: When InputMask functionality with standard options is required.
doc.inputmask_design_intent: InputMask enforces a specific character format (such as phone numbers, CCs, or dates) during entry, reducing user error and ensuring high data quality without manual formatting.
doc.inputmask_long_desc: An input component with a mask to enforce input following a specific format.
doc.inputmask_scenario_1: Financial Entry: Enforcing a 16-digit pattern with spaces for credit card numbers.
doc.inputmask_scenario_2: Contact Info: Formatting phone numbers (e.g., (999) 999-9999) as the user types.
doc.numberinput_a11y_stepper: Assign appropriate aria-labels to the spin buttons so their function can be understood by screen readers.
doc.numberinput_anatomy_input: An <input> element that accepts only numerical values.
doc.numberinput_anatomy_steppers: Up and down buttons for increasing or decreasing the value by a certain amount.
doc.numberinput_best_practice_1: Always define min, max, and step to prevent invalid out-of-range values and to convey the expected input range to the user.
doc.numberinput_best_practice_2: Display a unit label (e.g., 'kg', '%', '$') adjacent to the field so users understand the expected value format without guessing.
doc.numberinput_choice_matrix_desc: Select according to the nature of the value to be entered and the frequency of adjustment.
doc.numberinput_choice_number_when: When continuous increment/decrement operations of numerical values such as quantity, age, or price are expected.
doc.numberinput_choice_slider_when: When intuitive proportions or sensory adjustments within a range are prioritized over precise numerical values.
doc.numberinput_choice_text_when: For 'numbers' with a strong symbolic meaning, such as phone numbers, credit card numbers, or zip codes (see [Numeric Input Standardization](./?path=/docs/standardization-numeric-input-standardization--docs)).
doc.numberinput_design_intent: NumberInput is a component specialized for entering and fine-tuning numerical values. In addition to users directly entering numbers using the keyboard, it provides a UI where values can be intuitively adjusted using spin buttons (increment/decrement buttons).
doc.numberinput_long_desc: A component that provides numerical input.
doc.numberinput_scenario_admin: Admin Panel: Specifying the sort order (priority) numerically.
doc.numberinput_scenario_cart: Shopping Cart: Changing the number of items ordered (quantity).
doc.numberinput_title: Field specialized for numeric input with spin buttons
doc.otpinput_a11y_desc: Each digit input is individually focusable with auto-advance. Supports paste for the full code. Uses aria-label to describe the purpose.
doc.otpinput_a11y_label: Communicate to screen readers that each field is requesting individual entry, and make them recognize it as an 'authentication code entry' as a whole group.
doc.otpinput_anatomy_fields: Input Field Sequence: A group of inputs dedicated to a single character, lined up for the specified number of digits.
doc.otpinput_best_practice_1: Auto-focus the first input field when the OTP screen loads to reduce friction.
doc.otpinput_best_practice_2: Support pasting the entire OTP code from clipboard to improve the user experience.
doc.otpinput_choice_alt_when: When the input is a general text field without specific digit-by-digit entry (use Input).
doc.otpinput_choice_matrix_desc: Select based on the type of code input needed.
doc.otpinput_choice_self_when: When verifying identity with a one-time passcode (SMS, email, or authenticator app).
doc.otpinput_content_auto: To enhance convenience on mobile devices, it supports automatic completion from SMS (autocomplete="one-time-code").
doc.otpinput_design_intent: OtpInput is a specialized component for entering short authentication codes (usually 4 to 6 digits) used in two-factor authentication, etc. By providing fields categorized for each character, it clarifies the current entry position and reduces entry errors by functioning as a visual guide.
doc.segmentedcontrol_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.segmentedcontrol_anatomy_content: The primary area where main content or children are rendered.
doc.segmentedcontrol_anatomy_root: The outermost container managing state and layout.
doc.segmentedcontrol_basic_desc: A set of buttons primarily used to toggle between different views or layout options.
doc.segmentedcontrol_best_practice_1: Use SegmentedControl consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.segmentedcontrol_best_practice_2: Test SegmentedControl behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.segmentedcontrol_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like Tabs better suits the use case.
doc.segmentedcontrol_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.segmentedcontrol_choice_self_when: When SegmentedControl functionality with standard options is required.
doc.segmentedcontrol_compare_desc: For detailed differentiation, refer to the Selection Controls Guide. It summarizes differences between SegmentedControl, Dropdown, Tabs, and Button Group, and provides criteria for choosing between them.
doc.segmentedcontrol_count_desc:
- Recommended: Keep to 2–5 items.
- Reason: To maintain a design where each item has sufficient width and is easy to tap even on mobile screens.
- If there are too many: For 6 or more items, or if labels have many characters (5+), consider the following:
- Dropdown
- Tab bar (scrollable tabs)
doc.segmentedcontrol_count_reason: To maintain a design where each item has sufficient width and is easy to tap even on mobile screens.
doc.segmentedcontrol_count_too_many: For 6 or more items, or if labels have many characters (5+), consider the following:
doc.segmentedcontrol_design_intent: SegmentedControl provides a consistent, reusable pattern for mutually exclusive toggle group for switching data views, reducing implementation effort and ensuring design system compliance.
doc.segmentedcontrol_ex_app_settings: Light Mode / Dark Mode / System Settings
doc.segmentedcontrol_ex_attr: Male / Female / Other, In Stock / All
doc.segmentedcontrol_ex_category: All / Replies / Mentions (notifications), All / Missed Calls (phone app)
doc.segmentedcontrol_ex_time: Day / Week / Month switch in calendar
doc.segmentedcontrol_guideline_desc:
All options must be visible at once.
Do not allow horizontal scrolling, such as when tab triggers do not fit on the screen.
doc.segmentedcontrol_icon_desc: Icons and labels can be used together, or only icons can be displayed.
doc.segmentedcontrol_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the segmented control. Arrow keys navigate between segments. The focused segment is automatically selected.
doc.segmentedcontrol_long_desc: Details and usage for the SegmentedControl component.
doc.segmentedcontrol_opt_desc: Text labels should be concise and clear nouns or noun phrases.
doc.segmentedcontrol_opt_lang_note: Multi-language support: Consider that character counts may change significantly when switching between languages.
doc.segmentedcontrol_p_space_desc: Suitable for limited screen sizes such as smartphones by saving space with icon-only displays.
doc.segmentedcontrol_p_state_desc: Each segment has an Active (selected) and Inactive (unselected) state.
doc.segmentedcontrol_p_struct_desc: Consists of at least two segments.
doc.segmentedcontrol_scenario_1: View Toggling: Switching between 'List', 'Grid', and 'Calendar' layouts in a task manager.
doc.segmentedcontrol_scenario_2: Filtering Options: Quickly refining results by 'Price', 'Popularity', or 'Newest' without a dropdown.
doc.segmentedcontrol_two_desc:
Also available for two choices (e.g., On/Off, Yes/No).
Ensure that the design clearly indicates which one is selected when there are only two choices.
doc.segmentedcontrol_u1_desc: Pattern where the entire page layout or presentation itself changes significantly.
doc.segmentedcontrol_u2_desc: Restricts the "type" of data displayed, serving a role similar to tab menus.
doc.segmentedcontrol_u3_desc: Changes the order of data. Useful for one-tap switching when choices are few enough that a dropdown isn’t necessary.
doc.segmentedcontrol_u4_desc: Determines the "state" for a specific item.
doc.otpinput_length_change_desc: Change the number of input fields with the length property.
doc.otpinput_long_desc: Split input fields for entering one-time passwords (OTP) or PIN codes.
doc.otpinput_scenario_auth: Entering codes during login or password reset.
doc.otpinput_scenario_pay: Entering security codes during high-value payments.
doc.phoneinput_a11y_desc: The country selector is implemented as a native <select> element with aria-label='Country code', ensuring compatibility with assistive technologies. The phone number input uses aria-labelledby to associate itself with the field label, and aria-invalid when an error is present.
doc.phoneinput_anatomy_country: Country Selector: A native select element overlaid on a flag + dial code preview. Allows the user to pick their country.
doc.phoneinput_anatomy_number: Phone Number Input: A tel-type input for entering the local phone number, excluding the country dial code.
doc.phoneinput_best_practice_1: Pre-select the country based on the user's locale or IP geolocation when possible.
doc.phoneinput_best_practice_2: Show a placeholder that matches the expected format for the selected country (e.g., 090-0000-0000 for Japan).
doc.phoneinput_best_practice_3: Validate on submit rather than on every keystroke to avoid frustrating the user during entry.
doc.phoneinput_choice_input_when: When the phone format is always from a single country and no country selection is needed.
doc.phoneinput_choice_inputmask_when: When you need format enforcement (e.g., (99) 9999-9999) without a country selector.
doc.phoneinput_choice_matrix_desc: Choose based on whether international phone number entry is required.
doc.phoneinput_choice_phoneinput_when: When users need to enter an international phone number with country code selection.
doc.phoneinput_design_intent: PhoneInput combines a country code selector with a phone number field into a single cohesive input. It solves the common UX problem of collecting international phone numbers by letting users pick their country — displaying the flag and dial code — without needing to manually type the country code.
doc.phoneinput_long_desc: Composite input for international phone numbers with a country dial code selector.
doc.phoneinput_scenario_checkout: E-commerce Checkout: Collecting a shipping contact number that may be from any country.
doc.phoneinput_scenario_signup: User Registration: Collecting a mobile number for SMS verification during international sign-up.
doc.rangecalendar_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.rangecalendar_anatomy_content: The primary area where main content or children are rendered.
doc.rangecalendar_anatomy_root: The outermost container managing state and layout.
doc.rangecalendar_best_practice_1: Use RangeCalendar consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.rangecalendar_best_practice_2: Test RangeCalendar behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.rangecalendar_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like DateRangePicker better suits the use case.
doc.rangecalendar_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.rangecalendar_choice_self_when: When RangeCalendar functionality with standard options is required.
doc.rangecalendar_design_intent: RangeCalendar provides a consistent, reusable pattern for standalone calendar for selecting a date range without text input, reducing implementation effort and ensuring design system compliance.
doc.rangecalendar_scenario_1: Vacation Planning: Selecting a continuous block of dates for a flight and hotel stay.
doc.rangecalendar_scenario_2: Analytics Filtering: Choosing a custom start and end date to filter a performance dashboard.
doc.rangeslider_a11y_desc: Both thumbs are keyboard-navigable with arrow keys. Each thumb has aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax, and aria-valuenow attributes.
doc.rangeslider_best_practice_1: Display the current min and max values near the thumbs or in adjacent inputs for precise control.
doc.rangeslider_best_practice_2: Prevent thumbs from crossing each other to maintain intuitive min-max semantics.
doc.rangeslider_choice_alt_when: When only a single numeric value is needed (use Slider).
doc.rangeslider_choice_matrix_desc: Select based on whether a range or single value is needed.
doc.rangeslider_choice_self_when: When users need to define a numeric range (e.g., price range, date range).
doc.rangeslider_long_desc: A slider component for selecting a range (start and end).
doc.slider_a11y_desc: The thumb is keyboard-navigable with arrow keys. Uses role='slider' with aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax, and aria-valuenow.
doc.slider_a11y_keyboard: Ensure values can be increased or decreased by fixed amounts using the left/right (up/down) arrow keys.
doc.slider_anatomy_thumb: A circular handle that the user drags to change the value.
doc.slider_anatomy_track: A line indicating the range of value movement. Colors are separated between selected and unselected ranges.
doc.slider_basic_desc: Standard implementation for selecting a single numeric value from a range.
doc.slider_best_practice_1: Display the current value near the thumb or in a tooltip for precise feedback.
doc.slider_best_practice_2: Define appropriate step sizes to balance precision with ease of use.
doc.slider_choice_matrix_desc: Select according to the nature of the value being selected and the operational precision expected by the user.
doc.slider_choice_number_when: When you want to specify a concrete numerical value precisely in single units, such as age or quantity.
doc.slider_choice_slider_when: When sensory adjustment is more suitable than strict numerical values, such as volume, brightness, or price range.
doc.slider_content_labels: Display labels for the minimum and maximum values to clarify what is being adjusted.
doc.slider_custom_marks_desc: Labels and tick marks can be displayed at specific values using the `marks` property.
doc.slider_desc: An input to capture a numeric value from a specified range by dragging a knob
doc.slider_design_intent: Sliders are components for selecting a numerical value between a minimum and maximum value through intuitive drag operations. They are ideal when 'relative position' within a range or 'sensory adjustment' is prioritized over precise numerical input.
doc.slider_long_desc: Details and usage for the Slider component.
doc.slider_range_desc: Use multiple knobs to specify a range of start and end values.
doc.slider_scenario_filter: Narrowing down a specific price range from a product list.
doc.slider_step_desc: Restrict the numeric increment (step size) using the `step` property.
doc.slider_title: Input to capture a numeric value from a specified range by dragging a knob
doc.slider_usage_desc: Select a numeric value intuitively from the set range by dragging the knob.
doc.slider_vertical_desc: Align the slider vertically using the `vertical` property.
doc.timepicker_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.timepicker_anatomy_content: The primary area where main content or children are rendered.
doc.timepicker_anatomy_root: The outermost container managing state and layout.
doc.timepicker_best_practice_1: Use TimePicker consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.timepicker_best_practice_2: Test TimePicker behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.timepicker_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like DatePicker better suits the use case.
doc.timepicker_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.timepicker_choice_self_when: When TimePicker functionality with standard options is required.
doc.timepicker_desc: A component for users to select time. It wraps the native <input type="time"> and adjusts the styling.
doc.timepicker_design_intent: TimePicker provides a consistent, reusable pattern for time selection input with hour and minute controls, reducing implementation effort and ensuring design system compliance.
doc.timepicker_scenario_1: Shift Management: Setting the start and end times for employee work shifts.
doc.timepicker_scenario_2: Alarms & Reminders: Choosing a specific trigger time for system notifications.
doc.timepicker_title: A specialized input for selecting specific hours and minutes
doc.daterangepicker_scenario_booking: Selecting check-in/check-out dates or reservation periods.
doc.daterangepicker_scenario_report: Defining report date ranges for analytics or data exports.
doc.colorinput_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the color input field. Standard keyboard input is supported for hex values. Escape cancels editing.
doc.colorpicker_keyboard_desc: Tab moves focus within the color picker. Arrow keys adjust hue and saturation values. Escape closes the picker.
doc.datepicker_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the date input field. Arrow keys navigate the calendar. Enter selects a date. Escape closes the calendar.
doc.daterangepicker_keyboard_desc: Tab moves between start and end date fields. Arrow keys navigate the calendar. Enter selects dates. Escape closes the calendar.
doc.inputmask_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the masked input field. Standard keyboard input is supported within the mask pattern. Escape cancels where applicable.
doc.rangeslider_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses each slider thumb. Arrow keys adjust the value. Home and End move to min and max values respectively.
doc.slider_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the slider thumb. Arrow keys adjust the value incrementally. Home and End move to min and max values.
doc.timepicker_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the time input field. Arrow keys adjust hours and minutes. Escape closes the time picker panel.
doc.numberinput_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the input. Arrow Up increments the value; Arrow Down decrements it. Home moves to the minimum value; End moves to the maximum. Standard keyboard input is also supported.
doc.otpinput_keyboard_desc: Each digit field is individually focusable. Tab moves between fields. After entering a digit, focus advances automatically to the next field. Backspace clears the current field and moves focus back.
doc.phoneinput_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the country code selector first, then the phone number input. Arrow keys navigate country options in the dropdown. Standard keyboard input is supported in the number field.

guide.lvb_a11y_keyboard_screenreader: The use of the correct tag conveys the appropriate interaction method (Enter key vs Space) to users who rely on assistive technologies like screen readers.
guide.lvb_a11y_rightclick_desc: `<a>` allows 'Open in new tab,' but `<button>` does not.
guide.lvb_anchor_example: 'Proceed to Checkout', 'Read More', 'Sign Up Here (External Site)'
guide.lvb_antipattern_text: Avoid placing JS logic into `<a>` via onclick, or using window.location.href in `<button>` for navigation.
guide.lvb_confusion_submit_text: For form submission buttons (e.g., 'Submit', 'Save'), `<button type="submit">` is the best practice. It clearly defines the 'send data' intent and is announced correctly by screen readers.
guide.lvb_criteria_text: If the URL (address bar) changes after clicking, use `<a>`. If something is completed on the spot, use `<button>`.
guide.lvb_desc: Even if they look like the same 'button', HTML tags (`<a>` or `<button>`) should be used correctly according to their function and purpose.
guide.lvb_standard_text: Using `<a>` for page transitions and `<button>` for data submission or state changes is the correct approach in Web Standards, benefiting both accessibility and SEO.
guide.lvb_summary_text:
Want to go to another URL? → `<a>` 
Want to submit a form or change something? → `<button>`
guide.lvb_table_behavior_a: Navigates to the URL in href
guide.lvb_table_judgment_b: Task is completed on the spot
guide.lvb_table_scene_a: Go to detail page, Go to external site
guide.lvb_table_scene_b: Add to cart, Submit form, Open modal

loading.location_center: Screen center or covering a container
loading.location_inline: Inside buttons, next to text, or small areas
loading.purpose_data_fetching: Waiting for data loading or heavy processing
loading.spinner_vs_loader_desc: Both indicate a loading state, but their roles and display areas are different.

table.op_arrow: Move focus between items (Tabs, Radio Groups, etc.)
table.op_enter: Select or activate the focused item
table.op_escape: Close overlays or cancel the current action
table.op_page_up_down: Scroll or move between large units
table.op_space: Select or toggle the focused item
table.op_tab: Move focus to the next / previous interactive element

foundation.a11y_desc: WIM UI puts accessibility at the core of its design to provide an interface that is easy for everyone to use.
foundation.wcag_aa_desc: Maintains a contrast ratio of at least 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text.
foundation.semantic_tokens_desc: By using semantic tokens defined in the color system, contrast ratios are automatically ensured in both light and dark modes.
foundation.automated_checks_desc: Automated testing with `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y` and `axe-core` is integrated into the pipeline.
foundation.focus_mgmt_desc: Proper focus indicators are essential for keyboard users.
foundation.focus_ring_desc: A high-visibility focus ring (`--wim-shadow-focus`) is applied to all interactive elements.
foundation.offset_desc: Proper distance (`--wim-focus-outline-offset`) is maintained between the element and the focus ring to improve visibility without compromising design aesthetics.
foundation.focus_trap_desc: For overlays such as modals, drawers, and popovers, a Focus Trap feature is implemented to keep focus within the element.
foundation.keyboard_nav_desc: WIM UI components are fully operable without a mouse.
foundation.wai_aria_patterns_desc: Complex components such as tabs, radio buttons, and accordions implement keyboard interactions based on W3C's WAI-ARIA Authoring Practices.
foundation.roving_tabindex_desc: Supports smooth item movement using arrow keys.
foundation.reduced_motion_desc: Respects the OS 'Reduce Motion' setting and disables or simplifies unnecessary animations (support for `prefers-reduced-motion` media query).
foundation.test_maintenance_desc: Regularly run the following command to maintain accessibility.

doc.prompt_input_usage: Auto-resizing input for AI prompts. Includes send/attach buttons, handles Enter for send and Shift+Enter for newline.
doc.smart_search_input_usage: Input field that seamlessly expands from a standard search bar to an AI prompt. Supports transition from single-line search to multi-line dialogue.
doc.streaming_text_usage: Real-time Markdown rendering for LLM generated text. Includes a blinking cursor during streaming and aria-live notifications.
doc.thought_process_usage: Visualizes AI reasoning steps in a timeline. Features collapsible containers showing step status (running, completed, error).
doc.ai_patterns_desc: Combine `PromptInput` and `StreamingText` to build simple AI chat interfaces.
doc.ai_best_practices_loading: Set `loading={true}` on `PromptInput` while AI is generating a response to prevent duplicate submissions.
doc.ai_best_practices_streaming: Switch `isStreaming={false}` on `StreamingText` after completion to hide the cursor and stop `aria-live` updates.
doc.ai_best_practices_error: Display error messages in `StreamingText` content or use a separate `Alert` component when errors occur.

guide.colors_border_desc: Used to show element boundaries or separators.
guide.colors_contrast_checker_desc: You can check if background and text color combinations meet accessibility standards.
guide.colors_contrast_text_desc: Colors for text and icons on semantic fills (`text-on-*`). Use `text-on-disabled` only on `--wim-color-disabled` backgrounds.
guide.colors_customization_desc: If you want to change or add color schemes, edit the following files:
guide.colors_customization_pccs_desc: Defines specific color codes based on hue and tone (e.g., $pccs-v1).
guide.colors_customization_semantic_desc: Defines colors for specific purposes (Primary, Destructive, etc.) and dark mode color schemes.
guide.colors_desc: A guide to the colors used in the WIM UI design system. This system is designed based on PCCS (Practical Color Co-ordinate System) for consistent color design.
guide.colors_pccs_desc: WIM UI internally maintains a PCCS color palette, allowing for intuitive color selection based on tones.
guide.colors_pccs_file_link: Refer to src/tokens/_pccs-colors.scss and _semantic-colors.scss for detailed color codes.
guide.colors_pccs_mapping_desc: WIM UI manages colors as SCSS variables using PCCS notation (e.g., $pccs-v1, $pccs-gy8-5) and assigns them to semantic CSS variables.
guide.colors_scrollbar_desc: Colors used for scrollbars, such as in the ScrollArea component.
guide.colors_semantic_desc: Colors defined based on use or meaning, used to indicate state or role.
guide.colors_surface_desc: Colors used for application backgrounds and component surfaces, switching automatically in dark mode.
guide.colors_text_desc: Text on normal surfaces. `text-disabled` is for muted/disabled copy here — not for text on a disabled fill (use `text-on-disabled`).
guide.pccs_contrast_desc: You can check if PCCS color combinations meet accessibility standards.
guide.pccs_customization_desc: If you want to change specific color codes in the PCCS palette, edit the following file:
guide.pccs_customization_note: * Changing this file will update semantic colors (Primary, Success, etc.) and component colors that reference these colors all at once.
guide.pccs_desc: A list of the PCCS color palette, which forms the basis of WIM UI's color design. Categorized by tone (combination of lightness and saturation) to support intuitive color design.
guide.colors_special_styles_desc: Used for specialized visual effects such as semi-transparency and placeholder states.
guide.colors_interaction_desc: Colors for interactive states and overlay elements.
guide.colors_component_specific_desc: Private component colors (`--wim-comp-*`). Shipped in `styles.css` but not part of the public theme API — do not override for branding; use role tokens (`primary`, `surface*`, …) instead.

cat.ai_desc: Components for building AI-powered chat interfaces and visualizing generative AI output.
cat.advanced_inputs_desc: Input components for complex data formats or special interactions.
cat.alerts_desc: Components for communicating important information or feedback to users.
cat.app_shell_desc: Core structural components that define the application's top-level layout and identity.
cat.basic_inputs_desc: Components for basic text and numeric input.
cat.buttons_desc: Fundamental components for triggering actions and navigation.
cat.data_containers_desc: Components designed to encapsulate and organize content within distinct boundaries.
cat.data_indicators_desc: Components for visually communicating data status or information.
cat.data_structures_desc: Components for displaying large volumes of data in structured and readable formats.
cat.form_layout_desc: Auxiliary components for structuring, labeling, and organizing form fields.
cat.internal_desc: Internal building blocks used to construct higher-level public components.
cat.layout_desc: Foundational components for controlling the positioning and spacing of elements.
cat.loading_desc: Visual indicators to inform users about background processes and data loading states.
cat.media_desc: Components for embedding and controlling visual and auditory media content.
cat.nav_elements_desc: Components that define the application structure and assist in navigation.
cat.nav_utilities_desc: Helper components that provide additional navigation-related functionality like scroll-to-top.
cat.overlays_desc: Temporary UI elements that appear over the main content for focused interaction or information.
cat.pickers_desc: Interactive components for selecting values from ranges, dates, or color palettes.
cat.selection_desc: Form controls for making choices among multiple options, such as checkboxes and switches.
cat.typography_desc: Foundational components for consistent text styling, hierarchy, and iconic representation.
cat.utilities_desc: A collection of miscellaneous helper components for scrolling, error handling, and more.
cat.visualization_desc: Components for translating complex data sets into intuitive and interactive charts.

doc.tokens_desc: The component uses predefined design tokens for colors, spacing, and typography to ensure visual consistency.
doc.choice_alt_desc: Use a simpler native element or a different component when the full feature set is not needed.
doc.global_standards_desc: For core principles, design philosophy, and base accessibility specs, refer to Philosophy.

guide.refer_to_component_pages: Refer to specific component pages for detail.

rule.overload_dont_desc: Overloading with many complex rules (e.g., '8+ chars, with symbols')

a11y.guideline_desc: Design for accessibility to ensure all users can effectively use the interface.

critical.info_only_in_p_desc: Providing critical information only in the placeholder

guide.action_std_concept_desc: Ensures consistent visual feedback and property naming conventions across different components to improve development efficiency and usability.
guide.action_std_desc: Defines common rules for components that trigger user actions, such as buttons and links.
guide.action_std_note_desc: In specific contexts (e.g., Floating Action Buttons), fixed sizes other than the standard ones may be used.
guide.action_std_rule_1_desc: Manage dimensions using `sm`, `md`, and `lg` (prop name is `size`).
guide.action_std_rule_2_desc: Use Primary (High), Secondary (Medium), and Tertiary/Ghost (Low) for visual weight.
guide.action_std_rule_3_desc: Display a spinner during processing and disable interaction to prevent double submissions.
guide.action_std_rule_4_desc: Always provide an `aria-label` for icon-only buttons to support screen readers.
guide.feedback_std_concept_desc: Unifies colors and icons according to visual intent (Intent) to ensure users can instantly understand the importance of information.
guide.feedback_std_desc: Defines common rules for components that communicate system information to users, such as alerts and toasts.
guide.feedback_std_note_desc: Choose between Toast (temporary) and Alert (persistent) based on the message length and urgency.
guide.feedback_std_rule_2_desc: Uses the same icons for the same variants across all feedback components.
guide.feedback_std_rule_3_desc: Standardizes property names for titles (`title`) and descriptions (`description`).
guide.feedback_std_rule_4_desc: Provides an `onClose` property to allow users to explicitly close unnecessary information.
guide.nav_std_concept_desc: Unifies the visual representation of active states, allowing users to intuitively grasp their current location.
guide.nav_std_desc: Defines common rules for components that assist user movement and switching, such as tabs and pagination.
guide.nav_std_note_desc: Use 'Tabs' for switching major features, 'SegmentedControl' for auxiliary choices, and 'Pagination' for page navigation.
guide.nav_std_rule_1: Active Indication: Use a sliding indicator (moving bar) to achieve smooth state transitions.
guide.nav_std_rule_1_desc: Use sliding indicators (moving bars) for smooth state transitions.
guide.nav_std_rule_2: Keyboard Navigation: Supports item movement with arrow keys to ensure accessibility.
guide.nav_std_rule_2_desc: Support item movement via arrow keys to ensure accessibility.
guide.nav_std_rule_3: Responsive Support: Properly handles scrolling or collapsing based on screen width to maintain usability.
guide.nav_std_rule_3_desc: Appropriately handle scrolling or folding based on screen width to maintain usability.
guide.nav_std_rule_4: Consistent Interaction: Unifies feedback for hovers and clicks across all navigation elements.
guide.nav_std_rule_4_desc: Standardize hover and click feedback across all navigation elements.
guide.overlay_std_concept_desc: Provides a UI that allows users to complete tasks without hesitation by choosing the appropriate layering method according to information priority and contextual continuity.
guide.overlay_std_desc: Defines common rules for components displayed on top of the current context, such as dialogs and drawers.
guide.overlay_std_note_desc: Use 'Dialog' for full-screen focus, 'Popover' for supplementary information, and 'BottomSheet' for mobile selection.
guide.overlay_std_rule_1_desc: Divided into parts like `Root`, `Trigger`, and `Content` for flexible layout and logical structure.
guide.overlay_std_rule_2_desc: Declare and control open/close states using the `open` and `onOpenChange` properties.
guide.overlay_std_rule_3_desc: Ensure consistency in behaviors such as closing on background click or Escape key, focus trapping, and preventing background scrolling.
guide.overlay_std_rule_4_desc: Comply with the WAI-ARIA Modal pattern, using appropriate roles (`dialog`) and labeling (`aria-labelledby`).

button.consistency_desc: Always use the same priority level for the same type of action.
button.copy_usage: Best for accurately saving strings like IDs or URLs to the clipboard with one click.
button.group_usage: Best for presenting related operations together, such as 'Back/Next' or 'Edit/Save'.
button.guide_desc: Buttons that prompt user action should use visual weighting according to their importance and role.
button.icon_usage: Best for toolbars or cards where space is limited and intuitive operation is desired.
button.placement_conflict_desc: Keep only one Primary button per screen (or modal) in principle.
button.placement_desc: Place primary actions at the end of the common eye-tracking path (e.g., bottom right).
button.priority_danger_usage: Destructive actions that cannot be undone after execution, such as delete or reset.
button.priority_high_usage: The most important 'Primary Action' on the screen. Ideally only one per screen.
button.priority_low_usage: For supplementary operations or when many options need to be listed.
button.priority_medium_usage: Secondary actions that support the primary one. (Cancel, Edit, Back, etc.)
button.priority_weighting: When multiple buttons are on the same screen, use visual weighting to prevent user confusion.
button.semantics_desc: To maintain semantics and accessibility, choose buttons based on 'purpose' rather than just appearance.
button.semantics_guide_ref: For detailed criteria, please refer to the specific guide.
button.standard_usage: Most versatile action. Best when you need to convey intent clearly with text.

guide.hierarchy_desc: Visualizing the layers of components and how they are composed to maintain a healthy architecture.
guide.hierarchy_rules_desc: Design rules for maintaining healthy dependencies in WIM UI.
guide.hierarchy_tiers_desc: WIM UI is designed with four tiers based on component complexity and role. This keeps dependencies unidirectional (top-down) and improves maintainability.
guide.composition_map_desc: Mapping of which components major components use (wrap) internally. By combining lower-tier components, we provide consistent functionality.
guide.principles_desc: In WIM UI, we follow these principles to maintain consistency in DOM management and motion.
guide.input_std_desc: Standardized behavior and layout rules for input areas to ensure consistency across form components.

guide.title: CSS Strategy & Architecture
guide.desc: WIM UI adopts modern CSS techniques to achieve high maintainability and collision-free styling.
guide.sass_desc: Powerful features like nesting, variables, and mixins.
guide.layers_desc: WIM UI uses layers to clarify CSS priority.
guide.desc_general: Basic elements such as Button, Icon, InputBase.
guide.desc_complex: Higher-level components such as Snackbar, List.
guide.layers_benefit: Benefit: Non-layer styles always take precedence over styles within layers, allowing base component styles to be overridden without using `!important`.
guide.external_access_rule: The root element of a component is given a `:global(.wim-[ComponentName])` class to allow users to override styles externally.
guide.method_tokens_usage: Adjust themes by overriding CSS variables whenever possible.
guide.method_classname_usage: Styles can be injected externally through each component's `className` prop.
guide.method_global_usage: Target `:global` classes for global adjustments at the application level.
guide.public_css_desc: Published package paths. Changing these breaks consumers.
guide.public_css_styles: `wimui/styles.css` (required) — `:root` `--wim-*` (dark + density from `_ui-patterns.scss`) plus component CSS. Does not include reset.
guide.public_css_reset: `wimui/reset.css` (optional) — opinionated reset/base; omit if it conflicts with the host app.
guide.public_css_attrs: Document attributes (stable names): `data-theme` and `data-density` on `<html>` by default. See Token → Theme and Token → Density.

chart.guide_area_desc: Suitable for showing the magnitude of change over time and emphasizing the total volume.
chart.guide_bar_desc: Best for comparing values across different categories.
chart.guide_desc: A guide on how to choose the right chart based on your data and the message you want to convey.
chart.guide_funnel_desc: Visualizes gradual reduction in a process and conversion rates.
chart.guide_gauge_desc: Provides an intuitive display of current progress against a single numerical goal.
chart.guide_heatmap_desc: Represents the density of values across two axes (matrix) using colors.
chart.guide_line_desc: Used to show trends or changes over time.
chart.guide_pie_desc: Used to show parts of a whole (shares). Recommended for 5 categories or fewer.
chart.guide_radar_desc: Best for comparing data across multiple dimensions to see balance and characteristics.
chart.guide_scatter_desc: Used to identify correlations or distributions between two variables.
chart.guide_treemap_desc: Represents proportions of hierarchical data using varying area sizes.

guide.display_std_concept_desc: Visually indicates the relevance of information and provides a structure that makes complex data easy to read and scan.
guide.display_std_desc: Defines common rules for components used to organize and present information, such as Cards and DescriptionLists.
guide.display_std_note_desc: Use 'Card' for independent chunks of information, 'DescriptionList' for listing settings or attributes, and 'List' for simple enumerations of information.
guide.display_std_rule_1_desc: Unify definitions for Card variants (Elevated, Outline, Flat), border radius (Radius), and padding (Padding).
guide.display_std_rule_2_desc: Compose by dividing into sections such as `Header` (Title), `Body` (Details), and `Footer` (Actions).
guide.display_std_rule_3_desc: In DescriptionLists, clarify the weighting of font sizes and colors for item names (Labels) and content (Values) to enhance visibility.
guide.display_std_rule_4_desc: Provide appropriate alignments, such as list or grid formats, depending on the volume and nature of the data.
guide.indicator_std_concept_desc: Helps users visually organize information by selecting appropriate components based on information type and presence of interaction.
guide.indicator_std_desc: Defines common rules for components that supplement information attributes or states, such as badges, tags, and chips.
guide.indicator_std_note_desc: Use 'Badge' for numerical counts, 'Tag' for information classification, and 'Chip' for interactive choices or removable elements.
guide.indicator_std_rule_1: Sizing: Based on two sizes: `small` (sm) and `medium` (md) to ensure consistent dimensions.
guide.indicator_std_rule_1_desc: Use a consistent color palette (primary, positive, caution, destructive, informative) to convey status across all indicators.
guide.indicator_std_rule_2: Color Palette: Unifies semantic colors (Success, Warning, Error, etc.) to ensure consistent meaning of information.
guide.indicator_std_rule_2_desc: All indicator components (Badge, Tag, etc.) must support standard sizes (sm, md) for consistent visual weight.
guide.indicator_std_rule_3: Variant Unification: Supports `solid`, `outline`, and `subtle` appearances to distinguish information priority.
guide.indicator_std_rule_3_desc: Variants (solid, outline, soft) should be used to distinguish between different levels of information importance.
guide.indicator_std_rule_4: Accessibility: When using icons, combine them with label text or provide appropriate Aria attributes.
guide.indicator_std_rule_4_desc: When using icons, combine them with label text or provide appropriate Aria attributes.
guide.table_std_concept_desc: Organizes and presents large amounts of information, enabling users to efficiently compare data, identify specific items, and perform operations (edit, delete, etc.).
guide.table_std_desc: Defines common rules for components that list structured data, such as Table and DataGrid.
guide.table_std_note_desc: Use 'Table' for flexible layouts or static data, and 'DataGrid' when large data manipulation or complex filtering is required.
guide.table_std_rule_1: Unified Visual Style: Allow consistent switching of stripes, borders, and hover emphasis via properties.
guide.table_std_rule_1_desc: Consistently toggle styles like striped rows, borders, and hover effects through properties.
guide.table_std_rule_2: Header Functionality: Standardize sticky headers and click-to-sort functionality to ensure users do not lose track of information location.
guide.table_std_rule_2_desc: Standardize sticky headers and click-to-sort functionality to ensure users don't lose track of information location.
guide.table_std_rule_3: Responsive Design: Support switching to `mobileCard` mode for mobile browsing to maintain readability on small screens.
guide.table_std_rule_3_desc: Support switching to `mobileCard` mode for mobile browsing to maintain readability on small screens.
guide.table_std_rule_4: Interaction: Establish standards for row selection (selected state) and cell alignment (text left-aligned, numbers right-aligned, etc.).
guide.table_std_rule_4_desc: Establish standards for row selection (selected state) and cell alignment (text left-aligned, numbers right-aligned, etc.).

datastructure.chat_features: Dedicated chat components for message lists, inputs, avatars, etc. Easily build real-time dialogue UIs.
datastructure.chat_perf_note: `ChatUI` is suitable for real-time dialogue, but for large history displays, consider combining it with `InfiniteScroll` or using efficient data transfer like WebSockets.
datastructure.chat_usage: For support chats, AI chats, customer messaging screens.
datastructure.datagrid_features_desc: Provides rich spreadsheet-like features: virtualization (virtual scroll) for large datasets, column pinning, cell direct editing, etc.
datastructure.datagrid_usage: Screens needing fast scrolling through thousands to tens of thousands of records, or complex multi-functional data screens.
datastructure.desc_list_features: Elegantly formats and lists pairs of keys (item names) and values (details).
datastructure.desc_list_usage: User profile detail screens, product specification lists requiring responsive layout across screen widths.
datastructure.guide_desc: Organize and display large datasets, complex parent-child relationships, or time-series data.
datastructure.list_features: Simple vertical listing of items. Best for mobile-first layouts maintaining row-level independence.
datastructure.list_usage: Item lists on mobile devices, notification feeds, etc.
datastructure.semantics_selection: Choose based on the core semantics: `Table` or `DataGrid` for analysis, `TreeView` for hierarchy, `Timeline` for time series.
datastructure.stats_features: Emphasizes major numerical data (KPIs) visually while expressing trends like increases or decreases.
datastructure.stats_usage: Top display in analytics dashboards, highlighting key KPIs like daily revenue or new user count.
datastructure.table_features: Generate lightweight, simple tables. Ideal for data comparison, analysis, sorting, and filtering.
datastructure.table_usage: User lists, setting item lists, and views where the number of data records is limited.
datastructure.timeline_features: Visualizes sequential events along a timeline, such as update history or progress flow.
datastructure.timeline_usage: Product shipping status in e-commerce, workflow progress, system logs, or user activity logs.
datastructure.tree_features: Visual representation of hierarchical (parent-child) data with folding/unfolding capabilities, like directory structures.
datastructure.tree_usage: Directory structures like a file manager, organizational charts, category trees across multiple tiers.

guide.effects_common_vars_guideline: Prioritize using defined tokens such as var(--transition-base) or var(--easing-spring). This ensures visual consistency and motion quality across the entire library.
guide.effects_desc: Definitions for elevation (shadows) and motion (animations). They convey hierarchy and state changes to the user.
guide.effects_motion_desc: Duration and easing definitions to maintain consistent animation quality.
guide.effects_motion_guideline: Defines highly responsive motion. Hover and click interactions are ultra-fast (83ms-167ms), while entrances like dialogs feature natural deceleration (250ms-333ms). Prioritize using var(--transition-base) or specific easing tokens.
guide.effects_motion_out_back_desc: Adds emphasis to movements like button hovers by slightly overshooting before settling.
guide.effects_motion_spring_desc: Suitable for natural, elastic movements like opening/closing Accordions or Drawers.
guide.effects_shadow_ambient_desc: Soft, diffused shadow caused by ambient lighting environment. Provides stability and grounding.
guide.effects_shadow_elevation_desc: Sharper shadow caused by a specific light source. Emphasizes the height and separation of elements.
guide.effects_shadow_guideline: Utilizes a multi-layered design combining Ambient and Elevation lights. Choose the level of elevation based on element stacking order (z-index) and importance.
guide.effects_shadow_multi_layer_desc: By combining Ambient and Elevation layers, we achieve a more realistic depth that mimics real-world lighting.
guide.effects_opacity_desc: Opacity tokens for expressing UI states. Always reference these tokens instead of hardcoded values.
guide.effects_opacity_ghost: Ghost UI elements (close buttons, placeholder icons, etc.)
guide.effects_opacity_dim: Animation start/end states and passive visual decorations (loading dots, typing indicators)
guide.effects_opacity_subtle: In-progress or applying state — element is still interactive but visually de-emphasized
guide.effects_opacity_guideline: Use the five levels — disabled / ghost / secondary / dim / subtle — instead of hardcoded values (0.4–0.8).
guide.effects_interaction_bg_desc: When changing background colors in :hover or :active states, use CSS Color Level 4 oklch relative color syntax instead of opacity or filter: brightness(). This produces perceptually uniform lightness changes across both light and dark modes.
guide.effects_interaction_bg_rule_ng: NG — filter: brightness() or opacity alters all colors (bg, text, border) simultaneously and behaves differently in dark mode
guide.effects_interaction_bg_rule_ok: OK — oklch relative color adjusts only the L (lightness) channel, giving visually consistent results in any theme
guide.effects_interaction_bg_opacity_note: opacity may only be used for visibility toggles (opacity: 0 → 1). The disabled state may continue to use opacity tokens (--wim-opacity-disabled etc.).
guide.effects_interaction_bg_multivariant_desc: When the background color varies by variant, store it in a local CSS variable (--bg) and reference it in the hover rule.
guide.effects_interaction_bg_guideline: Use oklch(from var(--token) calc(l * 0.9) c h) for darkening, calc(l * 1.1) for lightening. Store dynamic backgrounds in a --bg local variable.
guide.effects_semantic_aliases_desc: Do not use value-based scale tokens directly in components. Use the following role-based aliases instead.

perf.animation_desc: For components with continuous or complex animations, use the `will-change` CSS property to prompt browser optimization.
perf.animation_micro_interactions_desc: Applied to small operations like switch toggles or accordion expansions to achieve an immediate, tangible feel.
perf.animation_note_desc: Use sparingly as it consumes memory and GPU resources. Avoid applying to many elements simultaneously.

guide.input_std_concept_desc: In WIM UI, we have unified the structure of the "right icon area" for all input and selection components. This ensures a consistent user experience without layout breakage, even when clear buttons, dropdown icons, and validation icons coexist.
guide.input_std_desc: Guidelines for standardized icon placement rules and the `allowClear` functionality in input fields and various picker components.
guide.input_std_note_desc: ColorPicker does not support `allowClear` as an exception, because it triggers the browser's native color picker due to its `type="color"` nature.
guide.input_std_rule_1: To prevent icon overlap, the right icon area is managed via Flexbox, allowing multiple icons (clear, dropdown, others) to be displayed in parallel.
guide.input_std_rule_1_desc: To prevent icon overlap, the right icon area is managed with Flexbox, displaying multiple icons (Clear, Dropdown, Others) in parallel.
guide.input_std_rule_2: When allowClear is enabled, the 'x' button is displayed only when a value exists, allowing the value to be reset on click.
guide.input_std_rule_2_desc: When `allowClear` is enabled, the "X" button is displayed only when a value exists, allowing the value to be reset on click.
guide.input_std_rule_3: For elements with dropdowns like Selectes, the chevron icon is rotated 180 degrees based on the open/closed state to enhance visual feedback.
guide.input_std_rule_3_desc: For elements with dropdowns like Selectes, the chevron icon is rotated 180 degrees according to the open/closed state to enhance visual feedback.
guide.input_std_rule_4: Each picker (Time, Color, Date, etc.) is built based on Tier 2 Input components whenever possible, inheriting basic features.
guide.input_std_rule_4_desc: Each picker (Time, Color, Date, etc.) is built based on the Tier 2 Input component as much as possible to inherit basic features.
guide.input_std_width_desc: The width of input components is optimized based on the nature of information and readability.
guide.input_std_width_fluid_desc: For AI prompts and long text notes, using `fullWidth` to provide a wider view is effective for information overview. However, as readability decreases when a single line is too long (e.g., more than 80 characters), it is recommended to limit the maximum width at the layout level.
guide.input_std_width_standard_desc: For items like names and email addresses, it is recommended to limit the width to approximately `max-width: 20rem` (320px). This reduces eye movement, improves readability, and prevents input errors.
guide.rvc_desc: Guidelines for proper usage and differences between Radio, Checkbox, and Switch.
guide.rvc_design_checkbox: Square (■) with a checkmark (✔) when selected.
guide.rvc_design_radio: Circular (●) with a filled center when selected.
guide.rvc_design_switch: Capsule shape with a knob that slides to indicate On/Off.
guide.rvc_note_default: Radio buttons should have a default (e.g., standard shipping). However, leave unselected for surveys.
guide.rvc_note_vertical: Stack options vertically and make labels clickable (improved accessibility).
guide.rvc_selection_switch: Toggle between two states (On/Off). Independent setting.
guide.rvc_timing_checkbox: Requires Confirmation: Since multiple items are selected, an 'Apply' button flow is common.
guide.rvc_timing_radio: Immediate: Selecting one often triggers immediate setting changes or navigation.
guide.rvc_usage_checkbox: Checkbox Use Cases: Filters (Color/Size), Notifications (News/Updates), Terms agreement
guide.rvc_usage_radio: Radio Use Cases: Payment method (Credit/Bank), Sort order (Price/Newest), Delivery time
guide.rvc_usage_switch: Switch Use Cases: Enabling features, Toggling modes (e.g. Dark Mode). Immediate effects.
guide.rvc_vs_switch_checkbox: Switch for immediate effect. Checkbox if a save button is needed.
guide.rvc_vs_switch_radio: Radio for 3+ choices. Switch for 2 states (On/Off).
guide.textarea_std_concept_desc: Provides a UI that balances ease of input and information visibility in flexible long-form text entry, reducing input errors.
guide.textarea_std_desc: Defines common rules for components that handle multi-line input, such as Textarea and Mentions.
guide.textarea_std_note_desc: Use standard 'Input' for short entries and 'Textarea' for long text or comments. Consider using 'Mentions' when a response to specific keywords is required.
guide.textarea_std_rule_1: Size Adjustability: Supports not only fixed sizes but also `fieldSizing: content`, where the height expands automatically based on the input.
guide.textarea_std_rule_1_desc: Supports not only fixed sizes but also `fieldSizing: content`, where the height expands automatically based on the input.
guide.textarea_std_rule_2: Explicit States: Clearly indicate states such as input error (Error) or disabled (Disabled) through changes in borders or background colors.
guide.textarea_std_rule_2_desc: Clearly indicate states such as input error (Error) or disabled (Disabled) through changes in borders or background colors.
guide.textarea_std_rule_3: Integrated Functions: When adding special completion functions like Mentions (@) or Hashtags (#), ensure styles are common with the basic text area.
guide.textarea_std_rule_3_desc: When adding special completion functions like Mentions (@) or Hashtags (#), ensure styles are common with the basic text area.
guide.textarea_std_rule_4: Layout Optimization: Standardize width control through the `fullWidth` property to maintain consistency within forms.
guide.textarea_std_rule_4_desc: Standardize width control through the `fullWidth` property to maintain consistency within forms.

basicinput.guide_desc: Choose components for entering basic text or numerical values from users.
basicinput.input_usage: Name, email address, phone number, etc.
basicinput.mask_usage: Credit cards, dates, fixed format inputs.

formlabels.a11y_risk_desc: Without correct implementation, screen readers might not read labels properly.
formlabels.allowed_cases: Cases where usage is exceptionally allowed
formlabels.deprecated_policy: Not recommended in principle due to many UX challenges.
formlabels.floating: A design pattern where the label is shown inside the field like a placeholder initially, shrinking and moving to the top when focused
formlabels.guide: Guidelines regarding label placement in forms and the use of Floating Labels
formlabels.line_break: Can line-break depending on label length
formlabels.missing_info_desc: Since it occupies space inside the field when empty, there's no room for format examples (hints), making it hard to convey 'what' and 'how' simultaneously.
formlabels.mobile_space_desc: When the need to save height on mobile outweighs usability concerns.
formlabels.mobile_width: Can effectively utilize width on mobile screens
formlabels.placeholder_benefit: Can use placeholders as supplementary text.
formlabels.scannability_benefit: Smoothly check inputs just by moving eyes from top to bottom.
formlabels.top_align: WIM UI recommends Top-aligned, displaying the label above the input field
formlabels.visibility_benefit: Fixed label position and sufficient font size ensure readability.

formlayout.guide_desc: Elements to organize input fields and enhance accessibility and usability.
formlayout.inputgroup_desc: Adds icons or units before/after (Prefix/Suffix) the input field.
formlayout.label_desc: Explicitly identifies input item names. Click on labels to focus the field.
formlayout.label_necessity_desc: All input items should have a `Label`; do not use placeholders as a replacement.
formlayout.legend_desc: The title for items grouped by Fieldset.
formlayout.proximity_principle_desc: Place `FieldError` immediately near the input item where the error occurred.
formlayout.visual_grouping_desc: Use `Fieldset` for semantic groups like address or profile information.

formui.abandon_form: Frustration builds up if they don't know what to fix, causing form abandonment.
formui.auto_conv_details: Absorb notation variants (e.g., full-width to half-width).
formui.auto_conv_effect: Reduces user burden and prevents data inconsistency.
formui.autocomplete_effect: Skips manual input and significantly reduces typos.
formui.btn_activation_details: Disable button until required fields are filled, or validate on click.
formui.btn_activation_effect: Prevents accidental submission in incomplete states.
formui.burden: Users feel burdened and abandon the flow when excessive input items or irrelevant information are required.
formui.char_limit_details: State limits (e.g., "Max 100") and show real-time counts.
formui.char_limit_effect: Prevents post-input corrections and gives reassurance.
formui.clear_cta_details: Use specific labels like "Submit" or "Next" with visual emphasis.
formui.clear_cta_effect: Users can execute the next action without hesitation.
formui.count_opt_effect: Reduces click count and lessens user "tedium".
formui.count_opt_examples: Use radios for few choices; limit items to essentials.
formui.error_confusion: Users get confused if instructions are ambiguous or error messages aren't specific.
formui.external_link_details: Don't lead users away during input; use new tabs if needed.
formui.field_width_effect: Improves visual balance and provides hints (affordance).
formui.field_width_examples: Set widths matching content (e.g., zip code, address).
formui.form_guide: Guidelines for designing forms that are easy for users to input and complete without stress.
formui.help_text_details: Crucial info near field; supplementary info in tooltips.
formui.help_text_effect: Clarifies rules and reduces hesitation or errors.
formui.increase_conversion: Aims to increase conversion rates by preventing input mistakes and errors, and reducing psychological burden.
formui.info_grouping_effect: Makes info chunks easier to recognize and smoothes the flow.
formui.info_grouping_examples: Place personal info, address, etc., together.
formui.inline_validation_effect: Notice errors immediately and encourage on-the-spot fix.
formui.input_method_details: Use DatePickers or Dropdowns to reduce free text input.
formui.input_method_effect: Prevents format errors and maintains data consistency.
formui.label_top_effect: Reduces eye movement and increases visibility, improving input speed.
formui.loading_indicator_effect: Conveys that process is ongoing, providing reassurance.
formui.long_complex_form: Forms are too long or complex
formui.many_choices: Displaying too many choices at once obscures which ones are required, leading to misinputs.
formui.mobile_keypad: On mobile, set `input type` appropriately, such as showing the numeric keypad for phone number fields.
formui.optimal_keypad_effect: Reduces input stress for mobile users.
formui.placeholder_label_effect: Ensures users always know what to enter and maintains a11y.
formui.placeholder_not_label: Use placeholders as hints; never substitute for labels.
formui.req_opt_effect: Allows users to judge at a glance what must be entered.
formui.req_opt_marks: Clearly mark "Required" items and add "(Optional)" to others.
formui.spacing_effect: Clarifies relations between Label, Input, and Help Message.
formui.step_viz_effect: Shows the path to the goal, providing reassurance and completion.
formui.step_viz_stepper: Show progress bars (Stepper) for multi-page forms.
formui.tap_mistake: Buttons and inputs that are too small induce mistaps and operational errors.
formui.unresponsive: Users will give up on the input completely if the responsive design is inadequate.

picker.behavior_memorized_or_copy: User knows value or wants to paste
picker.color_input_usage: When users need to paste HEX/RGB codes directly.
picker.color_picker_usage: Intuitive selection from palettes or gradients for themes/designs.
picker.date_picker_usage: Specifying birthdays, reservations, or deadlines with a visual calendar.
picker.date_range_input_usage: Specifying two dates via text input without opening a calendar.
picker.date_range_usage: Hotel stay durations, aggregation periods, etc.
picker.disabled_dates_desc: Dates that cannot be selected (e.g., past dates) should be grayed out.
picker.invalid_state_desc: Clearly indicate invalid states (e.g., graying out past dates).
picker.kb_a11y_desc: Ensure users can navigate pickers via `Tab` and confirm via `Enter`.
picker.mobile_overlay_desc: On mobile, use `Dialog` or `BottomSheet` for pickers that would take too much space.
picker.preview_feedback_desc: Provide constant visual feedback for the selected value (like `ColorInput`).
picker.range_slider_usage: Specifying ranges like price, age, or time intervals.
picker.slider_usage: Best for intuitive adjustments like volume or brightness.
picker.time_picker_usage: Selecting HH:mm separately for appointments or business hours.

placeholder.as_label_dont_desc: Reducing labels to look cleaner (Item names disappear during input)
placeholder.avoid_transient_info: Avoid including information that disappears during input (when starting to type).
placeholder.concise_words: Use short words readable at a glance, and choose placement appropriately according to info importance and length.
placeholder.guide_desc: Placeholders are for displaying short hints or examples (samples) of what to enter in an input field.
placeholder.philosophy_desc: A placeholder is just a "hint". It displays a specific input format example instead of the item name (label).

selection.btn_group_behavior_desc: Grouping multiple related operations. Clicking triggers an action.
selection.btn_group_scene_desc: When grouping independent action buttons like 'Save / Duplicate / Delete' or 'Edit / Delete'.
selection.checkbox_description: Allows multiple selections (0 or more). Each item is independent.
selection.checkbox_group_want_confirm: Confirm multiple values at once via 'Save' or 'Submit'
selection.chip_visual_usage: Display or select tags in a visually emphasized format
selection.choose_one_confirm_later: Select one from few candidates and submit later
selection.default_value_description: Radios usually have a recommended value pre-selected. Checkboxes are usually unselected by default.
selection.deferred_description: Radios and Checkboxes are normally used in forms where states are confirmed by 'Save' or 'Submit'.
selection.guide_desc: Choose the optimal format based on the number of options and the nature of the input.
selection.immediacy_deferred_alt: If you don't want to confirm until 'Submit', use Radio Button
selection.immediacy_needed: Result should be reflected the moment it's selected
selection.immediate_description: Switches and SegmentedControls should be used when settings are saved or views changed instantly.
selection.in_content_filter: Filtering or switching display format within the same content
selection.major_nav: Primary navigation or large-scale switches in the app
selection.multi_item_usage: Select multiple items from a list
selection.nature_multi_alt: If selecting multiple, use Checkbox or Chips
selection.radio_checkbox_guide_link: Guide: Refer to Guides / Radio vs Checkbox for detailed comparison.
selection.radio_description: Always exactly one selection. One item must always be selected.
selection.radio_group_usage: Selecting one option from a few (2–5) items. (e.g., shipping date, sort order).
selection.radio_individual_usage: Individual options (when placed independently without grouping)
selection.radio_usecase: Payment method (Credit/Bank), Sort order (Price Low/High), shipping date.
selection.range_global_alt: If moving across major screens, use Bottom Navigation
selection.range_partial: Inside a screen or changing display format
selection.search_filter_usage: Search and narrow down from a vast amount of data
selection.seg_count_alt: If 5 or more, use Dropdown or Horizontal Scroll Tabs
selection.seg_vs_other: Since SegmentedControl shares a similar role with other components, appropriate usage is important.
selection.segmented_behavior_desc: Switching values or display modes. Always exactly one is selected.
selection.segmented_scene_desc: When deciding or changing one state, such as 'Week / Month View' or 'Asc / Desc Sort'.
selection.segmented_usecase: Switch view format (e.g., Week/Month), change sort order (e.g., Asc/Desc).
selection.smooth: makes eye movement much smoother and reduces mistaps on mobile.
selection.space_saving_usage: Select from a medium-sized list while saving space
selection.switch_description: Toggles between two states (ON/OFF). Ideal for binary states like enabling/disabling.
selection.switch_group_usage: Immediate changes for multiple notification settings, etc.
selection.switch_in_place: Switch display mode or filters on the spot
selection.switch_usage: Immediate changes for Wi-Fi, Dark Mode, Notification settings.
selection.switch_usecase: Wi-Fi or Bluetooth ON/OFF, Dark Mode switch, instant notification enable.
selection.tab_exclusive_desc: Each tab has dedicated content and usually does not overlap
selection.tap_area_description: Make label texts clickable and ensure sufficient hit area.
selection.toggle_group_usage: Filter conditions, mode switch, size selection.
selection.toggle_group_visual_usage: Select from visually emphasized button formats

icons.bold_switch: When text becomes bold, icon weight also automatically thickens.
icons.doc_ref: For specific usage of the `Icon` component and a list of available icons, please see the Icon Component Documentation.
icons.feedback_clear: Provides clear visual feedback for the selected state.
icons.ghost_btn_reason: Matches border texture for a clean look.
icons.guide_title_desc: Guide for icon design principles, naming conventions, and usage guidelines across the app.
icons.heavy_weight_reason: Suits important actions needing strong attention.
icons.line_match: Matches icon stroke weight with other UI elements and borders.
icons.line_or_fill: There is no single correct answer to 'Line or Fill?'. It's important to differentiate them based on the app's nature and context where the icon is placed.
icons.mainstream_style_desc: Mainstream style: Outline for base, Filled for selected/important actions.
icons.no_mixing_desc: Avoid confusion; unify parallel features with same style.
icons.primary_btn_reason: Visibility needs to match button strength.
icons.radius_sync_desc: Match icon roundness to component roundness (Round vs Sharp).
icons.size_match: Icons automatically adjust to match the text font size.
icons.vis_priority_reason: Recognizable even when small due to silhouette.
icons.optical_alignment_desc: Adjust icons where the geometric center feels off (e.g., play button) to ensure they look visually centered.
icons.simplicity_desc: Strip unnecessary details to ensure icons remain recognizable at small sizes (16-24px).
icons.naming_conv_desc: Unify naming as `[Name]Icon` (e.g., SettingsIcon) to improve predictability within the codebase.
icons.accessibility_desc: Consider using `aria-label` or tooltips since icons alone may sometimes be ambiguous.

internal.category_desc: These are fundamental building block components used internally across various other components. They are not intended for direct use in application code, but understanding them helps when contributing to or extending WIM UI.
internal.category_note: These components are internal implementation details. Prefer using the higher-level public components that encapsulate them.
internal.comp_base_list_role: Standardizes layout and interaction states for list-like items used in Menus, Selectes, and TreeViews.
internal.comp_field_template_role: Standardizes label placement, mandatory marks, and error message display for all form-related components.
internal.comp_indicator_base_role: Standardizes visual styling and animation for status dots and badges.
internal.comp_input_base_role: Standardizes the visual container, icon slots (Prefix/Suffix), and clear button behavior for text-based inputs.
internal.comp_overlay_base_role: Standardizes portal-based rendering, backdrop, and focus management for Dialogs, Drawers, and BottomSheets.
internal.comp_status_content_role: Standardizes layout for empty states and error boundaries, including icon, title, and description.
internal.comp_feedback_close_role: Shared close button for Alert, Modal, Notification, and other overlay components.
internal.comp_feedback_icon_role: Standardized status icons (success, error, warning, info) used across feedback components.
internal.field_template_features_error_desc: Integrated display of `FieldError` when an error message is provided.
internal.field_template_features_layout_desc: Support for vertical (default) and horizontal layouts.
internal.input_base_features_clear_desc: Automatic clear icon display when `allowClear` and `hasValue` are true.
internal.input_base_features_width_desc: Flexible width control (XS to XL or custom values).
internal.overlay_base_features_portals_desc: Ensures the component is rendered outside the main DOM tree to avoid z-index issues.
internal.overlay_base_features_backdrop_desc: Manages the darkened background (Overlay) and its click-to-close behavior.
internal.overlay_base_features_focus_desc: Integrated with `FocusTrap` to prevent focus from escaping the modal.
internal.overlay_base_features_perf_desc: Uses `will-change: transform` for high-frequency animations to ensure 60fps, offloading to the GPU.
internal.philosophy_desc: Guidelines for internal design consistency and encapsulation that should be followed when extending WIM UI or adding new components.

guide.internal_desc: Overview of the internal building-block components that underpin WIM UI's public API. Understanding these helps you contribute to or extend the library consistently.

principle.dom_desc: Keep the rendered DOM as flat as possible. Avoid unnecessary wrapper elements that add depth without semantic value.
principle.animation_desc: Use the Transition component for enter/exit animations. Do not implement custom CSS keyframes without consulting the design system team.
principle.transition_desc: All transitions must respect the user's reduced-motion preference via the `prefers-reduced-motion` media query.

layout.flexibility: WIM UI provides a rich set of layout components from simple linear stacks to multi-dimensional grids. Choose the right one based on the structure and flexibility you need.
layout.linear_stack: Linear stacking of elements in one direction
layout.stack_usage: Vertical or horizontal list, spacing between cards
layout.flexible_flex: Flexible arrangement with fine-grained Flexbox control
layout.flex_usage: Horizontally aligned icons and text, custom gap
layout.multi_dim_grid: Multi-dimensional layout with rows and columns
layout.basic_box: Basic box wrapper with style props
layout.box_usage: Wrapping with background color or padding
