layout.container_usage: Centering page content within a maximum width
layout.bento_desc: Asymmetric grid cells spanning multiple rows and columns
layout.masonry_desc: Items fill columns top-to-bottom with varying heights
layout.splitter_desc: Drag handle between panes to resize; ideal for editors and split views
layout.gap_control_desc: Control spacing with the `gap` prop on Stack, Flex, Grid, or Group rather than adding margins to children.
layout.simple_grid_responsive_desc: Use SimpleGrid's `cols` prop with breakpoint objects to create responsive column layouts without custom CSS.
layout.box_as_prop_desc: Use Box's `component` prop (e.g., `component="section"`) to render semantic HTML while applying design-system styles.
layout.container_max_width_desc: Wrap page content in Container and set `size` to a breakpoint token to ensure readable line lengths on wide screens.

guide.layout_desc: Guidelines for roles and placement of Header, Sidebar, Main, and Footer.
guide.layout_footer_content: Recommended: Copyright, terms of service, privacy policy, language switcher, social links
guide.layout_footer_desc: Contains supplementary or legal information. Often omitted in web applications but critical for websites.
guide.layout_header_content: Recommended: Logo, global search, notifications, user profile, top-level navigation
guide.layout_header_desc: Provides context for the entire application and access to global actions. Should include features accessible from anywhere.
guide.layout_main_desc: The central area where users perform tasks. Data display and operations happen here.
guide.layout_overlay_desc: Layer for catching user attention or inputting supplementary info without interrupting the workflow.
guide.layout_pageheader_content: Recommended: Page title, breadcrumbs, primary action buttons, filter toggles
guide.layout_pageheader_desc: Contains the current page title, breadcrumbs, and primary actions for that page (create, save, delete, etc.).
guide.layout_responsive_desc: Adapts the layout based on screen size. Typically, sidebars become drawers and header menus collapse into hamburger menus on mobile.
guide.layout_responsive_mobile: Mobile (< 768px): Sidebar -> Drawer, Header Menu -> Hamburger
guide.layout_rightpanel_content: Recommended: Property panels, comment threads, chat, help documentation
guide.layout_rightpanel_desc: Displays details of selected items, settings, help, or notification history. Can be permanent or temporarily triggered.
guide.layout_sidebar_content: Recommended: Main menu, project lists, filtering options, category lists
guide.layout_sidebar_desc: Manages primary navigation within the application and hierarchical movement. Suitable for drill-down menus.

nav.active_state_desc: Always visually indicate which tab or menu item is currently active.
nav.anchor_desc: Shortcuts to specific sections on long pages.
nav.breadcrumb_desc: Understand current location and quickly return to parent categories.
nav.burger_desc: Mobile aggregation for many menu items.
nav.context_switch_desc: Best for switching views within the same context.
nav.fixed_pos_desc: Fix navigation positions so they don't move between pages.
nav.guide_desc: Choose ways for users to move within apps, content, or switch views.
nav.pagination_desc: Moving through pages of large datasets.

navutil.affix_desc: Pins sidebars or buttons at specific positions even during scrolling.
navutil.affix_usage_note: Use `Affix` to prevent important navigation from disappearing during scroll.
navutil.backtop_desc: Allows one-click scrolling to the top on long pages.
navutil.backtop_usage_note: Consider providing `BackTop` for pages requiring 3+ scrolls.
navutil.floatbtn_desc: Sticky buttons (e.g., bottom right) for prompts or inquiries.
navutil.floatbtn_usage_note: `FloatButton` is highly attention-grabbing; limit its use to avoid clutter.
navutil.guide_desc: Supplementary navigation elements that follow scrolls or jump instantly.

philosophy.title: Philosophy
philosophy.aria_support: Leverages WAI-ARIA to enhance support for assistive technologies.
philosophy.feedback_desc: Provides rapid and natural feedback for user operations, offering a comfortable "tangible" experience.
philosophy.focus_areas: We focus on the following points for design and development:
philosophy.kb_a11y: Supports keyboard operations so all users can use it.
philosophy.standard_overview_desc: For a high-level view of our design and implementation standards, please refer to the Standardization Overview.
philosophy.choice_matrix_desc: Foundation for all WIM UI components and design systems.
philosophy.scenarios_desc: Providing a tangible UI for all applications.
philosophy.tokens_desc: Foundation for all WIM UI components and design systems.
philosophy.responsive_desc: Standard responsive behavior follows the global breakpoint specifications.
philosophy.keyboard_nav_desc: Focus management and keyboard shortcuts across all interactive elements.
philosophy.principles_desc: All design decisions in WIM UI are based on the following five principles.
philosophy.principle_1_desc: All UI elements share a unified visual language through design tokens.
philosophy.principle_2_desc: Assumes WCAG AA compliant contrast ratios and WAI-ARIA patterns.
philosophy.principle_3_desc: Switching between light and dark modes is handled entirely by semantic tokens.
philosophy.principle_4_desc: Supports Japanese, English, and Portuguese, considering the typographic characteristics of each language.
philosophy.principle_5_desc: Provides an optimal experience on both desktop and mobile.

internal.philosophy_desc: Guidelines for internal design consistency and encapsulation that should be followed when extending WIM UI or adding new components.

qa.summary_desc: An overview of WIM UI's quality assurance, documentation, and test stability.
qa.summary_doc1_desc: The `Architecture/Standardization Overview` page has been created, enabling an overview of design philosophy and implementation rules in one place.
qa.summary_doc2_desc: Accessibility translation keys have been consolidated in `common.json`, enabling consistent aria-labels across the entire library.
qa.summary_fix1_desc: `react-i18next` is mocked globally in `test-setup.ts` with support for variable interpolation (`{{month}}`). Individual test files must not redefine the mock — use the shared setup.
qa.summary_fix2_desc: Use case-insensitive regular expressions for text queries (e.g., `/Close/i`). Prefer semantic queries (`getByRole`, `getByLabelText`) over `getByText` to make tests resilient to minor label changes.
qa.summary_fix3_desc: For components with animations or deferred state updates, use `waitFor` or `findBy*` queries. Always wait for DOM changes to settle before asserting.
qa.summary_fix4_desc: When a component's API changes (prop names, class names, rendered output), update the corresponding tests immediately to keep them in sync with the implementation.
qa.summary_section1_desc: WIM UI maintains unit tests for all components using Vitest and Testing Library. Tests follow a `describe/it` structure and are co-located with each component as `Component.test.tsx`.
qa.summary_section2_desc: The following tools have been introduced to maintain quality:
qa.summary_tool1_desc: `npm run test:coverage` visualizes code coverage (using v8).
qa.summary_tool2_desc: `npm run test:check` (`scripts/generate-missing-tests-report.cjs`) automatically detects components without test files.
qa.summary_tool3_desc: `npm run test:report` runs coverage measurement and automated checks together.

guide.std_overview_desc: At WIM UI, we maintain strict standards for both design and implementation to provide a consistent user experience. This page serves as an index to oversee these standardization documents and understand our design philosophy.
guide.std_pillar_1_desc: Provides a unified look and feel across all components, minimizing user learning costs.
guide.std_pillar_2_desc: Ensures equal access for all users through compliance with WAI-ARIA and full keyboard support.
guide.std_pillar_3_desc: Makes responses to operations clear, correctly conveying system and user states.
guide.std_cat_input_desc: Standards to enable users to operate intuitively without confusion.
guide.std_cat_display_desc: Standards for organizing information and conveying meaning accurately.
guide.std_cat_feedback_desc: Standards for providing appropriate feedback on system status to users.
guide.std_cat_layout_desc: Standards that define the overall structure and consistent placement of applications.
guide.std_doc_styling_tokens_desc: Guidelines on design tokens and CSS variable management.
guide.std_doc_unit_selection_desc: Standards for selecting units like currency or weight in input fields.
guide.std_doc_list_item_desc: Guidelines for using BaseListItem to maintain consistency across all selectable items.
guide.std_doc_data_display_desc: Defines common rules for components used to organize and present information, such as Cards and DescriptionLists.
guide.std_doc_data_indicator_desc: Defines common rules for components that supplement information attributes or states, such as badges, tags, and chips.
guide.std_doc_navigation_desc: Choose ways for users to move within apps, content, or switch views.
guide.std_doc_feedback_desc: Presents system state changes and user feedback according to urgency and context.
guide.std_doc_progress_indicator_desc: Defines the role, types, design patterns, and best practices for progress indicators.
guide.std_doc_overlay_desc: Layer for catching user attention or inputting supplementary info without interrupting the workflow.
guide.std_doc_app_layout_desc: Guidelines for roles and placement of Header, Sidebar, Main, and Footer.
guide.std_doc_qa_summary_desc: Checklist and summary of quality assurance standards across all components.
guide.std_doc_action_desc: Unified sizing and loading states for all action-oriented components.
guide.std_doc_input_area_desc: Guidelines for standardized icon placement rules and the allowClear functionality.
guide.std_doc_text_area_desc: Defines common rules for components that handle multi-line input.
guide.std_doc_numeric_input_desc: Guidelines and technical considerations for consistent numeric input handling.
guide.std_doc_range_selection_desc: Defines common rules for components where a user selects values from a range.
guide.std_doc_selection_group_desc: Defines common rules for components where a user selects one from several options.
guide.std_doc_labeling_desc: Defines common rules for components that supplement information attributes or states.
guide.std_doc_table_desc: Defines common rules for components that list structured data.
guide.std_doc_state_area_desc: Defines common rules for components that communicate specific screen-wide states.
guide.std_doc_sequence_desc: Defines common rules for components that communicate ordered information or progress.
guide.std_next_steps_desc: Individual standardization documents summarize component-by-component comparisons, accessibility status, and specific Do/Don'ts. Always refer to the corresponding standard when adding new components or modifying existing ones.
guide.label_std_desc: Defines common rules for components that supplement information attributes or states, such as badges, tags, and chips.
guide.label_std_concept_desc: Ensures users can visually organize information by choosing the appropriate component based on the type of information and the presence of interaction.
guide.label_std_rule_2_desc: Unifies semantic colors (Success, Warning, Error, etc.) to ensure consistent meaning of information.
guide.label_std_rule_3_desc: Differentiates usage: Badges/Tags are non-interactive, while Chips are interactive (removable/selectable).
guide.label_std_rule_4_desc: When using icons, combine them with label text or provide appropriate Aria attributes.
guide.label_std_note_desc: Use 'Badge' for numerical counts, 'Tag' for information classification, and 'Chip' for manipulating choices.
guide.list_item_std_desc: When displaying user-defined options (dropdown items, menus, comboboxes, etc.), use the internal component BaseListItem to maintain a consistent look & feel (padding, hover color, click hit area) across the entire product.
guide.list_item_std_reason_desc: Previously, each component manually implemented items via div or li, leading to inconsistent hit areas and spacing between icons and text. Unifying these improves the 'tangibility' of the UI and the overall product quality.
guide.list_item_std_rule_1_desc: Do not specify padding or background-color (hover) in custom SCSS.
guide.list_item_std_rule_2_desc: Use src/components/_internal/BaseListItem when rendering selectable items.
guide.list_item_std_rule_3_desc: Ensure --wim-color-surface-hover is applied for hover states (automatically handled by BaseListItem).
guide.list_item_std_rules_list: The following rules apply when rendering selectable list items. Do not implement custom padding, hover styles, or click areas — use BaseListItem to ensure consistency.
guide.list_item_std_note_desc: If BaseListItem does not meet your requirements, consult the architecture team before implementing a custom solution.
guide.range_std_desc: Defines common rules for components where a user selects values from within a specific range, such as sliders and calendars.
guide.range_std_concept_desc: Provides a UI that allows intuitive manipulation of continuous value sets and enables accurate value entry and verification.
guide.range_std_rule_1_desc: Manage `value` (single value) or `range` (start/end value pair) in a consistent prop format.
guide.range_std_rule_2_desc: Set `min` (minimum) and `max` (maximum) to restrict selections within the valid range.
guide.range_std_rule_3_desc: Present current selection values in real-time through tooltips or numeric displays during dragging or selection.
guide.range_std_rule_4_desc: Consider fine-tuning with keyboard arrow keys and combining with direct input (where applicable).
guide.selection_std_desc: Defines common rules for components where a user selects one (or more) from several options, such as tabs and segmented controls.
guide.selection_std_concept_desc: Achieves smooth view switching and filtering by enhancing the visibility of the selected state and ensuring accessibility, including keyboard operations.
guide.selection_std_rule_1_desc: Use `value` and `onChange` (or `onValueChange`) to manage the current selection state.
guide.selection_std_rule_2_desc: Apply sliders or background color changes to the selected item to clearly indicate the active one.
guide.selection_std_rule_3_desc: Support moving between items with arrow keys and making selections with the Enter/Space keys.
guide.selection_std_rule_4_desc: Set `tablist` (for switching tabs) or `radiogroup` (for selecting settings) appropriately based on context.
guide.sequence_std_desc: Defines common rules for components that communicate ordered information or progress, such as Stepper and Timeline.
guide.sequence_std_concept_desc: Visualizes the flow of information in chronological or process order, allowing users to intuitively grasp 'where they are now' and 'what lies in the past or future.'
guide.sequence_std_rule_1_desc: Link items with lines (Connectors) to explicitly show information continuity.
guide.sequence_std_rule_2_desc: Express the status of each step (Wait, Process, Finish, Error) using colors and icons for easy identification of progress.
guide.sequence_std_rule_3_desc: Support both horizontal and vertical directions, allowing selection based on screen space and information density.
guide.sequence_std_rule_4_desc: Each item basic configuration consists of three elements: 'Icon/Point', 'Title', and 'Description'.
guide.state_std_desc: Defines common rules for components that communicate specific screen-wide states, such as EmptyState and Result.
guide.state_std_concept_desc: Presents information so that users can correctly perceive the current system status and decide what to do next without hesitation.
guide.state_std_rule_1_desc: Organize information in the order of Title, Description, and Action Button to optimize eye-tracking.
guide.state_std_rule_2_desc: Use icons and colors (Success, Error, Info, etc.) appropriate for the situation, ensuring the meaning is clear without relying on language alone.
guide.state_std_rule_3_desc: Offer means for users to solve problems or continue working through the `action` or `extra` properties.
guide.state_std_rule_4_desc: Allow translation keys for titles and descriptions to facilitate multi-language support.
guide.styling_std_desc: Guidelines on distinguishing between SCSS variables and CSS custom properties, and rules for token management in WIM UI.
guide.styling_std_concept_desc: Static logic is managed via SCSS, while themes and runtime extensibility are managed via CSS custom properties (Design Tokens).
guide.styling_std_rule_scss_desc: Used for defining primitive values, mathematical calculations (Type Scale, spacing multipliers), and static constants used only within the library.
guide.styling_std_rule_css_desc: All design elements (colors, spacing, fonts, border widths, etc.) must be exported as CSS variables. This enables dark mode support and runtime theme overrides.
guide.styling_std_rule_component_desc: Within individual component stylesheets (.scss), use var() whenever possible. Avoid hardcoded values (1px, 2rem, etc.) and reference standardized tokens instead.
guide.range_std_note_desc: Components with Range in their name (RangeSlider, RangeCalendar) accept an array of two values. Single-value variants accept a scalar. Do not mix these types.
guide.selection_std_note_desc: Choose the component whose ARIA role matches the semantic intent. Use Tabs for content switching, SegmentedControl for mutually exclusive settings, and ToggleGroup for multi-select filtering.
guide.sequence_std_note_desc: Stepper represents active user progress (steps to complete), while Timeline displays past events in chronological order. Do not swap these roles.
guide.state_std_note_desc: EmptyState and Result share the same content hierarchy via StatusContent internally. Dropzone does not support an action prop — use surrounding layout for call-to-action.
guide.numeric_std_desc: Guidelines and technical considerations for consistent numeric input handling across browsers.
guide.numeric_std_concept_desc: While <input type="number"> seems ideal for numeric input, its cross-browser behavior is inconsistent, particularly regarding non-numeric characters like 'e' (scientific notation) and local formatting. We aim to standardize this behavior.
guide.numeric_std_usage_warning_desc: Use type="text" with inputmode="numeric" for fixed-format numbers (credit cards, IDs).
guide.numeric_std_usage_do_1: Use step and pattern attributes to guide user input.
guide.numeric_std_usage_dont_1: Don't rely on browser-native spin buttons for precise control.
guide.numeric_std_usage_dont_2: Avoid using type="number" when non-numeric separators (hyphens, spaces) are allowed.
guide.numeric_std_usage_dont_3: Do not assume the value is always a valid number on 'input' event across all browsers.
guide.numeric_std_problem_1_desc: Different browsers handle invalid characters differently when in number mode.
guide.numeric_std_problem_2_desc: The 'e' character is often allowed but unexpected by users.
guide.numeric_std_safari_behavior: Allows 'e' and handles as scientific notation
guide.numeric_std_problem_3_desc: Native spin buttons and padding vary wildly between rendering engines.
guide.numeric_std_problem_4_desc: Some screen readers treat number inputs as spin buttons, which might not be desirable for all types of data.
guide.numeric_std_spin_button_warning: Consider hiding native spin buttons via CSS for a more consistent UI.
guide.numeric_std_recommend_desc: For most use cases involving IDs or formatted numbers, use type="text" with appropriate semantic hints.
guide.numeric_std_exp_notation_desc: Be aware that large numbers may still be converted to scientific notation in some contexts.
guide.numeric_std_tokens_desc: Uses semantic tokens like --wim-color-border to ensure a consistent appearance across all browser inputs.
guide.numeric_std_responsive_desc: Ensures that specialized numeric input fields scale appropriately on mobile devices while maintaining touch-friendly hit areas.
guide.numeric_std_keyboard_desc: Supports standard keyboard navigation including Up/Down arrows for incrementing, ensuring compatibility with assistive technologies.
guide.numeric_std_i18n_desc: Handles local separators (dots vs. commas) and ensures that help text is properly localized for all supported regions.
guide.numeric_std_test_desc: Verified across major browsers (Chrome, Safari, Firefox) to ensure consistent value parsing and validation behavior.
guide.numeric_std_scenarios_desc: Useful when standardizing large-scale data entry forms where numeric precision and cross-browser consistency are critical.
guide.numeric_std_usage_desc: Refer to the standard when implementing or choosing components for numeric data entry.
guide.action_std_desc: Unified sizing and loading states for all action-oriented components.
guide.action_std_concept_desc: To ensure a consistent user experience, all buttons and interactive elements must follow the same sizing scale (sm, md, lg) and handle loading states predictably.
guide.action_std_rule_1_desc: All buttons must use the sm, md, lg scale defined in the design tokens.
guide.action_std_rule_2_desc: Interactive elements should show a spinner or skeleton when performing async operations.
guide.action_std_rule_3_desc: Icons always maintain a 8px gap from the text label.
guide.action_std_rule_4_desc: All interactive elements must have a visible 2px outline on focus.
guide.action_std_note_desc: Legacy components are being phased out in favor of the new standardized versions listed above.
guide.std_design_intent_desc: Reference documentation for architectural standards and design tokens.
guide.std_choice_matrix_desc: Refer to individual component pages for specific selection criteria.
guide.std_anatomy_desc: Technical tokens and global style definitions.
guide.std_content_guidelines_desc: Follow WIM UI voice and tone guidelines for all text content.
guide.std_motion_spec_desc: Standard transitions defined in effects tokens.
guide.std_a11y_spec_desc: All internal tokens are tested for WCAG contrast compliance.
guide.std_real_world_scenarios_desc: Standard design patterns across the entire product suite.
guide.std_best_practices_desc: Use semantic tokens instead of hardcoded values.
guide.std_keyboard_nav_not_applicable: Not applicable to this reference guide.
guide.std_doc_form_labels_desc: Guidelines for form label placement and association.

guide.spacings_desc: Definitions for Spacings and Border Radius to maintain consistent layouts and shapes.
guide.spacings_focus_desc: The stroke width and offset spacing of the outline displayed upon focus to ensure accessibility (such as clarifying the current location during keyboard operation).
guide.spacings_guideline_1: The base 1rem follows the browser standard (typically 16px).
guide.spacings_guideline_2: Use CSS variables like var(--spacing-md) for spacings; do not use direct numerical values.
guide.spacings_guideline_3: Use different border radii depending on the component size (Button: sm/md, Card: lg).
guide.spacings_margin_desc: Use CSS variables like `var(--spacing-md)`, do not hardcode values.
guide.spacings_radius_desc: Use according to component size (Button: sm/md, Card: lg).
guide.spacings_no_hardcode_desc: Always use these tokens for `margin` / `padding` / `gap`; never hardcode raw values like `8px` or `12px`. Even when asked to "use an 8px base", map to the nearest token (8px → `--wim-spacing-md`, 16px → `--wim-spacing-2xl`). This scale is intentionally compact (based on a Major Second-like ratio), so some steps are non-integer — relying on tokens keeps spacing consistent and theme-safe.
guide.spacings_semantic_aliases_desc: Do not use value-based scale tokens directly in components. Use the following role-based aliases instead.
guide.density_desc: Global control density remaps heights and paddings for form controls and dense data surfaces without changing layout spacing tokens.
guide.density_modes_desc: Density is selected with `data-density` on `<html>` (or any ancestor). The default is comfortable.
guide.density_comfortable_when: Marketing pages, settings, and everyday forms.
guide.density_comfortable_effect: Standard control heights (e.g. md = 42px) and roomy table cells.
guide.density_compact_when: Dashboards, admin tables, and information-dense tools.
guide.density_compact_effect: Tighter control heights (e.g. md = 36px), control paddings, switches, and table cells.
guide.density_usage_desc: Call `setWimDensity` or set the attribute yourself. Nested scopes can override a parent density.
guide.density_tokens_desc: These CSS custom properties change under `[data-density="compact"]`. Field, button, list, and table chrome that reference them (Input, Textarea, Button, SegmentedControl, Menu, Table, …) update automatically.
guide.density_stable_desc: These stay stable so page layout and identity chrome do not collapse:
guide.density_storybook_hint: In Storybook, use the Density toolbar control, or open Token → Density for a side-by-side demo.
guide.theme_desc: Dark/light switching is a public CSS contract. Attribute name, values, and the `<html>` default target must stay stable for consumers.
guide.theme_attr_desc: Canonical CSS contract is still data-theme on <html> (document.documentElement). Prefer WimProvider or setWimTheme / ThemeToggle to write it — do not invent alternate attribute names.
guide.theme_light_effect: Force light map even when the OS prefers dark (`:root:not([data-theme="light"])` excludes it).
guide.theme_nested_desc: A descendant with `data-theme="dark"` can scope a dark island (custom properties inherit). Prefer `<html>` for the app-wide theme.
guide.theme_toggle_desc: WimProvider is the recommended React entry for 	heme / density / locale. ThemeToggle can still write data-theme when pplyToDocument is true. If both control the same document theme, lift state and set pplyToDocument={false} on the toggle.
guide.theme_impl_desc: Component SCSS must not hardcode `[data-theme="dark"]` or `prefers-color-scheme`. Use semantic `--wim-color-*` tokens only.

perf.animation_desc: For components involving continuous or complex animations, we use the CSS `will-change` property to give the browser a hint for optimization.
perf.animation_micro_interactions_desc: Applied to small but frequent interactions like `Switch` toggles and `Accordion` expansions to ensure lag-free feedback.
perf.animation_note_desc: Use sparingly as it consumes memory and GPU resources. Avoid using on too many small elements simultaneously.
perf.resource_desc: In the `Image` component, we've introduced a `priority` prop. When set to `true`, it applies `fetchpriority="high"` to the underlying `img` tag.
perf.resource_usage_desc: For the largest image above-the-fold (LCP - Largest Contentful Paint).
perf.resource_benefit_desc: Informs the browser to prioritize this image over other non-critical resources.

typo.code_desc: Uses monospace font to clearly indicate inline code snippets.
typo.contrast_desc: Maintain sufficient contrast (WCAG AA or better) against background. Check via `ContrastChecker`.
typo.filled_usage: Selected states, critical alerts, dark mode visibility.
typo.guide_desc: Guidelines for maximizing readability and accessibility by clarifying info hierarchy.
typo.icon_alt_desc: Convey info to screen readers via `aria-label` etc., when icons have meaning (e.g., as buttons).
typo.icon_aria_desc: Assists text or provides standalone action clues. Use `aria-label` for standalone use.
typo.icon_role_desc: Icons assist text or indicate standalone actions.
typo.inline_desc: Emphasizes parts of text or applies specific styles.
typo.kbd_desc: Uses monospace font to clearly indicate keyboard operations or shortcuts.
typo.link_desc: Navigation to other pages or resources. Use `Link` for navigation and `Button` for execution.
typo.mark_desc: Emphasizes hit portions of search results or critical parts with background colors.
typo.outline_usage: Standard UI parts, navigation, form assistance.
typo.quote_desc: Visually separates external quotes or text to be emphasized.
typo.readability_desc: For better readability, it is recommended to limit the line-width of body text to 30–45 characters for Japanese and 45–75 characters for alphabetic languages (English, Portuguese, etc.) using components like `Container`.
typo.semantics_desc: Use heading levels (h1, h2...) correctly according to document structure, not just visual size.
typo.text_desc: Has appropriate line-height and spacing to ensure readability of long text.
typo.title_desc: Possesses visual weight (boldness/size) to indicate page structure.
typo.lh_jpan_loose:
Loose (1.8)
Provides a spacious line height, making it easier to read on small screens like mobile devices. It gives a relaxed impression and ensures smooth eye movement.
typo.lh_jpan_normal:
Normal (1.6)
The standard line height for WIM UI. It offers the best balance between readability and information density, ideal for general articles.
typo.lh_jpan_snug:
Snug (1.5)
Sits between tight and normal. Optimal for concise body text, labels, and short UI descriptions in Japanese. Balances density with readability.
typo.lh_jpan_tight:
Tight (1.4)
Used for headings and labels where high information density is required. Suitable for conveying a lot of information in limited space.

viz.area_data_desc: Changes in total values, emphasizing volume over time.
viz.axis_labeling_desc: Always clearly label units and axes.
viz.bar_data_desc: Categorical data, rankings, comparing differences between items.
viz.color_minimal_desc: Minimize colors; focus on differentiating items via PCCS palette.
viz.funnel_data_desc: Process reduction stages, conversion rate visualization.
viz.gauge_data_desc: Current position relative to a single target, achievement level.
viz.heatmap_data_desc: Multivariable matrix density, behavior pattern visualization.
viz.legend_pos_desc: Adjust legend placement so they don't crowd the chart.
viz.line_data_desc: Time series, continuous changes, trend analysis.
viz.multi_series_total_trend: Trends in totals for multiple series
viz.not_only_color_desc: Don't rely on color alone; use tooltips and labels for clarity.
viz.pie_data_desc: Composition ratios, market share, part of the total.
viz.scatter_data_desc: Correlation between 2 variables, outlier detection, distribution checks.
viz.selection_criteria_desc: Select the ideal chart for the story you want to tell and the nature of your data.
viz.treemap_data_desc: Hierarchical data relations, contribution to the whole.
viz.nodegraph_usage: Interactively edit and display node-based directed graphs such as approval flows and AI pipelines.
viz.nodegraph_data: Directed Acyclic Graphs (DAG), workflows, dependency diagrams.
viz.scheduleview_usage: View, create, and move appointments on a calendar with a timeline (week, day, month views).
viz.scheduleview_data: Time-series event data, shifts, bookings, schedules.

guide.visualization_desc: Guidelines for choosing the right chart or graph component based on the type of data and the story you want to tell.

voiceandtone.title: Voice & Tone
voiceandtone.error: When operational input fails, there is a risk of data loss, or systemic issues arise.
voiceandtone.everyday: When users are handling daily tasks.
voiceandtone.guide: Guidelines to support WIM UI's 'tangible UI' from a communication perspective.
voiceandtone.guide_desc: Defines consistent personality (Voice) and contextual tone (Tone) so users can trust the system and operate with confidence.
voiceandtone.new: When users employ new features, or complex operations are demanded.
voiceandtone.personality: At the core of WIM UI is the personality of a 'Reliable partner who assists user tasks and guides to sure success'.
voiceandtone.point1: Unobtrusively and flatly conveys only the minimum required info to let the users proceed at their own pace.
voiceandtone.point2: Briefly communicates a sense of security 'It is indeed completed' without extra hype, while sharing a feel of achievement.
voiceandtone.point3: Strictly avoid wording that blames users. Clearly present the fact of what happened and actionable specifics on how to solve it.
voiceandtone.point4: Guides users so they can confidently operate, by breaking down steps minutely and carefully explaining jargon.
voiceandtone.success: When a task is completed, or operational input is properly received.
voiceandtone.tone_desc: While maintaining the consistent Voice personality, the tone alters matching the user's situation and feelings.
voiceandtone.voice_clear_desc: Avoid jargon and roundabout expressions; choose words anyone can understand.
voiceandtone.voice_empathetic_desc: Present solutions from the user perspective instead of imposing system convenience during errors.
voiceandtone.voice_helpful_desc: Organize info so users can tell what to do next at a glance.
voiceandtone.voice_honest_desc: Avoid exaggeration or overly decorated words; convey facts accurately.
voiceandtone.voice_reliable_desc: Foster trust by maintaining consistent wording.
voiceandtone.voice_supportive_desc: Maintain an attitude of always supporting user goals.
voiceandtone.responsive_desc: Standard responsive behavior follows the global breakpoint specifications.

guide.title: Z-Index System
guide.desc: WIM UI manages stacking contexts through global tokens to prevent issues when multiple overlays overlap.
guide.layers_desc: Use the following tokens to achieve a consistent stacking order.
guide.guideline_no_raw_values_desc: Do not use raw values like `z-index: 100` on a component's root element. Always refer to the tokens above.
guide.guideline_stacking_context_desc: For overlaps within a component (e.g., slider track and thumb), create an independent stacking context within the component and use relative values.
guide.guideline_portals_desc: Many overlay components use `Portal` to render directly under `body`, minimizing interference from parent `z-index` or `overflow: hidden`.

doc.avatargroup_a11y_spec: Group the entire component with role="group" and assign an aria-label containing total count information, such as "15 project participants".
doc.avatargroup_anatomy_excess: A numerical badge that indicates the total number of users who are not visible because they exceed the display limit.
doc.avatargroup_anatomy_items: A stack of overlapping Avatar components that represent a collection of users or participants.

doc.avatargroup_long_desc: A component for displaying multiple avatars overlapping to visually represent a group or list of participants.
doc.avatargroup_max_desc: You can limit the maximum number of avatars to display. The excess will be shown as a number.
doc.avatargroup_scenario_chat: Chat: Displaying several member avatars in combination as a group icon representation.
doc.avatargroup_scenario_collab: Collaboration: Displaying a list of members currently viewing or editing a shared document.
doc.avatargroup_scenario_sns: SNS: Overlapping previews of users who reacted to a post to visualize activity level.
doc.avatargroup_size_desc: You can apply sizes to all avatars within the group.
doc.avatargroup_total_desc: You can explicitly specify the total count regardless of the number of actual avatar elements.
doc.barchart_stacked_desc: By stacking multiple items vertically, you can compare both the total amount and its breakdown simultaneously.

Box is the most basic layout component in WIM UI.
It provides properties that wrap CSS properties (p, m, bg, etc.), allowing you to apply styles intuitively without writing inline styles.

doc.box_scenario_2: Styling Primitive: Using as a generic wrapper to apply design tokens directly via component props.
doc.card_footer_desc: Area for supplementary information or secondary actions.
doc.card_header_desc: Area for placing card titles or primary actions.
doc.card_with_header_footer_desc: Structure content logically using Card.Header for titles and Card.Footer for actions.

doc.center_anatomy_content: The specific element or group being positioned at the exact center of its parent's viewport.

doc.center_best_practice_2: Test Center behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.

doc.center_feature_1_desc: Center elements with just a few lines of code.
doc.center_feature_2_desc: Maintains centering across different screen sizes.
doc.center_feature_3_desc: Adjust styles like padding and margin as needed.
doc.center_icon_center_desc: Ideal for centering icons within buttons or containers.
doc.center_inline_placement_desc: Use when you want to center text or icons inline.
doc.center_keyboard_desc: This component is a layout primitive with no keyboard interaction of its own. Apply keyboard navigation to interactive content placed inside it.
doc.center_long_desc: A component for centering elements (horizontally and vertically) within their parent container.
doc.center_scenario_1: Empty States: Perfectly centering an icon and message when a list or search results are empty.
doc.center_scenario_2: Loading Overlays: Placing a spinner or progress indicator at the radial center of a page or section.
doc.chatui_bp_grouping_desc: Group consecutive messages from the same sender
doc.chatui_c_container: The main wrapper for the chat interface
doc.chatui_f_flex_desc: Messages can be positioned left or right
doc.container_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.container_anatomy_content: The main body of content that is constrained within the container's horizontal limits.
doc.container_anatomy_root: The outer wrapper that calculates and applies the maximum width and automatic side margins.
doc.container_best_practice_1: Use Container consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.container_best_practice_2: Test Container behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.container_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like Box better suits the use case.

doc.container_choice_self_when: When Container functionality with standard options is required.
doc.container_design_intent: Container is the primary tool for managing content width and horizontal centering. It prevents text lines from becoming too long for readability on large screens by enforcing a maximum horizontal bound.
doc.container_feature_1_desc: Set the maximum width using size properties like xs, sm, md, lg, or xl.
doc.container_feature_2_desc: Horizontally centers content by default within the available space.
doc.container_feature_3_desc: Removes width restrictions to let the container span the full width of its parent.
doc.container_fluid_desc: Displays content across the full window width without restrictions.
doc.container_keyboard_desc: This component is a layout container with no keyboard interaction of its own. Apply keyboard navigation to interactive content placed inside it.
doc.container_long_desc: Detailed information and usage instructions for the Container component.
doc.container_scenario_1: Article Reading: Centering a blog post or documentation with a constrained width for optimal readability.
doc.container_scenario_2: Landing Pages: Creating horizontal boundaries for hero sections or feature lists across wide viewports.

doc.datagrid_action_column_desc: Use the render function to add custom buttons or links (e.g., Edit/Delete) to specific cells.
doc.datagrid_api_col_desc_2: Label or JSX to be displayed in the column header.
doc.datagrid_api_col_desc_4: Whether the user can sort the grid by this column.
doc.datagrid_api_col_desc_5: Custom cell renderer function receiving value, row, and index.
doc.datagrid_api_col_desc_6: Horizontal alignment of the cell content: left, center, or right.
doc.datagrid_api_col_desc_7: Data field key used to extract values for this column.
doc.datagrid_api_col_desc_8: Whether to pin this column to the left side of the grid.

doc.datagrid_api_props_desc_10: Pagination settings including total pages and current page.
doc.datagrid_api_props_desc_11: Whether to display alternate row background colors.
doc.datagrid_api_props_desc_12: Whether to show borders around every individual cell.
doc.datagrid_api_props_desc_13: Whether to highlight rows when the mouse hovers over them.
doc.datagrid_api_props_desc_14: Whether the header remains fixed at the top during vertical scrolling.

doc.datagrid_api_props_desc_7: Unique key field used to identify each row (string or function).
doc.datagrid_api_props_desc_8: Current sort configuration (column key and direction).
doc.datagrid_api_props_desc_9: Callback function triggered when a column header is clicked for sorting.
doc.datagrid_api_props_desc_mobile_card: Mobile view: Switch to card layout.
doc.datagrid_basic_usage_desc: Standard implementation of DataGrid. Simply pass your column definitions and row data to display the grid.
doc.datagrid_bordered_desc: Enabling bordered adds lines between all cells, creating a spreadsheet-like appearance.
doc.datagrid_empty_state_desc: Displays a custom emptyMessage when the dataset contains no rows.
doc.datagrid_full_featured_desc: A comprehensive implementation combining sorting, selection, pagination, and custom action columns.
doc.datagrid_loading_state_desc: Setting loading={true} displays a skeleton screen while data is being fetched.
doc.datagrid_long_desc_1: DataGrid is a high-performance component for displaying large datasets with advanced features like sorting, selection, and pagination.
doc.datagrid_long_desc_2: It offers more advanced capabilities than the Table component, including column pinning and horizontal scrolling for complex data requirements.
doc.datagrid_note: To help you choose between Table and DataGrid, please refer to the comparison section at the bottom of this page.
doc.datagrid_pagination_desc: Divide large datasets into manageable pages. Configure page size, current page, and change handlers.
doc.datagrid_row_selection_desc: Enable the selection property to manage row checkbox selection. Supports multi-select patterns.
doc.datagrid_sorting_desc: Enable sortable on specific columns to allow users to toggle between ascending, descending, and unsorted states.
doc.datagrid_sticky_column_desc: Pin specific columns (like IDs or Names) to the left side so they remain visible while scrolling horizontally.
doc.datagrid_sticky_header_desc: Keep the header row visible at the top while scrolling through long lists of data.
doc.datagrid_striped_desc: Enabling striped adds a background color to alternate rows for better readability.
doc.datagrid_table_vs_datagrid_1: Best for simple data presentation. Ideal for readability when handling smaller datasets.
doc.datagrid_table_vs_datagrid_2: Built for complex, data-heavy applications. Includes built-in support for sorting, selection, and pagination.
doc.datagrid_table_vs_datagrid_desc: Choose the component that best fits your data volume and required interactivity.
doc.divider_best_practice_1: Use dividers sparingly — too many can make the interface feel fragmented rather than organized.
doc.divider_best_practice_2: Prefer spacing or background color differences over dividers when visual separation is already clear.
doc.faq_section_a11y_2: Appropriate level (h2) is specified for heading.
doc.faq_section_a11y_3: Keyboard operations (Open/Close with Enter, Space, navigate with arrow keys) are possible.
doc.faq_section_anatomy_accordion: A collection of Accordion items that can be opened or closed to reveal or hide answers.
doc.faq_section_anatomy_content: The detailed answer text revealed when the question is clicked.
doc.faq_section_anatomy_header: Section Header with primary title and optional descriptive subtitle.
doc.faq_section_anatomy_item: Individual question-and-answer container within the section.
doc.faq_section_anatomy_trigger: The interactive question text that toggles the answer visibility.
doc.faq_section_best_practices_1: Limit the list to genuinely common questions; avoid adding rarely asked questions that add noise.
doc.faq_section_best_practices_2: Use `layout="left"` to make effective use of whitespace on wider screens.
doc.faq_section_best_practices_3: Always provide a `title` and `description` so users can understand the topic before browsing questions.
doc.faq_section_choice_1: When there are many FAQs or you want to place a detailed description at the top
doc.faq_section_choice_2: When you want to utilize white space and make the title stand out on desktop screens
doc.faq_section_choice_3: When you want to place it as part of a page (such as a widget)
doc.faq_section_design_intent: FAQ sections are crucial for quickly resolving user queries on websites or applications. This component goes beyond just listing Accordions by acting as a 'section' with appropriate headings and descriptions.
doc.faq_section_keyboard_desc: All keyboard interactions (open/close with Enter or Space, navigate items with arrow keys) are delegated to the internal Accordion component and require no additional implementation.
doc.faq_section_layout_left_desc: On desktop and larger screens, the title and accordion are lined up side-by-side. On mobile, they are automatically stacked vertically.
doc.faq_section_long_desc: FAQSection is a component for listing frequently asked questions (FAQs) and laying them out as a section. It internaly uses Accordion component to provide a consistent user experience.
doc.flex_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.

doc.flex_anatomy_content: The child elements that are distributed and aligned along the main and cross axes.

doc.flex_direction_desc: Control the flow of content using row (default) or column orientations.
doc.flex_feat_1_desc: Flex lines can be displayed horizontally or vertically.
doc.flex_feat_3_desc: Control whether the flex items wrap or not.
doc.flex_gap_desc: Easily manage spacing between child elements using design system tokens.
doc.flex_justify_desc: Distribute space along the main axis using properties like center, start, end, or space-between.

doc.flex_wrap_desc: Control how child elements wrap when they exceed the parent container width.

doc.grid_feat_flex_desc: Easily adjust column/row counts, gaps, alignment, and more.
doc.grid_feat_semantic_desc: Uses a div element by default and supports various HTML attributes.
doc.grid_keyboard_desc: This component is a layout primitive with no keyboard interaction of its own. Apply keyboard navigation to interactive content placed inside it.
doc.grid_long_desc: The Grid component simplifies implementing CSS Grid layouts.

doc.grid_scenario_2: Form Layouts: Precisely aligning labels and inputs across varying column spans and responsive breakpoints.

doc.group_align_desc: Use the align property to control vertical placement (top, center, end, etc.) when elements have mixed heights.

doc.group_feat_align_desc: Defaults to align="center", aligning elements of different heights to the middle.
doc.group_feat_gap_desc: Adjust gaps between elements with the gap property.
doc.group_feat_grow_desc: Using the grow property makes all child elements expand to fill available space.

doc.group_scenario_2: Tag Clouds: Displaying a collection of keywords or filters that wrap naturally across multiple lines.

doc.infiniteScroll_access_desc: Important information should not be placed in the footer as it may become difficult to access; consider using it with a "View More" button.
doc.infiniteScroll_long_desc: InfiniteScroll is used to automatically load additional content when the user reaches the bottom of the page. It is a useful alternative to pagination for list-formatted data.
doc.infiniteScroll_perf_desc: To avoid excessive DOM elements, use in conjunction with virtual scrolling is sometimes recommended.
doc.inputgroup_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.

doc.inputgroup_anatomy_root: The wrapper that visually unifies an input field with its adjacent prefixes, suffixes, or buttons into a single logical entity.
doc.inputgroup_best_practice_1: Use InputGroup consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.

doc.inputgroup_scenario_1: Currency Entry: Combining a text input with a fixed '$' prefix to clarify the expected value format.
doc.inputgroup_scenario_2: Search with Action: Attaching a 'Search' button directly to a search input for a unified look and feel.
doc.marquee_design_intent: Marquee provides an eye-catching, looping animation for content. It is ideal for news tickers, logo scrolls, or highlighting sponsors in a way that encourages passive scanning by the user.
doc.marquee_feat_custom_desc: Control duration, reverse direction, vertical orientation, and pausing on hover.
doc.marquee_feat_loop_desc: Automatically duplicates content for seamless scrolling.
doc.marquee_keyboard_desc: This component does not require specific keyboard interaction beyond standard Tab focus through any interactive content placed inside it.
doc.marquee_long_desc: The Marquee component is used to display content (text, images, icons, etc.) in a looping animation horizontally or vertically. Suitable for news tickers, logo scrolls, highlighting call-to-actions, etc.
doc.marquee_title: A component that scrolls content horizontally, often used for announcements or news tickers.
doc.patterns_header_desc: A header for administrative screens combining `Header`, `Input` (Search), `Badge`, and `Avatar`. It shows examples of responsive placement, user menus, and notification icon layouts.
doc.portal_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.portal_anatomy_content: The React component tree or DOM fragment being teleported into a different part of the document.
doc.portal_anatomy_root: The original location in the component hierarchy that manages the mounting and lifecycle of the portal.
doc.portal_best_practice_1: Use Portal consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.portal_best_practice_2: Test Portal behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.portal_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like VisuallyHidden better suits the use case.
doc.portal_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
