doc.portal_design_intent: Portal is a structural utility for rendering components outside their parent DOM hierarchy. It is essential for ensuring that overlays, such as modals, tooltips, or dropdowns, are not cropped by parent overflow styles.
doc.portal_ex_mechanism_desc: Technique for rendering React components into a different DOM subtree outside of parent hierarchy.
doc.portal_ex_overflow_desc: Ensure floating elements are not cut off by containers with hidden exit or scroll overflow.
doc.portal_ex_target_desc: Render content into specific existing elements like document.body or custom containers.
doc.portal_ex_u1_desc: Displaying high-priority modal windows at the document root level.
doc.portal_ex_u2_desc: Ensuring tooltips and floating menus remain visible regardless of local overflow styles.
doc.portal_ex_u2_desc_2: Context-specific tooltips rendered at the global level for collision avoidance.
doc.portal_keyboard_desc: This component is a utility with no keyboard interaction of its own. Keyboard navigation applies to the content rendered through the portal.
doc.portal_long_desc: Detailed information and usage instructions for the Portal component.
doc.portal_props_desc_1: The React Node or element to be rendered through the portal.
doc.portal_props_desc_2: The target DOM element or selector where content will be teleported.
doc.portal_scenario_1: Global Modals: Rendering high-priority dialogue windows at the document root for correct z-index stacking.
doc.portal_scenario_2: Tooltips: Ensuring that floating informational popups are not cut off by paren't overflow:hidden styles.
doc.portal_u1_desc: Modals and lightboxes that need to span the entire application view.
doc.portal_u2_desc: Tooltips and popovers that must escape local scroll containers.
doc.portal_u3_desc: Secondary UI elements that should not affect the primary page layout flow.
doc.portal_when_to_use_desc: Guidelines on when to leverage portals for complex layout requirements.
doc.scrollarea_basic_desc: Standard implementation used to wrap content with custom, cross-browser consistent scrollbars.
doc.scrollarea_both_desc: Cases where simultaneous vertical and horizontal scrolling is required include:
doc.scrollArea_desc: A custom scrollbar component that provides high-performance, cross-browser consistent themes while maintaining a native-like feel.
doc.scrollarea_keyboard_desc: Arrow keys scroll the content area when it is focused. Page Up and Page Down scroll by larger increments. Home and End move to the beginning and end of the scrollable content.
doc.scrollarea_long_desc: Details and usage for the Scroll Area component.
doc.scrollarea_note_desc:
`ScrollArea` can control the scrolling direction with the `scrollAxis` property as `x` (horizontal), `y` (vertical), or `both` (both directions).
When horizontal space is needed, such as for wide tables or images, enable horizontal scrolling by specifying `scrollAxis="x"` or `"both"`.
The default is `y` (vertical only).
doc.scrollarea_simple_desc: For normal text or simple lists, it is common to use only vertical (`y`) direction to maintain readability.
doc.scrollarea_uc_diag_desc: Complex illustrations where the full picture doesn’t fit on the screen.
doc.scrollarea_uc_map_desc: When there is a need to move coordinates freely.
doc.scrollarea_uc_sheet_desc: When both columns and rows are numerous.
doc.scrollprogress_basic_desc: Visual indicator (usually a top bar) showing how far the user has scrolled through a page or container.
doc.scrollprogress_desc: A component that visualizes the progress of reading a page.
doc.scrollprogress_feat_custom_desc: Supports color variations. Can be customized to match your brand.
doc.scrollprogress_feat_target_desc: Supports scrolling within specific elements in addition to the entire window.
doc.scrollprogress_keyboard_desc: This component is a visual indicator with no keyboard interaction.
doc.scrollprogress_long_desc: Shows how far the user has read the current page with a progress bar, typically at the top of the screen. Useful for providing a visual guide of reading progress in long documents or articles.
doc.scrollprogress_usage_2: Scroll monitoring within a specific container
doc.sidebar_mobile_drawer_desc: With responsive (default: true), the Sidebar becomes an off-canvas drawer below the md breakpoint. Control it with mobileOpen and close it with onOverlayClick. Use HamburgerMenu with visibleBelow as the toggle inside your Header.
doc.simplegrid_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.simplegrid_anatomy_content: The collection of identical grid items being distributed across the responsive tracks.
doc.simplegrid_anatomy_root: The grid container that enforces equal-width columns and manages the responsive auto-fit behavior.
doc.simplegrid_best_practice_1: Use SimpleGrid consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.simplegrid_best_practice_2: Test SimpleGrid behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.simplegrid_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like Grid better suits the use case.
doc.simplegrid_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.simplegrid_choice_self_when: When SimpleGrid functionality with standard options is required.
doc.simplegrid_design_intent: SimpleGrid provides a streamlined way to create responsive, equal-width grids. It allows specifying a fixed number of columns or a minimum item width, automatically handling responsive transitions without manual media queries.
doc.simplegrid_ex_auto_desc: The number of columns changes automatically according to the screen width by specifying `minChildWidth`.
doc.simplegrid_ex_break_desc: The number of columns can also be explicitly specified for each breakpoint.
doc.simplegrid_feat_auto_desc: Automatically adjusts the number of columns based on the minimum width of child elements using the `minChildWidth` property.
doc.simplegrid_feat_fixed_desc: Fix the number of columns using the `cols` property.
doc.simplegrid_keyboard_desc: This component is a layout primitive with no keyboard interaction of its own. Apply keyboard navigation to interactive content placed inside it.
doc.simplegrid_long_desc: The SimpleGrid component is a high-level component for easily creating responsive grid layouts.
doc.simplegrid_scenario_1: Product Listings: Creating a responsive grid of product cards that automatically adjusts column count.
doc.simplegrid_scenario_2: Icon Displays: Lining up feature icons with equal spacing and width across multiple rows.
doc.skeleton_animation_desc: You can select no animation, pulse (blinking), or wave.
doc.skeleton_design_intent: Skeleton provides a placeholder to reduce perceived loading times. By mimicking the structure of the final content (such as avatars, text lines, or cards), it prepares the user for the upcoming data and prevents layout shifts (CLS).
doc.skeleton_title: Placeholder shapes that mimic the layout and dimensions of content during its loading state.
doc.skeleton_usage_example_desc: You can combine multiple skeletons to create placeholders such as actual card layouts.
doc.stack_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.stack_anatomy_content: The sequence of elements being arranged with uniform gaps along the stack direction.
doc.stack_anatomy_root: The layout container that enforces a vertical (or horizontal) stack formatting context for its children.
doc.stack_best_practice_1: Use Stack consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.stack_best_practice_2: Test Stack behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.stack_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like Flex better suits the use case.
doc.stack_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.stack_choice_self_when: When Stack functionality with standard options is required.
doc.stack_design_intent: Stack is the primary tool for vertical spacing and alignment. It ensures that related elements, like a title and its description, have consistent vertical gaps, creating a clear visual rhythm.
doc.stack_feat_flex_desc: Internal use of the `Flex` component allows for Flexbox properties such as `align` and `justify`.
doc.stack_feat_reset_desc: Specify `row` or `column` via the `direction` property (defaults to `column`).
doc.stack_feat_space_desc: Adjust spacing by specifying tokens like `xs`, `sm`, `md` or numerical values in the `gap` property.
doc.stack_keyboard_desc: This component is a layout primitive with no keyboard interaction of its own. Apply keyboard navigation to interactive content placed inside it.
doc.stack_long_desc: The `Stack` component is used to arrange elements vertically or horizontally and manage spacing between them.
doc.stack_row_desc: Elements can be side-by-side by specifying `direction="row"`.
doc.stack_scenario_1: Form Spacing: Vertically aligning input fields and their labels with consistent gap spacing.
doc.stack_scenario_2: Card Content: Arranging a title, image, and description text in a clear vertical rhythm.
doc.stack_spacing_desc: Spacing tokens from WIM UI (xs, sm, md, lg, xl, etc.) can be used directly.
doc.stack_title: A layout component for vertical or horizontal alignment
doc.table_sticky_header_desc: By combining the `stickyHeader` and `maxHeight` props, the header can be fixed at the top when scrolling.
doc.togglegroup_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.togglegroup_anatomy_content: The collection of related buttons that act as mutually exclusive or additive options for user selection.
doc.togglegroup_anatomy_root: The container that manages the internal state and manages focus navigation across its collection of toggle buttons.
doc.togglegroup_best_practice_1: Use ToggleGroup consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.togglegroup_best_practice_2: Test ToggleGroup behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.togglegroup_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like SegmentedControl better suits the use case.
doc.togglegroup_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.togglegroup_choice_self_when: When ToggleGroup functionality with standard options is required.
doc.togglegroup_design_intent: ToggleGroup provides a button-based alternative to checkboxes or radio groups. It is designed for compact toolbars or settings where a clear, tactile 'active' state is preferred for selection.
doc.togglegroup_group: When binary toggle states (On / Off) are grouped together.
doc.togglegroup_icon_only_desc: Useful for toolbars where space is limited and icons are universally understood.
doc.togglegroup_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the toggle group. Arrow keys navigate between options. Enter or Space selects the focused option. In single-select mode, selection moves with arrow keys automatically.
doc.togglegroup_long_desc: ToggleGroup components allow users to select one or multiple options from a set of buttons. It's often used for formatting options, alignment, or filtering where a button-like interface is preferred over checkboxes or radio buttons.
doc.togglegroup_multi_desc: Similar to a CheckboxGroup but with a button visual.
doc.togglegroup_reason_1: When you need a button-like interface for selection.
doc.togglegroup_scenario_1: Text Formatting: Grouping Bold, Italic, and Underline buttons in a compact editor toolbar.
doc.togglegroup_scenario_2: View Switching: Choosing between 'List', 'Grid', and 'Calendar' views with a button-based interface.
doc.togglegroup_single_desc: Similar to a RadioGroup but with a button visual.
doc.togglegroup_toolbar: For toolbars (e.g., text formatting: Bold, Italic, Underline).
doc.transition_desc: Utilities for managing smooth enter and leave animations with CSS classes
doc.transition_fade_desc: A simple fade-in/fade-out using opacity changes. Includes width animation when button labels change.
doc.transition_feat_1_desc: Coordinates classes like `enter` (during transition), `enterFrom` (start), `enterTo` (end), and `leave` series.
doc.transition_feat_2_desc: Automatically unmount child elements after the leave animation is complete.
doc.transition_feat_3_desc: Correctly supports React's lifecycle and hydration.
doc.transition_keyboard_desc: This component is a utility animation wrapper with no keyboard interaction of its own. Keyboard navigation applies to the content placed inside it.
doc.transition_long_desc: The `Transition` component is a utility for easily adding transition animations (enter/leave) to components using CSS classes. It applies and manages classes at appropriate times according to each stage of the transition.
doc.transition_slide_desc: An example combining opacity and position (transform) transitions.
doc.transition_stage_enter_timing: Applied throughout the entire enter phase.
doc.transition_stage_enterFrom_timing: Applied at the start of the enter phase (before the first frame).
doc.transition_stage_enterTo_timing: Applied at the end of the enter phase.
doc.transition_stage_leave_timing: Applied throughout the entire leave phase.
doc.transition_stage_leaveFrom_timing: Applied at the start of the leave phase.
doc.transition_stage_leaveTo_timing: Applied at the end of the leave phase.
doc.transition_title: Utilities for managing smooth enter and leave animations with CSS classes
doc.treeselect_cascade_desc: Selecting a parent automatically selects all its descendants. If only some children are selected, the parent shows an indeterminate state. Use this when you want to select an entire category at once.
doc.treeselect_exclusive_desc: A parent and its descendants cannot be selected at the same time. Selecting a parent clears all its descendants; selecting a child clears its ancestors. Use this when selections at different granularity levels should be mutually exclusive (e.g. preventing simultaneous selection of "Year" and "Month").
doc.treeview_checkbox_mode_desc: When the `checkable` property is enabled, a checkbox is displayed for each item, allowing for multiple item selections.
doc.toolbar_a11y_desc: Root uses role="toolbar" with aria-orientation. Provide aria-label or aria-labelledby. Groups use role="group". Separators are decorative (aria-hidden).
doc.toolbar_best_practice_1: Always set an accessible name on the toolbar (aria-label).
doc.toolbar_best_practice_2: Prefer ghost IconButton at size sm inside the toolbar for density.
doc.toolbar_best_practice_3: Separate unrelated action clusters with Toolbar.Separator.
doc.toolbar_choice_alt_when: When you only need joined or gapped buttons that share a variant (no toolbar semantics).
doc.toolbar_choice_matrix_desc: Choose based on whether you need an action strip, a joined button cluster, or an application menu.
doc.toolbar_choice_menubar_when: When you need File / Edit / View style menus with floating submenus.
doc.toolbar_choice_self_when: When composing IconButton / ToggleGroup / Button into a formatting or bulk-action strip.
doc.toolbar_design_intent: Editors and inspectors need a compact, predictable place for related actions. Toolbar provides the ARIA toolbar pattern and visual density without inventing a new button API.
doc.toolbar_i18n_desc: Toolbar itself has no built-in copy. Localize aria-label and child control labels in the consuming app.
doc.toolbar_keyboard_desc: Arrow keys move focus between focusable children along the orientation axis. Home and End jump to the first and last control.
doc.toolbar_long_desc: Toolbar groups IconButton, ToggleGroup, and Button controls into a single accessible action strip with density sizing and arrow-key focus movement.
doc.toolbar_scenario_1: Style and alignment controls above a document editor.
doc.toolbar_scenario_2: Delete / download / share actions that appear when gallery items are selected.

faq.section_default_desc: Answering common questions about WIM UI.
faq.a1: WIM UI is a modern, accessible design system based on React. It features practical capabilities like container queries and multilingual support.
faq.a2: Simply install the package via npm and import the desired components. You can check the specifications of each component in the Storybook.
faq.a3: Yes. All components use semantic color tokens and automatically switch based on the system OS setting or the `data-theme` attribute.
faq.a4: You can customize it to fit your brand by overriding Sass (SCSS) variables or CSS custom properties (design tokens).

appshell.guide_desc: AppShell and its sub-components define the top-level frame of your application. Use the table below to understand each component's role and placement, then choose the right combination for your scenario.
appshell.shell_usage: Root container that manages layout slots and responsive behavior
appshell.header_usage: Branding, global search, user profile, and top-level navigation
appshell.navbar_usage: Mobile-first top navigation bar optimized for thumb reach
appshell.sidebar_usage: Primary navigation and hierarchical drill-down menus
appshell.footer_usage: Legal info, language switcher, and supplemental links
appshell.tabbar_usage: Mobile tab navigation for switching between top-level sections
appshell.few_features: Few main features, balanced desktop & mobile

dashboard_doc.subtitle: A dashboard component for managing widgets with add and remove support. Provides widget layout on a CSS grid based on BentoGrid, and a management UI for dynamic changes via edit mode.
dashboard_doc.design_intent: Dashboard has two modes: a display mode for viewing widgets side by side, and a management mode for adding and removing widgets. By keeping the scope to add/remove without dnd-kit, dependencies are minimized while realizing a dynamic management UI that BentoGrid alone cannot provide.
dashboard_doc.choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
dashboard_doc.choice_dashboard_when: When you need to dynamically manage widgets
dashboard_doc.choice_bentogrid_when: When you want to arrange fixed content beautifully
dashboard_doc.choice_grid_when: When you only need to control column count
dashboard_doc.content_guideline_1: Keep widget `title` concise (~20 chars) and clearly indicate which data the dashboard refers to.
dashboard_doc.content_guideline_2: Use `description` for supplementary information such as time period or aggregation conditions.
dashboard_doc.content_guideline_3: Widget `content` accepts any React node: numbers, charts, lists, etc.
dashboard_doc.content_guideline_4: Handle the empty state when widgets reach 0 in the parent component.
dashboard_doc.motion_spec_1: Edit mode toggle: show/hide of delete buttons is handled via CSS `transition`.
dashboard_doc.motion_spec_2: For widget add/remove animation, combine React Transition Group or similar in the parent component.
dashboard_doc.a11y_spec_1: The root element does not use `role="region"`; the dashboard name is provided via `aria-label`.
dashboard_doc.a11y_spec_4: Remove buttons include the widget name in `aria-label` (e.g., "Remove Revenue").
dashboard_doc.scenario_1: SaaS admin panel: display and manage KPI cards, charts, and activity feeds as widgets
dashboard_doc.scenario_2: Personal settings page: a home screen where users can customize which widgets to display
dashboard_doc.scenario_3: Operations dashboard: overview of multiple data points such as server metrics and order counts
dashboard_doc.best_practice_1: Use `span` to combine wide widgets (charts, etc.) and narrow widgets (KPI numbers, etc.) for visual emphasis.
dashboard_doc.best_practice_2: After removing a widget via `onRemove`, also remove the `id` from the parent's state array. The component handles display only; data management is delegated to the parent.
dashboard_doc.best_practice_3: If drag-and-drop is needed, combine with dnd-kit and wrap `DashboardWidgetCard` with `useDraggable`.
dashboard_doc.variation_editable_desc: Clicking the edit button shows a remove button on each widget and an "Add Widget" button.
dashboard_doc.responsive_desc: Uses container queries. Auto-switches to 2 columns at `md` and 1 column at `sm`. The `columns` prop is passed to the `--dashboard-columns` CSS custom property.
dashboard_doc.keyboard_desc: Tab key to move between interactive elements in widgets and the edit button. Enter/Space to activate focused buttons (edit toggle, remove, add).

doc.accordion_a11y_spec: Properly set aria-expanded for triggers and aria-labelledby for content, and support navigation with keyboard arrow keys.
doc.accordion_anatomy_content: The expandable panel revealed when its trigger is activated, designed to hold details, settings, or nested controls.
doc.accordion_anatomy_icon: Usually a caret, indicating the state by pointing up when open and down (or right) when closed.
doc.accordion_anatomy_item: A logical unit consisting of a clickable trigger and its corresponding collapsible content area.
doc.accordion_anatomy_trigger: The interactive header that users click to toggle the visibility of the expansion panel. Contains a status icon.
doc.accordion_best_practice_1: Provide clear labels for triggers (headings) that make it easy to guess the content inside.
doc.accordion_best_practice_2: Avoid hiding critical notifications or mandatory actions that users must not miss inside an accordion.
doc.accordion_choice_accordion_when: When you want to arrange multiple related topics vertically, such as FAQs or detailed settings, and allow users to choose only what they need to read.
doc.accordion_choice_disclosure_when: In very simple cases like 'Show Details' where you just want to open and close a single fragment of information.
doc.accordion_choice_matrix_desc: Choose based on the priority of information and the space occupancy tolerance on the page.
doc.accordion_choice_tabs_when: When each topic is very important and the types of information are clearly separated, and you want to switch or compare them quickly.
doc.accordion_design_intent: Accordion is used to lower the cognitive load on users by dividing a large amount of information or settings into logical groups and hiding them by default. Users can expand only specific sections as needed and focus on the information they are interested in.
doc.accordion_disabled_desc: By passing the `disabled` prop to an `Accordion.Item`, you can disable interaction with that item.
doc.accordion_features_1_desc: Choose whether only one item can be opened at a time or multiple items can be opened simultaneously.
doc.accordion_features_2_desc: You can click an already open item in `single` mode to close it.
doc.accordion_features_3_desc: Complies with WAI-ARIA and holds appropriate roles and attributes.
doc.accordion_guideline_1: Use when displaying all content at once would make the screen cluttered, such as in FAQs or supplemental details.
doc.accordion_guideline_2: Effective in limited spaces like mobile screens, as it allows users to choose and open only the information they need.
doc.accordion_keyboard_desc: Tab moves focus through accordion triggers. Enter or Space toggles the focused item open or closed. Arrow keys are not required but the trigger order follows DOM order.
doc.accordion_long_desc: The accordion component allows content to be folded and displayed, letting users click to reveal more details.
doc.accordion_multiple_desc: By setting `type="multiple"`, you can have multiple items open at the same time.
doc.accordion_scenario_faq: FAQ: Use questions as triggers and hide answers to improve the overall view.
doc.accordion_scenario_filter: Search Filters: Group filter items by category and secure operation space by closing unnecessary filters.
doc.accordion_scenario_settings: Settings Page: Group detailed settings options by function to make the hierarchical structure easy to understand.
doc.bentogrid_a11y_desc: Uses semantic list structure. Each grid item should have a meaningful heading for screen readers.
doc.bentogrid_anatomy_content: The set of individual cards or panels that are arranged within the grid to showcase specific features or data.
doc.bentogrid_anatomy_root: The grid container that defines the masonry-like columns and rows for its responsive items.
doc.bentogrid_best_practice_1: Use BentoGrid consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.bentogrid_best_practice_2: Test BentoGrid behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.bentogrid_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like Grid better suits the use case.
doc.bentogrid_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.bentogrid_choice_self_when: When BentoGrid functionality with standard options is required.
doc.bentogrid_design_intent: BentoGrid organizes content into a modern, visually dynamic 'bento box' style arrangement. It uses varying card sizes and placements to create a strong visual hierarchy, making it ideal for feature showcases or dashboard overview pages.
doc.bentogrid_flexible_span_desc: You can use classes like wim-bento-grid-item--col-span-2 to make specific items span multiple rows or columns.
doc.bentogrid_keyboard_desc: This component is a layout primitive with no keyboard interaction of its own. Apply keyboard navigation to interactive content placed inside each item.
doc.bentogrid_modern_design_desc: Card format layout, suitable for showcasing product features.
doc.bentogrid_prop_header: Content displayed at the top of the item (image, placeholder, etc.)
doc.bentogrid_prop_icon: Icon displayed next to the title
doc.bentogrid_responsive_desc: Automatically adjusts to 1 column on mobile and 3 columns on desktop (default setting).
doc.bentogrid_scenario_1: Feature Showcase: Highlighting key application features with varied card sizes for high visual impact.
doc.bentogrid_scenario_2: Portfolio Gallery: Displaying projects or creative works in a dynamic, modern grid arrangement.
doc.bentogrid_subtitle: The BentoGrid component is used to create a modern, visually appealing "bento box" style grid layout.
doc.masonry_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.masonry_anatomy_content: The individual cards or images of varying dimensions being arranged into the waterfall flow.
doc.masonry_anatomy_root: The layout system that calculates the optimal column placement for unevenly sized content.
doc.masonry_best_practice_1: Use Masonry consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.masonry_best_practice_2: Test Masonry behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.masonry_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like Grid better suits the use case.
doc.masonry_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.masonry_choice_self_when: When Masonry functionality with standard options is required.
doc.masonry_columns_adj_desc: Adjust layout density by changing the column count.
doc.masonry_design_intent: Masonry creates a 'waterfall' grid effect where items of varying heights are packed tightly together, minimizing gaps. It is particularly effective for image galleries, social media feeds, or disparate cards.
doc.masonry_feat_auto_desc: Uses CSS column-count to automatically distribute elements into columns.
doc.masonry_feat_columns_desc: Specify any number of columns with the columns property.
doc.masonry_feat_spacing_desc: Easily adjust item spacing with the spacing property.
doc.masonry_keyboard_desc: This component is a layout container with no keyboard interaction of its own. Apply keyboard navigation to interactive content placed inside it.
doc.masonry_long_desc: Masonry is a layout component that efficiently places elements of varying heights to fill gaps. Used primarily for image galleries and cards with mixed heights.
doc.masonry_scenario_1: Photo Gallery: Displaying a mix of portrait and landscape images in a tight, gap-less arrangement.
doc.masonry_scenario_2: Social Feed: Rendering cards of varying lengths (text, media) into a dense, optimized layout.
doc.masonry_spacing_adj_desc: Adjust distance between elements with the spacing property.
doc.masonry_title: Masonry layout for efficient element placement
doc.splitter_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.splitter_anatomy_content: The individual panels (panes) that contain the application's interactive data or views being resized.
doc.splitter_anatomy_root: The main container that calculates panel ratios and coordinates the resize operations across all child segments.
doc.splitter_best_practice_1: Use Splitter consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.splitter_best_practice_2: Test Splitter behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.splitter_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like Grid better suits the use case.
doc.splitter_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.splitter_choice_self_when: When Splitter functionality with standard options is required.
doc.splitter_constraints_desc: Limit the resize range of panels using the `minSize` or `maxSize` properties.
doc.splitter_design_intent: Splitter allows users to customize their workspace by resizing adjacent panels. It is ideal for complex IDE-like environments, dashboards, or side-by-side data comparison views where screen real estate must be managed flexibly.
doc.splitter_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the splitter divider handle. Arrow keys resize the panels when the divider is focused. Home and End reset to minimum and maximum sizes respectively.
doc.splitter_long_desc: The Splitter is a layout component that allows multiple panels to be resized via drag operations.
doc.splitter_pc_only: Desktop Only: Resizing via pointer operations like drag-and-drop is primarily designed for desktop environments. Use on touch devices is not intended.
doc.splitter_scenario_1: IDE Layouts: Allowing users to resize side-by-side editor and preview panels for a custom workspace.
doc.splitter_scenario_2: Side-by-side Comparison: Resizing two documents or data versions to focus on specific differences.

doc.appshell_a11y_2: Proper landmark regions for screen readers
doc.appshell_a11y_desc: Uses semantic HTML5 elements (header, aside, main, footer) for proper landmark regions. Supports keyboard navigation between sections.
doc.appshell_anatomy_content: The central area reserved for the application's primary route content or page-specific views.
doc.appshell_anatomy_root: The main container that manages the overall grid or flex layout of the application sections.
doc.appshell_basic_layout_desc: A simple layout with just a header and main content.
doc.appshell_best_practice_1: Use AppShell consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.appshell_best_practice_2: Test AppShell behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.appshell_bp_a11y_desc: Ensure proper heading hierarchy and landmark regions for screen readers.
doc.appshell_bp_centered_desc: For reading-focused apps, use `centered` with appropriate `maxWidth`.
doc.appshell_bp_mobile_nav_desc: Use navbar for mobile-first applications to improve thumb-reachability.
doc.appshell_bp_padding_desc: Use the `padding` prop to control spacing around main content for better readability.
doc.appshell_bp_perf_desc: Keep sidebar and header content lightweight for better initial load and transitions.
doc.appshell_bp_responsive_desc: Test your layout on different screen sizes to ensure a consistent experience.
doc.appshell_bp_semantic_desc: Combine AppShell with Header, Sidebar, Footer, and Navbar components for consistent styling.
doc.appshell_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like Flex better suits the use case.
doc.appshell_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.appshell_choice_self_when: When AppShell functionality with standard options is required.
doc.appshell_composition_desc: AppShell also provides sub-components for more granular control:
doc.appshell_desc: A flexible application shell component that provides a complete layout structure for modern web applications. AppShell combines header, sidebar, main content, footer, and navbar areas into a cohesive layout system.
doc.appshell_design_intent: AppShell is the structural foundation of a web application. It orchestrates the positioning of high-level areas like navigation, headers, and main content into a cohesive, responsive layout, ensuring they remain interactive and accessible across different viewports.
doc.appshell_feat_centered_desc: Option to center content with maximum width constraint
doc.appshell_feat_flex_desc: Compose your layout with any combination of header, sidebar, main content, footer, and navbar
doc.appshell_feat_padding_desc: Control padding on the main content area
doc.appshell_feat_responsive_desc: Automatically adapts to different screen sizes
doc.appshell_feat_semantic_desc: Uses proper semantic elements (header, aside, main, footer)
doc.appshell_keyboard_desc: This component is a layout shell. Keyboard navigation applies to the interactive elements placed within each slot (header, sidebar, main, footer).
doc.appshell_mobile_drawer_desc: At or below the md breakpoint the Sidebar automatically becomes an off-canvas drawer (responsive is enabled by default). Pair it with HamburgerMenu shown only on mobile via visibleBelow. The app manages a single open state, and onOverlayClick closes the drawer when the overlay is tapped.
doc.appshell_overview_desc: The AppShell component is designed to be the foundation of your application's layout. It handles the positioning and organization of major UI sections, allowing you to focus on building your application's features.
doc.appshell_resp_desktop_desc: Full layout with the sidebar visible by default.
doc.appshell_resp_fallback_note: Note: by default, a plain sidebar (the sidebar prop or AppShell.Sidebar) simply stacks above the main content at or below the md breakpoint. This is only a safety fallback — the primary content gets pushed down by the full height of the navigation. For production apps, switch the navigation on mobile: use the Sidebar component for an off-canvas drawer (see the Mobile Drawer Pattern above), or move primary navigation to a bottom TabBar via the navbar prop.
doc.appshell_resp_mobile_desc: Sidebar is typically hidden, and a bottom navbar is shown for primary navigation.
doc.appshell_resp_padding_desc: Content padding adjusts automatically to maximize usable space on smaller screens.
doc.appshell_resp_tablet_desc: Sidebar may collapse into an icon-only view or become a drawer.
doc.appshell_scenario_1: Admin Dashboard: Managing a fixed sidebar and a sticky header for a comprehensive management interface.
doc.appshell_scenario_2: Mobile Web App: Switching to a bottom TabBar while maintaining a consistent main content area for small screens.
doc.appshell_sections_footer_desc: Positioned at the bottom; typically contains copyright, links, and legal information. Uses the `Footer` component.
doc.appshell_sections_header_desc: Fixed or sticky positioning; typically contains branding, navigation, and user actions. Uses the `Header` component.
doc.appshell_sections_main_desc: Primary content area with optional padding and centering; scrollable when content exceeds viewport height.
doc.appshell_sections_navbar_desc: Bottom navigation bar for mobile applications, fixed at the bottom. Uses the `Navbar` component.
doc.appshell_sections_sidebar_desc: Collapsible navigation panel with configurable width; can be positioned on left or right. Responsive for mobile.
doc.appshell_with_footer_desc: Include a footer for additional information.
doc.appshell_with_navbar_desc: Perfect for mobile applications with bottom navigation.
doc.footer_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.footer_anatomy_content: The main navigation links, sitemaps, or social icons distributed within the footer layout.
doc.footer_anatomy_root: The outermost container that separates the site's footer from the main content area, usually with a border or background change.
doc.footer_best_practice_1: Use Footer consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.footer_best_practice_2: Test Footer behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.footer_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like Header better suits the use case.
doc.footer_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.

doc.header_basic_desc: Place `Header.Section` inside the `Header` component. Use the `align` property ("start", "center", "end") on `Header.Section` to control content positioning.
doc.header_best_practice_1: Use Header consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.header_best_practice_2: Test Header behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.header_bordered_desc: Using the bordered property adds a border at the bottom, helpful for clearly separating content.
doc.header_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like Navbar better suits the use case.
doc.header_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.header_choice_self_when: When Header functionality with standard options is required.
doc.header_design_intent: Header is the primary navigation hub of an application. It provides consistent access to brand identity and high-level navigation, ensuring users can always orient themselves and access key features.
doc.header_glass_desc: Using the glass property applies a blur effect to the background, making it translucent and revealing content behind it.
doc.header_interactive_demo_desc: Use the Controls below to change properties like bordered, glass, and background in real-time.
doc.header_keyboard_desc: Tab moves focus through interactive links and buttons within the header in DOM order.
doc.header_long_desc: Header is a general-purpose header component placed at the top of pages or sections.
doc.header_scenario_1: Global Navigation: Providing fixed access to branding, search, and user profile links at the top of the UI.
doc.header_scenario_2: Contextual Toolbars: Creating sticky action bars for specific tasks that follow the user during scrolling.
doc.header_sticky_desc: Using sticky or fixed properties allows the header to follow as you scroll.
doc.header_title: Header section for layout top and primary navigation

doc.aspectratio_a11y_desc: No specific ARIA requirements — accessibility is determined by child content.

doc.aspectratio_best_practice_1: Use AspectRatio consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.aspectratio_best_practice_2: Test AspectRatio behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.

doc.aspectratio_long_desc: A component for displaying content such as images or videos responsively while maintaining a specified ratio (e.g., 16:9 or 4:3).
doc.aspectratio_scenario_1: Integrating AspectRatio into workflows for data collection or display.
doc.aspectratio_scenario_2: Using AspectRatio in management views for information organization.
doc.audio_a11y_desc: Uses native audio element enhanced with custom accessible controls. Each button has an aria-label describing its function.
doc.audio_anatomy_content: The primary area where main content or children are rendered.
doc.audio_anatomy_root: The outermost container managing state and layout.
doc.audio_autoplay_desc: Combine autoPlay and muted to start audio automatically without user interaction. Suitable for ambient background music or notification sounds.
doc.audio_basic_desc: Provides basic functions like play, pause, and volume control.
doc.audio_best_practice_1: Use Audio consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.audio_best_practice_2: Test Audio behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.audio_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like Video better suits the use case.
doc.audio_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.audio_choice_self_when: When Audio functionality with standard options is required.
doc.audio_custom_controls_desc: Customize which controls are displayed, such as seek bars and playback speed.
doc.audio_customization_desc: Add features like playback speed adjustment, loop playback, and waveform display.
doc.audio_design_intent: Audio provides a consistent player interface for audio content with controls for play, pause, volume, and seek.
doc.audio_full_featured_desc: A complete player with playlist, waveform visualizer, playback speed, fade-in/out, crossfade, hotkeys, and sleep timer all enabled.
doc.audio_important_notice_desc: Playback without user interaction may be restricted by browser autoplay policies.
doc.audio_keyboard_desc: Tab moves focus through the audio controls. Space toggles play and pause. Arrow keys adjust the seek position or volume. M mutes or unmutes.
doc.audio_long_desc: A component for playing and controlling audio files.
doc.audio_premium_features_mdx_desc: Use the demoDelay prop to display a skeleton UI before the player becomes active — ideal for simulating async data fetching.
doc.audio_scenario_1: Podcast & Language Learning: Play episode lists in sequence with playlist support. Users can adjust playback speed for listening comprehension training.
doc.audio_scenario_2: Chat & Voice Messages: Embed a compact inline audio player within chat messages for one-tap playback of voice notes.
doc.audio_scenario_3: Background BGM & Notifications: Use autoPlay + muted for ambient background music, or trigger short notification sounds after user actions.
doc.audio_styling_desc: Flexibly change the appearance, including border radius and color schemes.
doc.audio_title: Component for playing and controlling audio files.
doc.audio_token_primary: Accent color for the play button, progress bar fill, and active state.
doc.audio_token_primary_light: Background color for active buttons (translucent primary color).
doc.audio_token_radius_full: Pill shape, circular buttons, and slider thumbs.
doc.carousel_a11y_spec: Support navigation with arrow keys and provide appropriate labels (aria-label) for each slide. A means for users to pause during auto-play must be provided.
doc.carousel_accessibility_desc: Supports keyboard navigation (arrow keys). slides carry aria-labels, and autoplay pauses on interaction.
doc.carousel_anatomy_indicators: Dots or numbers showing the current position and total count.
doc.carousel_anatomy_nav_buttons: Arrow buttons to move to previous or next slides.
doc.carousel_anatomy_viewport: The visible area where active slides are displayed.
doc.carousel_aspect_ratio_desc: Combine with the AspectRatio component to maintain consistent slide dimensions.
doc.carousel_autoplay_desc: Enable the autoplay property to automatically rotate slides at a set interval.
doc.carousel_basic_desc: Standard setup for the Carousel component.
doc.carousel_benefit_attention_desc: Dynamic UI movement draws user attention to highlighted content.
doc.carousel_benefit_emphasis_desc: Large-scale banners increase the promotional impact of featured items.
doc.carousel_benefit_space_desc: Packs multiple pieces of content into a single area for proactive user browsing.
doc.carousel_best_practice_1: When using autoplay, ensure enough time for users to read the content and include controls like pausing on hover.
doc.carousel_best_practice_2: Always provide indicators (dots, etc.) for current position and navigation buttons to ensure usability.
doc.carousel_challenge_perf_desc: Loading many high-resolution images can slow down page rendering.
doc.carousel_challenge_perf_sol: Use lazy loading or virtualization to render only visible slides.
doc.carousel_challenge_stress_desc: Confusing controls or intrusive autoplay can frustrate users.
doc.carousel_challenge_stress_sol: Provide clear nav buttons and ensure autoplay pauses on user hover/touch.
doc.carousel_challenge_unseen_desc: Users may overlook content that isn't immediately visible.
doc.carousel_challenge_unseen_sol: Show a 'peek' of the next slide or use clear indicators (dots).
doc.carousel_char_carousel: Displays multiple items simultaneously; primarily user-controlled navigation.
doc.carousel_char_slider: Provides continuous scrolling via drag/swipe; also used for numeric ranges (RangeSlider).
doc.carousel_char_slideshow: Focuses on automatic rotation of large visuals or full-screen images.
doc.carousel_choice_carousel_when: Display multiple items simultaneously and allow users to switch via navigation. Suitable for banners and product showcases.
doc.carousel_choice_matrix_desc: Select the optimal component based on the content type and display method.
doc.carousel_choice_slider_when: Allows continuous scrolling via drag or swipe. Used for image galleries or numeric range selection (RangeSlider).
doc.carousel_choice_slideshow_when: Primary focus is autoplay, switching large visuals or full-screen images in order. Ideal for hero sections.
doc.carousel_design_intent: Carousels are used to efficiently present multiple contents with equal priority in a limited display area. They are highly visually appealing and suitable for content that you want users to browse proactively, such as banners or featured new products.
doc.carousel_differences_intro: While similar, these terms often refer to slightly different use cases.
doc.carousel_features_desc: Key functionalities of the Carousel component.
doc.carousel_guideline_1: Use when you want to effectively showcase multiple contents with equal priority (banners, featured products, etc.) in a limited space.
doc.carousel_guideline_2: Suitable for presenting visually compelling images or cards with a storytelling feel.
doc.carousel_image_example_desc: An example implementation of an image gallery or banner slider.
doc.carousel_long_desc: Details and usage for the Carousel component.
doc.carousel_no_loop_desc: Setting loop={false} stops the carousel at the last slide without returning to the start.
doc.carousel_point_affordance_desc: Intuitively signal the presence of more content to the user.
doc.carousel_point_content_desc: Design for diverse content types like images, text blocks, or mixed media.
doc.carousel_point_responsive_desc: Ensure the layout adapts size and count dynamically based on screen width.
doc.carousel_req_auto_desc: Auto-rotates slides and pauses automatically when user interacts.
doc.carousel_req_indicator_desc: Visually represent current position and total count using dots or numbers.
doc.carousel_req_kbd_desc: Enables arrow key navigation and maintains proper focus management.
doc.carousel_req_loop_desc: Wraps back to the first slide after reaching the end of the list.
doc.carousel_req_nav_desc: Allow slide switching via previous/next buttons or swipe gestures.
doc.carousel_req_touch_desc: Specifically optimized for swipe interactions on mobile devices.
doc.carousel_responsive_desc: Adjust the number of visible slides based on breakpoints (e.g., 1 for mobile, 3 for desktop).
doc.carousel_scenario_gallery: Photo Gallery: Show multiple images one by one in a large display.
doc.carousel_scenario_hero: Hero Banner: Dynamically present campaigns or features on the site's top page.
doc.carousel_scenario_products: Recommended Products: Neatly introduce multiple products of the same category in a compact arrangement.
doc.carousel_specify_slides_desc: Use the slidesToShow property to determine how many slides are visible at once.
doc.carousel_what_is_desc: A Carousel is a UI component that scrolls through multiple items horizontally, helping to save screen space.
doc.icon_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.icon_adv_1: Consistency in design as all icons can be centrally managed
doc.icon_adv_2: Encapsulating file formats and styling makes changes easier
doc.icon_adv_3: Easily reuse the same icons in various components like buttons, list items, and form fields
doc.icon_advantages: Advantages of Making Icon an Independent Component
doc.icon_anatomy_content: The primary area where main content or children are rendered.
doc.icon_anatomy_root: The outermost container managing state and layout.
doc.icon_anim_table_row_example_desc: Spinners during button submission, indicators during search execution, icons during data updates
doc.icon_anim_table_row_features_desc: Can be displayed in sizes (`small` / `medium` / `large`) that blend naturally into existing UI layouts
doc.icon_anim_table_row_usage_desc: To indicate "processing" inline within buttons, input fields, next to text, etc.
doc.icon_anim_vs_loader: Differences Between Icon Animation and Loader Component
doc.icon_anim_vs_loader_desc: Specifying LoadingIcon or SpinnerIcon in the Icon component automatically applies a 360-degree rotation animation (wim-rotate). Separately, the Loader component also has animations indicating loading. These serve different purposes, so use them appropriately.
doc.icon_best_practice_1: Use Icon consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.icon_best_practice_2: Test Icon behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.icon_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like Image better suits the use case.
doc.icon_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.icon_choice_self_when: When Icon functionality with standard options is required.
doc.icon_close_vs_small_desc: Use CloseIcon for standard 'close' actions in dialogs or headers. Use CloseSmallIcon for 'delete' actions in tags, chips, or input fields where visibility in small areas is required.
doc.icon_color_desc: Apply colors using tokens like primary, success, and error, or specify custom color values.
doc.icon_comp_usage_loading: Display while waiting for content to load
doc.icon_design_intent: Icon provides a consistent, reusable pattern for scalable vector icons with consistent sizing and coloring, reducing implementation effort and ensuring design system compliance.
doc.icon_gallery_action_desc: Icons representing user operations and actions.
doc.icon_gallery_comm_desc: Icons related to notifications and messages.
doc.icon_gallery_display_desc: Icons related to display modes and devices.
doc.icon_gallery_file_desc: Icons representing file types and media.
doc.icon_gallery_filled_desc: Mainly used for "active state," "actions to emphasize," and "improving visibility at small sizes."
doc.icon_gallery_nav_desc: Icons indicating page transitions and directions.
doc.icon_gallery_outline_desc: Mainly used for "subtle expression," "navigation," and "input assistance."
doc.icon_gallery_status_desc: Icons for state display and notifications.
doc.icon_gallery_ui_desc: Icons used as general UI elements.
doc.icon_gallery_user_desc: Icons related to user management and login.
doc.icon_loader_anim_desc: Waveform animations where multiple elements (3 bars or dots, etc.) move with a time lag (`bars` / `dots` / `pulse`)
doc.icon_loader_example_desc: Initial page load, fetching list data, transitioning between content
doc.icon_loader_feat_desc: Rich in visual variations and has a strong presence as an independent loading indicator. Supports `sm` / `md` / `lg` / `xl` sizes and multiple colors
doc.icon_loader_usage_desc: To display waiting for content to load on a full page or section basis
doc.icon_long_desc: Icon component used throughout the application
doc.icon_scenario_1: Visual Labels: Adding 'Home' or 'Settings' icons to navigation items for faster recognition.
doc.icon_scenario_2: Status Indicators: Using checkmarks or warning triangles to communicate task outcomes at a glance.
doc.icon_size_desc: Adjust dimensions using numeric values or standard size tokens like xs, sm, md, lg, or xl.

doc.image_best_practice_2: Test Image behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
