doc.image_choice_self_when: When Image functionality with standard options is required.
doc.image_design_intent: Image provides a consistent, reusable pattern for displaying images with responsive sizing, fallback, and styling, reducing implementation effort and ensuring design system compliance.
doc.image_feat_aspect_desc: Adjust image fitting with the fit (object-fit) property.
doc.image_feat_caption_desc: Add descriptive text below the image using the caption property.
doc.image_feat_styling_desc: Easily change appearance with radius, shadow, and border properties.
doc.image_keyboard_desc: This component does not require specific keyboard interaction. Ensure a meaningful alt text is provided for screen reader accessibility.
doc.image_long_desc: The Image component is a wrapper component for displaying images in a refined manner. It features responsive sizing, rounded corners, shadows, borders, and captions.
doc.image_scenario_1: Integrating Image into workflows for data collection or display.
doc.image_scenario_2: Using Image in management views for information organization.
doc.image_variant_caption: Add a caption to display an image description.
doc.image_variant_rounded: Adjust corner radius with the adius property.
doc.image_variant_shadow: Enable shadow for a floating effect.
doc.lightbox_a11y_desc: Proper ARIA roles (dialog) and focus management are implemented. Keyboard navigation allows for closing and navigating through galleries.
doc.lightbox_best_practice_1: Keep captions concise to avoid covering the main content.
doc.lightbox_best_practice_2: Always provide a clear and easily accessible close button.
doc.lightbox_choice_alt_when: Use Image for simple inline display without expansion. Use Dialog for general-purpose modal content that is not primarily media.
doc.lightbox_choice_matrix_desc: Deciding between Lightbox and standard Image or Dialog components.
doc.lightbox_choice_use_when: Use when you want to allow users to view high-resolution versions of images or when presenting a related collection of media items (gallery).
doc.lightbox_desc: A high-quality overlay component for displaying images and media with gallery and zoom functionality.
doc.lightbox_design_intent: Lightbox provides an immersive, premium viewing experience for media content, minimizing surrounding noise and focusing the user's attention on visual assets.
doc.lightbox_keyboard_desc: Supports Escape to close, left/right arrow keys for gallery navigation, and Tab for control focus.
doc.lightbox_scenario_1: Product image gallery in an e-commerce application.
doc.lightbox_scenario_2: Expanding a chart or infographic in a data-rich dashboard.
doc.video_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.video_adv_aspect_desc: Users can choose how the video fits the screen, such as `contain` or `cover`.
doc.video_adv_desc: By using `advancedControls={true}`, you can access various features required for modern video players.
doc.video_adv_pip_desc: Includes a toggle button for PiP mode to float the video in a corner of the screen.
doc.video_adv_playlist_desc: Treat multiple videos as a list, providing a list selection UI and automatic transition when a video ends.
doc.video_adv_q_desc: Select video quality like 1080p, 720p from a dropdown, switching playback seamlessly from the current position.
doc.video_adv_resume_desc: By specifying with `videoId`, it automatically saves the playback position and resumes from where it left off on the next visit.
doc.video_adv_skip_desc: Includes skip buttons on the operation bar, and on mobile, double-tapping the left or right of the screen also performs skip actions.
doc.video_adv_speed_desc: A UI that allows users to freely change the playback speed from 0.25x to 2.0x.
doc.video_anatomy_content: The primary area where main content or children are rendered.
doc.video_anatomy_root: The outermost container managing state and layout.
doc.video_best_practice_1: Use Video consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.video_best_practice_2: Test Video behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.video_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like Audio better suits the use case.
doc.video_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.video_choice_self_when: When Video functionality with standard options is required.
doc.video_desc: A component for embedding and controlling local or remote video content
doc.video_design_intent: Video provides a consistent, reusable pattern for video playback component with controls and advanced features, reducing implementation effort and ensuring design system compliance.
doc.video_feat_1_desc: Toggle playback UI display with the `controls` property.
doc.video_feat_2_desc: Supports background video effects by combining `autoPlay`, `loop`, and `muted`.
doc.video_keyboard_desc: Tab moves focus through the video controls. Space toggles play and pause. Arrow keys adjust seek position or volume. M mutes or unmutes. F toggles fullscreen.
doc.video_long_desc: The `Video` component is for easily embedding video files. It supports autoplay, loop, toggle controls display, rounded corners, shadows, and more.
doc.video_mobile_desc: When using custom controls, the volume slider is hidden in mobile environments with a screen width of 576px or less. The mute/unmute toggle button remains visible.
doc.video_mobile_reason_1_desc: Expanding the volume slider within a narrow control bar would inevitably overlap with other elements like the seek bar and settings icons.
doc.video_mobile_reason_2_desc: Major video platforms like YouTube, Netflix, and Prime Video do not have volume sliders in their mobile apps. On mobile, adjusting volume via device hardware buttons (Volume Up/Down keys) is the standard UX.
doc.video_mobile_reason_3_desc: Even if the volume slider is hidden, the sound can still be toggled on/off with the mute button.
doc.video_premium_features_mdx_desc: Use the demoDelay prop and fadeIn effect to show a skeleton UI before the video loads — ideal for simulating latency or async data fetching.
doc.video_scenario_1_desc: Use autoPlay, loop, and muted together to create a looping background video on landing page hero sections for dynamic visual impact.
doc.video_scenario_2_desc: Use playlist and customControls to showcase multiple product videos in sequence, with quality switching and resume playback.
doc.video_scenario_3_desc: Leverage advancedControls with playback speed, chapter skipping, and PiP mode for an interactive learning video experience.
doc.video_title: A component for embedding and controlling local or remote video content
doc.video_variant_custom: With WIM UI's unique custom control UI applied.
doc.video_variant_full: A full-featured player with all advanced features (playlist, aspect ratio, quality, resume playback, shortcuts, etc.) enabled.
doc.video_variant_rounded: A design with rounded corners and shadows.
doc.watermark_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.watermark_anatomy_content: The primary area where main content or children are rendered.
doc.watermark_anatomy_root: The outermost container managing state and layout.
doc.watermark_best_practice_1: Use Watermark consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.watermark_best_practice_2: Test Watermark behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.watermark_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like Image better suits the use case.
doc.watermark_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.watermark_choice_self_when: When Watermark functionality with standard options is required.
doc.watermark_design_intent: Watermark provides a consistent, reusable pattern for overlaying watermark text or images on content for protection, reducing implementation effort and ensuring design system compliance.
doc.watermark_scenario_1: Integrating Watermark into workflows for data collection or display.
doc.watermark_scenario_2: Using Watermark in management views for information organization.
doc.watermark_var_auto_desc: When using the `image` prop, if you omit either `width` or `height`, the other dimension will be automatically calculated based on the image's native aspect ratio. If both are omitted, it defaults to a width of 125px with a corresponding height.
doc.watermark_var_image_desc: Uses an image such as a logo as a watermark via the `image` prop.

gallery_doc.a11y_spec_3: Checkbox buttons have `aria-label` containing Select/Deselect and the item title.
gallery_doc.best_practice_1: Provide bulk action buttons via `renderActions`; they only appear in the toolbar when items are selected.
gallery_doc.best_practice_2: Shift+click range selection matches file manager UX. Consider adding a brief usage hint near the toolbar.
gallery_doc.best_practice_3: `background-color: var(--wim-color-surface-subtle)` serves as a placeholder during image loading. Combine with Skeleton if needed.
gallery_doc.choice_gallery_when: When you need select, delete, share, or other operations
gallery_doc.choice_lightbox_when: When users need to view images one by one in detail
gallery_doc.choice_masonry_when: When you need a Pinterest-style layout
gallery_doc.choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
gallery_doc.content_guideline_1: Use concise `alt` text describing the subject or content (avoid sequential names like "Image 1").
gallery_doc.content_guideline_2: `title` is intended for short labels (~20 chars); `caption` for supplementary information (~50 chars).
gallery_doc.content_guideline_3: If the gallery may be empty, control the empty state in the parent component.
gallery_doc.design_intent: Gallery is designed not merely as an image grid, but as an interactive media selection component with selection state. Enabling `selectable` switches to multi-select and bulk action mode, covering a "manage and operate" use case distinct from Masonry (layout-first) and Lightbox (browse-first).
gallery_doc.keyboard_desc: Full keyboard navigation: Arrow keys to move focus, Space/Enter to toggle select or trigger `onItemClick`, Ctrl/Cmd+A to select all, Escape to clear selection, Home/End to jump to first/last.
gallery_doc.motion_spec_1: The selection toolbar animates in with `opacity` + `translateY` (`--wim-duration-fast`).
gallery_doc.motion_spec_2: Images apply a `scale(1.04)` zoom transition on hover/selected state (`--wim-duration-base`).
gallery_doc.motion_spec_3: The checkbox overlay fades in from `opacity: 0 → 1` on hover.
gallery_doc.responsive_desc: Uses container queries. Auto-switches to 2 columns at `sm` and 1 column at `xs`. The `columns` prop is reflected based on the component's actual width, not the viewport width.
gallery_doc.scenario_1: Media library: multi-select images for bulk delete, download, or tagging in an admin panel
gallery_doc.scenario_2: File picker: multi-select files for upload or attachment operations
gallery_doc.scenario_3: Photo album: apply bulk like or share actions to selected photos
gallery_doc.subtitle: A grid-layout image gallery component. As a differentiator from Masonry and Lightbox, it features multi-select and bulk action support, making it reusable as a file selection UI.
gallery_doc.variation_selectable_desc: Checkboxes appear and Shift+click enables range selection. A toolbar showing count and bulk actions appears when items are selected.

imagecompare_doc.a11y_spec_1: The handle uses role="slider" with aria-valuenow, aria-valuemin, aria-valuemax, and aria-orientation.
imagecompare_doc.a11y_spec_2: Arrow keys move the divider, and Home/End jump to fully showing one image or the other.
imagecompare_doc.a11y_spec_3: Give each image meaningful alt text so the comparison is understandable without sight.
imagecompare_doc.best_practice_1: Start the divider near the center so both images are visible on load.
imagecompare_doc.best_practice_2: Constrain the component to the images' aspect ratio to avoid distortion.
imagecompare_doc.best_practice_3: Preload both images so dragging never reveals an unloaded half.
imagecompare_doc.choice_cropper_when: Crop, rotate, or frame a single image.
imagecompare_doc.choice_matrix_desc: Use ImageCompare to reveal the difference between two images, and ImageCropper to edit a single one.
imagecompare_doc.choice_self_when: Show the difference between a before and an after image.
imagecompare_doc.content_guideline_1: Use two images of identical dimensions and alignment; any offset reads as a difference.
imagecompare_doc.content_guideline_2: Add before and after labels when the direction of the comparison is not obvious.
imagecompare_doc.design_intent: Comparing two images side by side hides subtle differences. Overlaying them under a single divider keeps both in the same position, so the eye reads the change directly.
imagecompare_doc.i18n_desc: The drag-handle label is overridable through the labels prop; the before and after badges accept any node, so their text comes from your app.
imagecompare_doc.keyboard_arrows: Move the divider (hold Shift for larger steps)
imagecompare_doc.motion_spec_1: The divider follows the pointer directly during a drag, with no easing, so the reveal feels physical.
imagecompare_doc.motion_spec_2: Keyboard adjustments move the divider in discrete steps (2%, or 10% with Shift).
imagecompare_doc.responsive_desc: The component fills the width of its container by default; set an explicit width and height, or wrap it in an aspect-ratio box, to match your images.
imagecompare_doc.scenario_1: A photo editor shows the original beside a retouched version under one slider.
imagecompare_doc.scenario_2: An AI image tool compares the source image with the generated result.
imagecompare_doc.subtitle: ImageCompare overlays two images and reveals them with a draggable divider — a before/after slider for comparing edits, restorations, or AI-generated results against their source.

media.alt_text_desc: Always set alt text for images/videos. Helps accessibility and SEO.
media.autoplay_limit_desc: Minimize autoplay on audio/video as it often surprises users and violates a11y standards.
media.carousel_desc: Best for banner ads, product galleries, or story-format content displays.
media.custom_controls_desc: Add custom controls to match your app's tone & manner.
media.guide_desc: Effectively use images, videos, and audio to convey information visually and aurally.
media.performance_desc: Use `lazy loading` for performance optimization, and `AspectRatio` to prevent layout shifts.
media.skeleton_usage_desc: Show a `Skeleton` during heavy media file loading to indicate progress.

doc.affix_a11y_spec: Ensure that the fixed element does not obscure other focus targets when a keyboard user moves focus. It is important to set offset values appropriately.
doc.affix_anatomy_container: The area monitored for scrolling. Usually the entire document, but a specific element can also be specified.
doc.affix_anatomy_element: The actual following content itself (button, card, list, etc.).
doc.affix_basic_desc: Standard usage of the Affix component.
doc.affix_best_practice_1: Use for pinning vital interface elements like navigation bars, action buttons, or table of contents, ensuring they remain accessible during scrolling.
doc.affix_best_practice_2: Avoid overusing Affix, as having too many fixed elements can clutter the viewport and diminish the space available for main content.
doc.affix_best_practice_3: Ensure that the fixed element does not obscure other important information or overlap with interactive components like headers or footers.
doc.affix_bottom_desc: Use the offsetBottom property to fix content relative to the bottom of the screen.
doc.affix_choice_affix_when: When you want to temporarily fix part of the content and keep it accessible after scrolling.
doc.affix_choice_anchor_when: When you want to provide navigation for jumping to specific sections within a page.
doc.affix_choice_matrix_desc: Select based on the purpose of fixed display and the target scope.
doc.affix_choice_sticky_when: When always fixing a specific layout block (header, sidebar, etc.) to the top or side of the page.
doc.affix_design_intent: Affix is used to keep specific elements in a fixed position on the screen according to scrolling. It ensures that important action buttons, navigation, or tables of contents (TOC) always remain in the user's view, improving convenience.
doc.affix_keyboard_desc: This component is a positioning wrapper with no keyboard interaction of its own. Keyboard navigation applies to the interactive content placed inside it.
doc.affix_long_desc: Details and usage for the Affix component, which fixes an element to a specific position.
doc.affix_scenario_cta: Product Pages: Fixing a "Buy Now" button to the bottom of the screen to enable conversion actions from any position.
doc.affix_scenario_stats: Dashboards: Ensuring that top-level totals or aggregation criteria are always referencable while scrolling to check detailed data.
doc.affix_scenario_toc: Document Sites: Fixing a table of contents to the right side of long articles to facilitate understanding current location and section movement.
doc.affix_target_note: When using Affix for the entire page scroll, the default window target works perfectly. However, if you are using Affix inside a modal or a specific scrollable view, remember to pass the parent container to the target prop.
doc.anchor_a11y_spec: Each link is keyboard-focusable, and scrolling is triggered by the Enter key. Uses `aria-current` to indicate the current location.
doc.anchor_accessibility_desc: Each anchor item is assigned appropriate ARIA attributes for screen reader accessibility.
doc.anchor_anatomy_ink: A visual guide (vertical line or dot) that indicates the currently active item.
doc.anchor_anatomy_item: A link to each section. Includes visual emphasis for the active state.
doc.anchor_basic_desc: Detailed information and usage instructions for the Anchor component.
doc.anchor_best_practice_1: Keep anchor text short and aligned with the heading of the target section for consistency.
doc.anchor_best_practice_2: Position the anchor list in a sidebar or fixed area so users can navigate from any scroll position.
doc.anchor_choice_anchor_when: When you have many sections on a single page and want them to function like a table of contents.
doc.anchor_choice_matrix_desc: Choose the most appropriate navigation method based on the page structure and content type.
doc.anchor_choice_nav_when: When you want to move between different pages across the site rather than staying on a single page.
doc.anchor_choice_tabs_when: When you want to switch between content rather than displaying it all at once.
doc.anchor_design_intent: The Anchor component provides quick access to specific content areas (sections) within a page. It is intended to help users understand their current location on a long page and navigate to their destination without stress.
doc.anchor_keyboard_desc: Tab moves focus through each anchor link in the list. Enter activates the focused link and scrolls to the target section.
doc.anchor_scenario_article: Long-form Article: Placed at the beginning as 'Table of Contents' to allow readers to start from where they want.
doc.anchor_scenario_nav: Product Landing Page: Placed under the hero section to guide users to key sections like 'Features', 'Pricing', and 'FAQ'.
doc.anchor_scenario_toc: Technical Documentation: Jump to specific API descriptions or sections from a table of contents in the sidebar.
doc.anchor_title: A component for smooth scrolling to specific sections
doc.anchor_tracking_desc: Monitors scroll position to automatically activate the corresponding anchor item.
doc.anchor_visibility_desc: The anchor link highlights the active item based on the current scroll position.
doc.backtop_a11y_spec: Assign aria-label="Back to page top" to the button to clearly convey the purpose to screen readers.
doc.backtop_anatomy_button: An interactive element fixed at the bottom right of the screen.
doc.backtop_anatomy_icon: A symbol like an upward arrow that intuitively suggests the action.
doc.backtop_best_practice_1: Use on pages with long content where scrolling is significant (typically 3-4 screens deep).
doc.backtop_best_practice_2: Ensure the button's position does not overlap with other floating elements like chat icons or persistent action buttons.
doc.backtop_best_practice_3: Standard placement is the bottom-right corner, aligning with user expectations for universal design patterns.
doc.backtop_choice_backtop_when: On vertically long pages where a quick return to the top is needed during or after reading.
doc.backtop_choice_matrix_desc: Consider the optimal navigation based on page length and user behavior patterns.
doc.backtop_choice_pagination_when: When physically splitting content to avoid generating long scrolls in the first place.
doc.backtop_choice_sticky_when: When you want to keep navigation like a global menu visible at all times.
doc.backtop_custom_desc: You can customize the content of the BackTop button.
doc.backtop_desc: A button that appears when the page is scrolled and allows the user to quickly return to the top.
doc.backtop_design_intent: The BackTop component is used to allow users viewing long content to return to the top of the page with a single click. It serves as an auxiliary tool to save scrolling time and improve navigation efficiency.
doc.backtop_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the back-to-top button. Enter or Space scrolls the page back to the top.
doc.backtop_scenario_article: Articles & Terms: Vertically long text content like blog posts or terms of use.
doc.backtop_scenario_dashboard: Admin Panels: Pages where many widgets or data tables are arranged, making it difficult to grasp the whole at once.
doc.backtop_scenario_feed: Infinite Scroll: Dynamic pages where items increase as you scroll, such as product lists or timelines.
doc.backtop_target_desc: You can specify a target container for the scroll event.
doc.backtop_usage_1: When the page is very long and needs a quick way to return to the top.
doc.backtop_usage_2: When the user needs to frequently scroll back to the top for navigation or other actions.
doc.breadcrumb_a11y_spec: Assign aria-label="Breadcrumb" to the nav element and structure it with ol/li elements. The current page must have aria-current="page" set.
doc.breadcrumb_anatomy_current: Located at the end of the list, indicating the currently displayed location. Usually has no link.
doc.breadcrumb_anatomy_link: A link to a higher hierarchy level. Clicking it allows the user to return to that level.
doc.breadcrumb_anatomy_separator: A character dividing items. Visually indicates the depth of the hierarchy.
doc.breadcrumb_best_practice_1: Always include the current page as the last item without a link to indicate the user's location.
doc.breadcrumb_best_practice_2: Keep breadcrumb labels concise and matching the titles of the linked pages.
doc.breadcrumb_choice_anchor_when: When jumping between specific sections within a long page.
doc.breadcrumb_choice_breadcrumb_when: When showing the overall hierarchical structure (directory) of the site in order and indicating the path the user has taken.
doc.breadcrumb_choice_matrix_desc: Select the optimal navigation based on the site structure and user movement paths.
doc.breadcrumb_choice_tabs_when: When switching between different views within the same page or the same hierarchy level.
doc.breadcrumb_custom_separator_desc: Customize the separator character using the `separator` property.
doc.breadcrumb_design_intent: Breadcrumbs are used to help users understand their current location within a site's hierarchical structure and to quickly return to higher levels. They are especially helpful in deep sites for maintaining information context.
doc.breadcrumb_keyboard_desc: Tab moves focus through each breadcrumb link. Enter activates the focused link.
doc.breadcrumb_long_desc: A navigation component that helps users understand their current location and easily return to higher-level pages.
doc.breadcrumb_scenario_admin: Admin Panel: Returning to a list from details of setting items (User Settings > Security > Two-Step Verification).
doc.breadcrumb_scenario_ec: E-commerce Site: Tracing category hierarchies (Home > Electronics > TV) to find a target product.
doc.breadcrumb_scenario_files: File Management: Returning to upper levels from deep folder hierarchies (Documents > Project > 2024).
doc.breadcrumb_usage_desc: Pass an array of labels and links to the `items` property.
doc.breadcrumb_with_icons_desc: Icons can be displayed for each item.
doc.infinitescroll_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.infinitescroll_anatomy_content: The list items that are incrementally added to the view as the load trigger is fired.
doc.infinitescroll_anatomy_root: The scrollable viewport or container that monitors the scroll position to trigger data fetching.
doc.infinitescroll_best_practice_1: Use InfiniteScroll consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.infinitescroll_best_practice_2: Test InfiniteScroll behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.infinitescroll_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like Pagination better suits the use case.
doc.infinitescroll_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.infinitescroll_choice_self_when: When InfiniteScroll functionality with standard options is required.
doc.infinitescroll_design_intent: InfiniteScroll automatically loads more content as the user reaches the end of the current list. It is best for discovery-driven feeds where users want to browse without the interruption of page breaks.
doc.infinitescroll_keyboard_desc: Tab moves focus through items in the list. New items are announced to screen readers via aria-live when loaded.
doc.infinitescroll_scenario_1: Social Feeds: Loading more posts as the user scrolls down an activity timeline.
doc.infinitescroll_scenario_2: Image Galleries: Progressively displaying high-resolution photos in a search result grid.
doc.ks_a11y_spec: Uses dl (description list) with dt for action label and dd for key combination. Each key is wrapped in a native kbd element for screen reader support.
doc.ks_best_practice_1: Group shortcuts by category (Navigation, Editing, View) using the 'title' prop for each group.
doc.ks_best_practice_2: Provide platform-specific key sets (⌘ vs Ctrl) detected at render time, rather than listing both.
doc.ks_choice_alt_when: Use Tooltip with a single Kbd for inline hints. Use CommandPalette for an interactive, searchable shortcut launcher.
doc.ks_choice_matrix_desc: Choose based on where and how shortcuts will be presented.
doc.ks_choice_use_when: When presenting multiple shortcuts in a list — help modal, settings page, onboarding overlay.
doc.ks_desc: Display a structured list of keyboard shortcuts
doc.ks_design_intent: Improve discoverability of keyboard shortcuts by presenting them in a structured, scannable format. Using native kbd elements ensures consistent rendering and accessibility.
doc.ks_keyboard_desc: This is a static display component. It does not require keyboard navigation beyond standard Tab focus.
doc.ks_long_desc: KeyboardShortcuts renders labeled key combinations using semantic dl/dt/dd elements and the Kbd component. Ideal for help dialogs, settings panels, and onboarding overlays.
doc.ks_scenario_help: Help dialog: A keyboard shortcuts reference panel opened with '?' or from the Help menu.
doc.ks_scenario_onboarding: Onboarding overlay: Highlight a few key shortcuts to help new users work efficiently from day one.
doc.ks_scenario_settings: Settings page: A dedicated 'Keyboard Shortcuts' section where users can view and optionally customize shortcuts.
doc.menu_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.menu_anatomy_content: The collection of menu items, groups, and submenus that form the navigation hierarchy.
doc.menu_anatomy_root: The container that manages the structural hierarchy and the selection state of the menu items.
doc.menu_best_practice_1: Use Menu consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.menu_best_practice_2: Test Menu behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.menu_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like Dropdown better suits the use case.
doc.menu_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.menu_choice_self_when: When Menu functionality with standard options is required.
doc.menu_design_intent: Menu provides a persistent or toggleable list of options for navigation or complex actions. It is more structural than a simple dropdown, often used in sidebars or specialized action groups.
doc.menu_scenario_1: Context Menus: Providing 'Add to Project' or 'Export' actions when right-clicking an item.
doc.menu_scenario_2: Settings Navigation: Organizing account sub-pages like Security and Billing in a profile sidebar.
doc.navbar_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.navbar_anatomy_content: The flexible area within the bar for placing logos, navigation links, and action buttons.
doc.navbar_anatomy_root: The horizontal bar that persists at the top of the viewport as the primary entry point for navigation.
doc.navbar_basic_usage_desc: Place components like Navbar.Brand and Navbar.Content inside the Navbar component.
doc.navbar_best_practice_1: Use Navbar consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.navbar_best_practice_2: Test Navbar behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.navbar_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like Header better suits the use case.
doc.navbar_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.navbar_choice_self_when: When Navbar functionality with standard options is required.
doc.navbar_content_placement_desc: Flexible layouts are possible by combining multiple Navbar.Content components with the justify property (start, center, end).
doc.navbar_desc_2: It functions as a container for brand logos, navigation links, action buttons, etc.
doc.navbar_design_intent: Navbar is the primary top-level navigation container. It typically houses the brand identity, global search, and key navigation links, providing a fixed and familiar entry point to the site's main areas.
doc.navbar_glass_desc: Use the glass property to apply a background blur effect (frosted glass effect). Highly effective when placed as a fixed header over colourful background images or gradients.
doc.navbar_keyboard_desc: Tab moves focus through navigation links and action buttons. Enter or Space activates focused links.
doc.navbar_layout_desc: Flexible layouts are possible by using multiple `Navbar.Content` components and combining the `justify` property (`start`, `center`, `end`).
doc.navbar_long_desc: Navbar is a responsive navigation header placed at the top of the page.
doc.navbar_scenario_1: App Header: Housing the brand logo and 'Login/Signup' buttons on every page.
doc.navbar_scenario_2: Admin Toolbar: Quick access to search and system help across a management dashboard.
doc.pagination_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.pagination_anatomy_content: The individual interactive page number buttons and 'Next/Previous' status indicators.
doc.pagination_anatomy_root: The control bar that manages the current page state and provides directional navigation.
doc.pagination_best_practice_1: Use Pagination consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.pagination_best_practice_2: Test Pagination behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.pagination_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like InfiniteScroll better suits the use case.
doc.pagination_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.pagination_choice_self_when: When Pagination functionality with standard options is required.
doc.pagination_cons_1_desc: Emphasise the active button so the current page is immediately clear.
doc.pagination_cons_2_desc: Assign appropriate aria-labels to each button (e.g., "Next", "Previous", "Page X").
doc.pagination_cons_3_desc: Use ellipses (...) when there are many pages to avoid displaying all page buttons.
doc.pagination_cons_4_desc: Include "Previous" and "Next" buttons to facilitate sequential page movement. Disable buttons on the first and last pages.
doc.pagination_design_intent: Pagination splits large datasets into discrete pages. It is intended for scenarios where users need to locate specific items across a known volume of data or when page-load performance is a priority.
doc.pagination_feat_all_in_one_desc: All features can be used simultaneously.
doc.pagination_feat_quick_jumper_desc: Enable showQuickJumper to display an input field for direct jumps to a specific page.
doc.pagination_feat_simple_desc: The simple property switches to a compact display format, showing "Current Page / Total Pages" instead of page numbers.
doc.pagination_feat_size_changer_desc: Enable showSizeChanger to allow users to change the number of items displayed per page.
doc.pagination_feat_size_changer_props_1: showSizeChanger - Whether to show the page size selector
doc.pagination_feat_size_changer_props_2: pageSizeOptions - Array of selectable page sizes (default: [10, 20, 50, 100])
doc.pagination_feat_size_changer_props_3: onPageSizeChange - Callback for when the page size is changed
doc.pagination_feat_total_display_desc: Use showTotal to display the total count and the range of items currently being shown.
doc.pagination_keyboard_desc: Tab moves focus through page buttons. Enter or Space activates the focused page button. Arrow keys may navigate between adjacent pages.
doc.pagination_onchange_change_desc: The onChange callback now receives both the page number and the page size:
doc.pagination_onchange_change_desc_2: This allows the same callback to handle changes in page size.
doc.pagination_scenario_1: E-commerce Lists: Navigating through hundreds of products in discrete sets (e.g., 20 per page).
doc.pagination_scenario_2: Search Results: Accessing specific 'pages' of results while maintaining a consistent mental map of progress.
doc.pagination_var_interactive_desc: A live example where you can actually change pages.
doc.pagination_var_many_pages_desc: Ellipses are automatically displayed when there are many pages.
doc.pagination_var_sibling_desc: Adjust the number of pages displayed before and after the current page using the siblingCount property.
doc.sidebar_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.sidebar_anatomy_content: The list of navigation links, icons, and categories that form the secondary navigation layer.
doc.sidebar_anatomy_root: The vertical panel that can be static or collapsible, housing application-level navigation.
doc.sidebar_best_practice_1: Use Sidebar consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.sidebar_best_practice_2: Test Sidebar behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.sidebar_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like Navbar better suits the use case.
doc.sidebar_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.sidebar_choice_self_when: When Sidebar functionality with standard options is required.
doc.sidebar_collapsed_desc: Collapses the sidebar to a minimum size using the `collapsed` property. Only icons will be visible.
doc.sidebar_custom_width_desc: Adjust the expanded width using the `width` property.
doc.sidebar_desc: A collapsible navigation or informational panel on the side of the screen
doc.sidebar_design_intent: Sidebar provides a secondary vertical navigation layer, typically on the left. It is used for deep site hierarchies or application-level tools that need to stay accessible beside main content.
doc.sidebar_keyboard_desc: Tab moves focus through navigation items. Enter activates the focused item. Collapse toggle is also keyboard accessible.
doc.sidebar_long_desc: A sidebar is a navigation or information panel placed on the side of a page.
doc.sidebar_pc_only: Desktop Only: This component is primarily designed for desktop (mouse and keyboard) use. For small-screen devices like smartphones, consider alternatives such as a `TabBar` or drawer menu.
doc.sidebar_scenario_1: SaaS Dashboards: Providing persistent vertical navigation for 'Reports', 'Users', and 'Configuration'.
doc.sidebar_scenario_2: File Explorers: Displaying folder structures alongside a main content viewer.
doc.sidebar_title: A collapsible navigation or informational panel on the side of the screen
doc.sidebar_usage_desc: Place `Sidebar.Header`, `Sidebar.Content`, and `Sidebar.Footer` inside `Sidebar`, and place `Sidebar.Item` inside `Sidebar.Content`.
doc.stepper_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.stepper_anatomy_content: The sequence of step indicators, labels, and optional descriptions that show user progress.
doc.stepper_anatomy_root: The container that tracks the overall process state and manages the current step identification.
doc.stepper_b_cont_desc: For many steps (5+). Perceived as a single flow, reducing the perceived burden.
doc.stepper_b_hor_desc: Suitable for wide screens like desktops, following the natural eye movement from left to right.
doc.stepper_b_linear_desc: Ensures data integrity in processes where the previous step must be completed (e.g., checkout).
doc.stepper_b_non_desc: Suitable for processes editable in any order (settings, profile, etc.).
doc.stepper_b_sep_desc: For fewer steps (3–4). Emphasizes the independence of each stage.
doc.stepper_b_ver_desc: Ideal for mobile environments or many steps. Makes it easier to expand detailed information.
doc.stepper_best_practice_1: Use Stepper consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.stepper_best_practice_2: Test Stepper behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.stepper_c_needs_avoid: Basic operations that are intuitively understood (posting, uploading, etc.)
doc.stepper_c_needs_reco: When complex procedures with a fixed order are required.
doc.stepper_c_steps_avoid: Simple flows with 3 or fewer steps (Input → Confirm → Done)
doc.stepper_c_steps_reco: 4 or more steps (registration, checkout, detailed surveys, etc.)
doc.stepper_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like Tabs better suits the use case.
doc.stepper_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.stepper_choice_self_when: When Stepper functionality with standard options is required.
doc.stepper_design_intent: Stepper guides users through multi-step processes by visualizing their progress. It breaks down complex tasks into manageable units, reducing cognitive load and providing a clear path to completion.
doc.stepper_keyboard_desc: Tab moves focus through step indicators. Enter or Space activates a step when non-linear mode is enabled.
doc.stepper_r_fb_desc: Clearly indicates Completed, Current, and Pending states, giving a sense of steady progress.
doc.stepper_r_fear_desc: Visualizes "how much more until completion," reducing the user’s psychological burden.
doc.stepper_r_task_desc: Divides complex form inputs into manageable units, increasing completion rates while maintaining focus.
doc.stepper_scenario_1: Checkout Flow: Guiding users through Shopping Cart > Shipping > Payment > Confirmation.
doc.stepper_scenario_2: User Onboarding: Breaking down the initial profile setup into three or four manageable steps.
doc.stepper_title: A component that visually displays current progress
doc.stepper_var_err_desc: Indicates that an error occurred in a specific step.
doc.stepper_var_icon_desc: Custom icons can be displayed instead of standard numbers.
doc.stepper_var_inter_desc: An example where steps can actually be advanced or reversed.
doc.stepper_var_lver_desc: Suitable for horizontal layouts where you want to center steps.
doc.stepper_var_ver_desc: Suitable for limited space or when there are many steps.
doc.steps_clickable_desc: By setting `onChange`, users can click each step to change the state.
doc.steps_long_desc: Provides detailed information and usage instructions for the Steps component.
doc.steps_usage_desc: Visually guides a sequence of flows or progress status.
doc.steps_vertical_desc: You can align steps vertically using `direction='vertical'`.
doc.steps_with_icons_desc: Custom icons can be set for each step to enhance visual clarity.
doc.tab_desc: A container to organize related content into switchable view panels
doc.tab_navigation_title: Tabs for navigating within a page or between contexts
doc.tab_title: A container to organize related content into switchable view panels
doc.tabbar_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.tabbar_anatomy_content: The individual tab items, usually consisting of a thumb-friendly icon and a short label.
doc.tabbar_anatomy_root: The bottom-fixed navigation bar that provides access to the primary sections of a mobile application.
doc.tabbar_badge_desc: You can display notification counts or indicators by adding the `badge` property to `TabBar.Item`.
doc.tabbar_basic_usage_desc: Use `TabBar.Item` to define each tab. Set icons and labels, and switch the active tab with the `onClick` event.
doc.tabbar_best_practice_1: Use TabBar consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.tabbar_best_practice_2: Test TabBar behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.tabbar_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like Tabs better suits the use case.
doc.tabbar_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.tabbar_choice_self_when: When TabBar functionality with standard options is required.
doc.tabbar_design_intent: TabBar provides a primary navigation interface for mobile apps, fixed at the bottom of the screen. It allows users to quickly switch between top-level sections with a single tap.
doc.tabbar_icon_only_desc: Labels are optional. If the label is omitted, the icon is centered vertically.
doc.tabbar_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the tab bar. Arrow keys navigate between tab items. Enter or Space activates the focused tab.
doc.tabbar_long_desc_p1: TabBar is a navigation bar fixed at the bottom of the screen for mobile applications. It is used to switch between primary screens.
doc.tabbar_mobile_only: Mobile Only: This component is primarily designed for mobile devices (touch operation, small screens). For desktop environments, consider using `Sidebar` or `Navbar`.
doc.tabbar_scenario_1: Mobile Home Screen: Switching between 'Home', 'Search', 'Notifications', and 'Profile' tabs.
doc.tabbar_scenario_2: Messenger Apps: Navigating between 'Chats', 'Calls', and 'Contacts' on small devices.
doc.tabnavigation_a11y_desc: Follows WAI-ARIA guidelines with proper roles, labels, and keyboard navigation support.
doc.tabnavigation_anatomy_content: The collection of interactive tab links that represent different page routes or views.
doc.tabnavigation_anatomy_root: The navigation wrapper that synchronize the active link state with the current application route.
doc.tabnavigation_basic_desc: The default style is `underline`. This is commonly used for secondary page navigation.
doc.tabnavigation_best_practice_1: Use TabNavigation consistently across your application to maintain a predictable user experience.
doc.tabnavigation_best_practice_2: Test TabNavigation behavior across different screen sizes and input methods to ensure accessibility.
doc.tabnavigation_choice_alt_when: When a simpler alternative like Tabs better suits the use case.
doc.tabnavigation_choice_matrix_desc: Select the most appropriate component based on your requirements.
doc.tabnavigation_choice_self_when: When TabNavigation functionality with standard options is required.
doc.tabnavigation_contained_desc: The Contained style is similar to a SegmentedControl, often used for changing data display formats (e.g., switching the time axis of a chart).
doc.tabnavigation_design_intent: TabNavigation provides a tab-style interface for page-level navigation. Unlike content Tabs, these are typically linked to URL routes, allowing users to move between distinct but related views.
doc.tabnavigation_icons_desc: You can add an icon to each item using the `icon` property.
doc.tabnavigation_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the tab navigation. Arrow keys navigate between tab items. Enter or Space activates the focused tab.
doc.tabnavigation_long_desc: TabNavigation provides a set of links for navigating between different views or contexts. Unlike the `Tabs` component, it is designed primarily for page-level navigation and filtering, typically involving URL transitions.
doc.tabnavigation_pill_desc: The Pill style is suitable for operations that do not drastically change the context, such as filtering a list or toggling a state.
doc.tabnavigation_scenario_1: Account Settings: Toggling between localized route-based views for 'Profile', 'Security', and 'Billing'.
doc.tabnavigation_scenario_2: Entity Dashboards: Switching between 'Overview', 'Activity', and 'Assets' within a specific detail page.
doc.tabs_a11y_1: Supports keyboard arrow-key navigation between tab list items.

doc.hovercard_feat_delay_desc: To prevent accidental triggers, a longer display delay (default 700ms) is typically set compared to Tooltips.
doc.hovercard_feat_interaction_desc: HoverCards are designed for hovering over the displayed content itself or clicking links within it.
doc.hovercard_feat_interaction_rich: Enhanced interactivity including links, media, and nested buttons.
doc.hovercard_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the trigger element. The hover card appears when the trigger receives focus. Escape closes the card. Focus is not trapped inside the card.
doc.hovercard_long_desc: A component to display additional information when hovered.
doc.hovercard_pc_only_desc: This component is designed primarily for PCs as it assumes pointer hover operations. It may not work as intended on touch devices.
doc.hovercard_scenario_1: Integrating HoverCard into workflows for data collection or display.
doc.hovercard_scenario_2: Using HoverCard in management views for information organization.
doc.hovercard_title: A floating card that reveals additional information or previews when hovering over an element.
doc.hovercard_vs_tooltip: HoverCard is similar to Tooltip, but differs in the following ways:
doc.loader_keyboard_desc: This component does not require specific keyboard interaction beyond standard Tab focus.
doc.menu_a11y_1: Keyboard navigation support (focus moves with Tab key)
doc.menu_comp_divider_desc: Inserts a divider between menu items.
doc.menu_comp_itemgroup_desc: Groups menu items with a displayed title.
doc.menu_comp_menu_desc: Root component managing display modes and open/closed states.

doc.menu_comp_submenu_desc: Expandable submenus. Requires a unique itemKey.
doc.menu_keyboard_desc: Arrow keys navigate menu items. Enter or Space activates the focused item. Escape closes submenus or the menu.
doc.menu_long_desc: A versatile menu component for navigation or action lists. Supports submenus, grouping, and multiple display modes.
doc.menu_props_default_open_keys: Array of keys for submenu opened by default

doc.menu_stories_icons_desc: Example of menu items with icons.

doc.popconfirm_a11y_focus: Appropriately set whether to focus on the 'Execute' button (immediate execution priority) or the 'Cancel' button (safety priority) when the popup is displayed.
doc.popconfirm_anatomy_actions: Usually placed as a pair of 'Cancel' and a specific execution verb (e.g., 'Delete', 'Save').
doc.popconfirm_anatomy_description: Supplements with what will happen as a result of the action (e.g., 'This operation cannot be undone') (optional).
doc.popconfirm_anatomy_title: Presents the confirmation item in a concise question (e.g., 'Are you sure you want to delete?').
doc.popconfirm_anatomy_trigger: The element, such as an action button or link, that requires confirmation.
doc.popconfirm_best_practice_1: Use for irreversible or high-impact actions (delete, discard) where simple confirmation is needed.
doc.popconfirm_best_practice_2: Keep the confirmation message short and make the destructive action button clearly distinguishable.
doc.popconfirm_choice_dialog_when: For actions with a very significant impact (e.g., deleting an account, initializing the entire system) that require strong user attention and explicit agreement.
doc.popconfirm_choice_matrix_desc: Choose based on the significance of the action and how much screen context you want to maintain.
doc.popconfirm_choice_popconfirm_when: For minor actions where you want to prevent accidental operation (e.g., deleting a single task, turning off a setting) without leaving the current operation position.
doc.popconfirm_design_intent: Popconfirm provides a lightweight confirmation prompt for actions that have a significant impact if performed unintentionally, such as deletions or state changes. Unlike a Dialog, it appears near the trigger element, allowing for quick decision-making while maintaining context.
doc.popconfirm_ex_desc: An example of setting `Popconfirm` on a delete button to prevent accidental user operations.
doc.popconfirm_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the trigger. When the confirmation popup is open, Tab moves focus between the confirm and cancel buttons. Enter or Space activates the focused button. Escape closes without confirming.
doc.popconfirm_long_desc: Detailed information and usage instructions for the Popconfirm component.
doc.popconfirm_scenario_delete: Individual Data Deletion: Preventing accidental operation when deleting a single item in a list.
doc.popconfirm_scenario_state: Important Status Changes: Confirmation when switching states with an impact range, such as 'making public content private'.
doc.popconfirm_usage_desc: Clicking the button displays a confirmation dialog popup, asking the user to confirm before execution.
doc.popover_a11y_focus: It is recommended to move focus to the first input field when the popover opens and trap focus within the overlay.
doc.popover_anatomy_arrow: Visually points to the element from which the popover originated (optional).
doc.popover_anatomy_content: The floating container that houses forms, lists, or rich text.
doc.popover_anatomy_trigger: The element that invokes the popover upon clicking.
doc.popover_best_practice_1: Use for displaying supplementary information or simple input forms without a full page transition.
doc.popover_best_practice_2: Make the trigger element clear and ensure the popover can be easily dismissed by clicking outside or via an explicit close button.
doc.popover_best_practice_3: Keep the content within the popover focused; consider using a Dialog for more complex layouts or multi-step processes.
doc.popover_choice_dialog_when: For critical decisions or large-scale forms that span multiple steps.
doc.popover_choice_matrix_desc: Select based on the complexity of information and the requirement for task completion.
doc.popover_choice_popover_when: For filter settings related to a specific button or when simple form inputs are required.
doc.popover_choice_tooltip_when: For purely textual descriptions that require no user interaction.
doc.popover_design_intent: Popovers are interactive overlays used to provide detailed information or additional actions related to a specific element while maintaining the current screen context. They are less intrusive than Dialogs and more functional than Tooltips, allowing for complex operations like inputs, selections, or link clicks.
doc.popover_feat_interaction_complex: Supports focus trapping and complex nested components like forms.
doc.popover_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the trigger element. Enter or Space opens the popover. Tab moves focus within it. Escape closes it.
doc.popover_long_desc: Detailed information and usage instructions for the Popover component.
doc.popover_note: Use Popover only when interactive content is required. For simple supplementary explanations, use Tooltip instead.
doc.popover_scenario_filter: Data Filters: A UI for setting detailed filtering conditions in table columns.
doc.popover_scenario_settings: Quick Settings: User preferences when clicking an avatar or status change tools.
doc.popover_use_cases: Filter panels, inline settings, further action menus, etc.
doc.tooltip_a11y_linkage: Uses aria-describedby to link the trigger and tooltip, allowing screen readers to announce the supplementary information.
doc.tooltip_anatomy_content: A small balloon with a dark background providing concise hints or labels.
doc.tooltip_anatomy_trigger: The element (button, icon, etc.) that reveals the tooltip on hover or focus.
doc.tooltip_best_practice_1: Use for displaying supplementary explanations for icons or short text.
doc.tooltip_best_practice_2: Do not include interactive elements like links or buttons within a tooltip. Use a Popover for that instead.
doc.tooltip_best_practice_3: Keep text concise and ensure that important information can be understood even without the tooltip.
doc.tooltip_choice_hovercard_when: For rich previews like user profiles or link metadata that include images or multiple sections.
doc.tooltip_choice_matrix_desc: Select based on the amount of content and the level of interaction required.
doc.tooltip_choice_popover_when: For richer content like links, buttons, or longer descriptions that might need interaction.
doc.tooltip_choice_tooltip_when: For short, plain text descriptions that require no user interaction beyond hovering.
doc.tooltip_delay_desc: You can set the delay time before the tooltip is displayed using the `delay` property (Default: 200ms).
doc.tooltip_design_intent: Tooltips are lightweight text labels that provide extra information about an interactive element (like icon-only buttons) or clarify technical terms. They help prevent user confusion and lower the learning curve without cluttering the UI.
doc.tooltip_keyboard_desc: Tab focuses the trigger element. The tooltip appears on focus. Escape closes it.
doc.tooltip_long_desc: Tooltips are used to provide context and explanations for UI elements, supplementing information without interrupting user actions.
doc.tooltip_scenario_help: Glossary: Defining technical terms or abbreviations in context.
doc.tooltip_scenario_icon: Icon Labels: Providing text labels for icon-only buttons like '+' or '?'.

story.spoiler_review: I have been using this laptop for about three months now, mostly for software development and occasional photo editing. The keyboard has a surprisingly comfortable amount of travel for such a thin chassis, and the trackpad is large and accurate without being in the way while typing. Battery life comfortably covers a full workday of mixed use, including a couple of hours of video calls. The display gets bright enough to work outdoors and the color accuracy is good enough for my photo work after a quick calibration. My only real complaints are the limited port selection, which forces me to carry a small hub, and the fan noise under sustained heavy load. Overall, I would happily recommend it to anyone who values portability over raw performance.
story.spoiler_rich_cons: the port selection is limited, so plan on carrying a hub, and the fans become audible under sustained load such as long compiles or video exports.
story.spoiler_rich_pros: light, quiet, great battery life, and the keyboard is genuinely pleasant to type on for long sessions.

doc.spoiler_a11y_desc: The toggle is a native <button> carrying aria-expanded for the current state and aria-controls pointing to the clamped region, so assistive technologies announce both the action and its target. The clamped text is hidden visually by overflow, not removed from the accessibility tree, so screen readers can always read the full content. Focus stays on the toggle across expand and collapse, keeping the keyboard position stable.
doc.spoiler_best_practice_1: Let the component decide whether the toggle is needed instead of tracking text length yourself — the overflow check already accounts for container width, font size, and translations.
doc.spoiler_best_practice_2: Use the controlled expanded prop when the state must be shared (for example, an "expand all reviews" action or persisting the state per item); otherwise prefer the simpler uncontrolled default.
doc.spoiler_best_practice_3: Avoid nesting interactive elements near the clamp edge: a link that ends up half-hidden on the clamped line is still focusable but not fully readable. Keep links and buttons in the always-visible part or at the start of the text.
doc.spoiler_choice_accordion_when: When hiding and revealing titled sections of arbitrary content, such as FAQ entries or settings groups, where each section has a header.
doc.spoiler_choice_matrix_desc: Choose based on what is being collapsed:
doc.spoiler_choice_scrollarea_when: When the full content must stay reachable inside a fixed-height region and scrolling is preferable to expanding the page.
doc.spoiler_choice_self_when: When a single block of running text (review, comment, product description, bio) should be previewed by line count and expanded in place.
doc.spoiler_default_expanded_desc: defaultExpanded renders the full text initially while keeping the toggle so users can collapse it. Use the expanded prop instead for fully controlled state.
doc.spoiler_design_intent: Long user-generated text competes with everything else on the page: a feed of full-length reviews buries the content around it, while hard truncation hides information with no way back. Clamping to a line count (rather than a pixel height) keeps the cut point aligned with the text grid at any font size, and letting the component decide whether a toggle is needed removes the most common failure of hand-rolled implementations: a dangling "show more" under text that already fits.
doc.spoiler_keyboard_desc: Tab moves focus to the toggle button; Enter and Space activate it, as with any native button. Focus remains on the toggle after expanding or collapsing, so repeated activation toggles the state without re-orienting.
doc.spoiler_labels_desc: showLabel and hideLabel replace the built-in localized labels, for example to name the content ("Read full review").
doc.spoiler_lines_desc: The lines prop sets how many lines remain visible while collapsed. The value is injected as a CSS custom property, so it adapts to any font size or container width.
doc.spoiler_long_desc: Spoiler truncates reviews, comments, and other long text to a configurable number of lines using CSS line-clamp, and reveals the rest through a toggle button wired with aria-expanded and aria-controls. The toggle appears only when the text actually overflows the collapsed height (re-checked via ResizeObserver on resize and content changes), and the clamped text stays in the DOM so screen readers and in-page search still see the full content.
doc.spoiler_prop_defaultExpanded: Initial expanded state for uncontrolled usage.
doc.spoiler_prop_expanded: Controlled expanded state. Use together with onExpandedChange.
doc.spoiler_prop_hideLabel: Label of the toggle while expanded. Defaults to the localized "Show less".
doc.spoiler_prop_lines: Number of text lines shown while collapsed.
doc.spoiler_prop_onExpandedChange: Called with the next state when the toggle is activated.
doc.spoiler_prop_showLabel: Label of the toggle while collapsed. Defaults to the localized "Show more".
doc.spoiler_rich_desc: Children are not limited to plain strings; nested markup such as paragraphs and inline emphasis is clamped as a whole.
doc.spoiler_scenario_1: Clamp each review in a list to 3 lines so users can scan many opinions quickly and expand only the ones worth reading in full.
doc.spoiler_scenario_2: Collapse long comments in discussions and activity feeds; short replies render without a toggle, so the thread stays visually uniform.
doc.spoiler_scenario_3: Show the first lines of a long description above the fold and let interested users expand it without navigating away from the purchase actions.
doc.spoiler_short_desc: When the text fits within the line limit, no toggle is rendered — lists mixing short and long entries stay clean without extra logic.
doc.spoiler_title: Collapse long text to a fixed number of lines with an accessible "show more" toggle.

doc.polymorphism_desc: All components in this category support the `asChild` prop. When enabled, the component will not render its default HTML element but will instead delegate its props and styles to its immediate child element. This is powered by Radix UI's Slot pattern.
doc.polymorphism_note: Ensure that the child element is a single valid React element. Props such as `className`, `style`, and event handlers from the parent will be merged with those on the child.

doc.errorboundary_anatomy_content: The fallback UI components (like a heading and retry button) that are displayed when an error is caught.
doc.errorboundary_anatomy_root: The wrapper that intercepts React lifecycle errors and prevents them from bubbling up to the entire application.
doc.errorboundary_best_practice_1: Wrap large, independent sections of your app (like sidebars or feature modules) so a single failure doesn't crash the entire UI.
doc.errorboundary_best_practice_2: Provide a clear 'Try Again' button that restarts the failed process rather than just showing a static error message.
doc.errorboundary_choice_alt_when: For simple form validation errors where a FieldError or Alert is more appropriate.
doc.errorboundary_choice_matrix_desc: Select based on the size of the component tree you wish to protect.
doc.errorboundary_choice_self_when: For critical UI segments or third-party integrations that might throw unexpected runtime exceptions.
doc.errorboundary_custom_desc: By providing fallback as a function, you can freely customize the error message and reset button.
doc.errorboundary_def_desc: Displays a default error UI with a "Try again" button.
doc.errorboundary_design_intent: ErrorBoundary acts as a safety net for the application. It gracefully handles unexpected runtime crashes in the component tree, providing users with a meaningful 'safe state' and a way to recover (retry) instead of a blank screen or a broken UI.
doc.errorboundary_feat_1_desc: Prevents the entire app from crashing due to the failure of a single component.
doc.errorboundary_feat_2_desc: You can provide your own fallback UI or use the default one.
doc.errorboundary_feat_3_desc: Includes a reset mechanism to retry rendering of child elements.
doc.errorboundary_long_desc: The ErrorBoundary component catches JavaScript errors that occur anywhere in its child component tree, logs those errors, and displays a fallback UI instead of the crashed component tree.
doc.errorboundary_scenario_1: Wrapping dynamic charts or third-party widgets that might throw unexpected errors.
doc.errorboundary_scenario_2: Protecting the main dashboard view from failures in auxiliary data providers.
doc.errorboundary_title: Boundary element to catch runtime errors and show fallback UI
